a_rows_sample.anchor: Do NOT treat the existing verification reports as authoritative. They are intermediate verification artifacts and must themselves be checked against the source corpus.
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames the entire session: chronological/document evolution across ~200 steps in phase_measure_theory is itself evidence that must be reconstructed; existing verification reports are intermediate artifacts, not authoritative, and must themselves be re-checked against the primary source corpus. The objective is not to assess whether the latest document looks plausible but to reconstruct and verify the complete evolution from Step 1 through Step 200 and establish whether every important surviving claim has a traceable, justified path from its source through development into the final theory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: For every step, determine: 1. What was proposed? ... 17. If the idea remains unresolved, is that explicitly represented as unresolved?
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a 17-question per-step extraction protocol: what was proposed, what motivated it, definitions introduced, mathematical claims, assumptions, objections/contradictions identified, whether the idea was modified/rejected/superseded, whether it was experimentally tested and whether that test was actually executed or merely proposed, which later document addresses it, its final surviving form, where that form appears in current documentation, whether an absence is intentional or a documentation gap, whether a transformed appearance is justified, and whether unresolved status is explicitly represented as such.

a_rows_sample.anchor: "this is now the revised definition" does NOT make that definition verified ... "tested" does NOT mean the test was actually executed ... programme/process status is evidence about the development process, not mathematical proof.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates and applies the existing verification rule that programme/process status is evidence about the development process, not mathematical proof: labels such as 'revised', 'frozen', 'PASS', 'ratified', 'tested', or 'canonical' appearing in a document do not by themselves establish that a definition is verified, mathematically proven, experimentally executed, mathematically sound, or that canonicality has been demonstrated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ### A. Senior Mathematician ... ### B. Senior Statistician ... Explicitly distinguish: defined -> mathematically valid -> statistically justified -> empirically validated. ### C. Senior DDD / Enterprise Architect ... Verify whether the mathematical concepts and the DDD concepts actually refer to the same things.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires the verifier to simultaneously hold three role-based checklists: (A) a senior-mathematician checklist covering definitions, domains/codomains, well-formedness, notation, quantifiers, assumptions, propositions, derivations, proof obligations, existence, uniqueness, consistency, satisfiability, identifiability, computability, convergence, invariance, algebraic properties, probability foundations, statistical validity, measurement theory, and information-theoretic claims, never accepting a formula merely because it looks sophisticated; (B) a senior-statistician checklist (probability-space assumptions, estimands, random variables, distributions, likelihoods, priors, posteriors, sampling, independence, uncertainty propagation, missingness, confidence/credible intervals, calibration, selection bias, identifiability, estimation, statistical decision theory, aggregation, empirical validation) with the explicit ladder defined -> mathematically valid -> statistically justified -> empirically validated; and (C) a senior-DDD/enterprise-architect checklist (bounded contexts, ubiquitous language, aggregates, entities, value objects, domain events, commands, policies, services, authority, responsibilities, state ownership, invariants, domain boundaries, terminology, semantic consistency, architecture implications), whose most important obligation is verifying that mathematical concepts and DDD concepts actually refer to the same things and never allowing a mathematical term and a DDD term to silently acquire different meanings.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Create: verification/200-step-longitudinal-verification-plan.md ... Create: verification/200-step-traceability-matrix.md ... | Step | Source | Idea / Question | Definition | Derivation | Assumption | Test | Later Resolution | Final Location | Status |
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires two first deliverables before deep verification begins: a 200-step longitudinal verification plan (all discovered documents, their actual logical/document ordering -- not assumed filename ordering -- step number, subject, dependencies, predecessor/successor documents, whether the document introduces/refines/rejects/tests/consolidates theory, expected verification work, relevant existing artifacts, priority, status) and a step traceability matrix with columns Step/Source/Idea-Question/Definition/Derivation/Assumption/Test/Later-Resolution/Final-Location/Status covering all 200 steps, using the marker NO-SURVIVING-THEORY for a step verified to have no lasting theoretical contribution rather than omitting it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Classify every significant statement as one or more of: DEFINITION, AXIOM / POSTULATE, ASSUMPTION, CONJECTURE, PROPOSITION, THEOREM, DERIVATION, EMPIRICAL CLAIM, OBSERVATION, DESIGN CHOICE, POLICY, ARCHITECTURAL CLAIM, DDD CLAIM, OPEN QUESTION, SPECULATION. Never upgrade a weaker category into a stronger one.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a 14-category epistemic-role classification scheme distinct from the 200-step programme's other vocabularies: DEFINITION, AXIOM/POSTULATE, ASSUMPTION, CONJECTURE, PROPOSITION, THEOREM, DERIVATION, EMPIRICAL CLAIM, OBSERVATION, DESIGN CHOICE, POLICY, ARCHITECTURAL CLAIM, DDD CLAIM, OPEN QUESTION, SPECULATION, with the standing rule that a weaker category may never be silently upgraded into a stronger one.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If it defines: K_{t+1} = delta(K_t,e_t) verify: what exactly is K? what exactly is e? what is the domain of delta? is delta total or partial? can delta actually be evaluated?
a_rows_sample.statement: Illustrates the required mathematical well-formedness check with two worked examples: for a claimed function f: A -> B, verify that A exists, B exists, f is actually defined, every allowed input has an output, and the claimed properties follow; for a claimed transition K_{t+1} = delta(K_t, e_t), verify exactly what K and e are, what delta's domain is, whether delta is total or partial, what its preconditions are, whether delta can actually be evaluated, what information it requires, and what happens when a precondition fails.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Use verdicts: DERIVATION_VALID, DERIVATION_VALID_CONDITIONAL, DERIVATION_INCOMPLETE, DERIVATION_INVALID, DERIVATION_NOT_RECONSTRUCTABLE
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires every important derivation to be independently reconstructed (not merely checked for the presence of intermediate equations) as Premises -> transformation -> intermediate result -> conclusion, testing whether each transformation follows, whether hidden assumptions are introduced, whether variables/dimensions/types are compatible, whether quantifiers are preserved, whether boundary conditions are missing, and whether an invoked theorem's conditions are actually satisfied; assigns one of five verdicts: DERIVATION_VALID, DERIVATION_VALID_CONDITIONAL, DERIVATION_INCOMPLETE, DERIVATION_INVALID, DERIVATION_NOT_RECONSTRUCTABLE.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Required Inputs -> Available Inputs -> Algorithm -> Output ... Use: COMPUTABLE, COMPUTABLE_CONDITIONAL, COMPUTABLE_BUT_INTRACTABLE, NOT_COMPUTABLE_FROM_AVAILABLE_INFORMATION, NOT_YET_ESTABLISHED
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires distinguishing 'algorithmically describable' from 'computable from the available information' for every computational definition, established via the chain Required Inputs -> Available Inputs -> Algorithm -> Output and questions about observability, parameter availability, known distributions, estimable probabilities, identifiable models, finiteness, termination, complexity, reproducibility, and determinism; assigns one of five verdicts: COMPUTABLE, COMPUTABLE_CONDITIONAL, COMPUTABLE_BUT_INTRACTABLE, NOT_COMPUTABLE_FROM_AVAILABLE_INFORMATION, NOT_YET_ESTABLISHED.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Cross-reference the existing A6-statistical-register.md ... Definition -> Assumptions -> Estimand -> Estimator -> Sampling/Observation Model -> Result -> Validation
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires independently re-verifying the existing A6-statistical-register.md against the primary corpus rather than trusting its conclusions, establishing for every statistical formula the chain Definition -> Assumptions -> Estimand -> Estimator -> Sampling/Observation Model -> Result -> Validation, and explicitly flagging nine anti-patterns: probability without probability space, likelihood without likelihood model, posterior without prior, confidence without statistical definition, uncertainty without scale/type, independence without justification, convergence without estimand, estimator without sampling model, and empirical claims without experiment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Create: verification/ubiquitous-language-verification.md ... | Term | First Meaning | Later Meaning | Final Meaning | Same Concept? | DDD Meaning | Mathematical Meaning | Conflict |
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires a complete terminology map for at least 35 named terms (Knowledge, Evidence, Observation, Information, Assertion, Assessment, Claim, Proposition, Truth, Belief, Confidence, Uncertainty, State, Knowledge State, System State, Event, Command, Action, Transition, Process, Policy, Authority, Decision, Determination, Validation, Verification, Provenance, Lineage, Context, Conflict, Unknown, Underdetermined, Refuted, Supported, Accepted, Validated), tracking first/later/final meaning, DDD meaning vs mathematical meaning, and whether these are the same concept; requires identifying synonym collisions, overloaded terms, terminology drift, silent renames, meaning changes, math/DDD semantic mismatches, terms in equations absent from the ubiquitous language, and ubiquitous-language terms with no formal definition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Origin -> Problem -> Discussion -> Proposed Resolution -> Verification -> Final Status ... Use this when an important earlier question/problem disappears from later documents without an explicit resolution. This is a major finding.
a_rows_sample.statement: For every significant historical issue, requires constructing the chain Origin -> Problem -> Discussion -> Proposed Resolution -> Verification -> Final Status and assigning one of eight statuses: RESOLVED, PARTIALLY_RESOLVED, SUPERSEDED, REJECTED, STILL_OPEN, LOST_IN_EVOLUTION, CONTRADICTED, DOCUMENTATION_GAP. Singles out LOST_IN_EVOLUTION -- an important earlier question/problem that disappears from later documents without any explicit resolution -- as a major finding category in its own right.

a_rows_sample.anchor: For every final-theory definition/proposition, trace backwards: Final Theory -> Verification Artifact -> Later Source -> Earlier Source -> Original Motivation ... mark: ORIGIN_NOT_ESTABLISHED ... For every major early theoretical idea trace forward: Original Idea -> Later Development -> Final Treatment
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires both backward traceability (Final Theory -> Verification Artifact -> Later Source -> Earlier Source -> Original Motivation, marking ORIGIN_NOT_ESTABLISHED if a final concept has no historical derivation) and forward traceability (Original Idea -> Later Development -> Final Treatment, classifying each early idea as survived/changed/rejected/replaced/absorbed/remains-unresolved/disappeared), explicitly to prevent the final documentation from presenting a partial history as if it were the complete theory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Distinguish: TEST_PROPOSED from TEST_EXECUTED from EMPIRICALLY_SUPPORTED from MATHEMATICALLY_PROVEN.
a_rows_sample.statement: For every claim of TESTED/PASS/VERIFIED/VALIDATED/COMPUTABLE/CONFORMANT/SOUND, requires finding the underlying evidence by asking whether an actual experiment was executed, what the input/procedure/expected/observed results were, whether it is reproducible, and whether passing the test actually establishes the claimed theorem; requires distinguishing TEST_PROPOSED, TEST_EXECUTED, EMPIRICALLY_SUPPORTED, and MATHEMATICALLY_PROVEN as four non-interchangeable statuses.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ### Existence Does at least one object/state/model satisfying the definition actually exist? ### Satisfiability Can all declared invariants simultaneously hold? ... The existing observation that the invariant system may be vacuous or unsatisfiable is a high-priority verification target.
a_rows_sample.statement: For every formal model, requires explicitly testing (not assuming) existence -- does at least one object/state/model satisfying the definition actually exist -- and satisfiability -- can all declared invariants simultaneously hold; flags a prior existing observation that the invariant system may be vacuous or unsatisfiable as a high-priority verification target.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Identify contradictions between: Step N and Step N+1, early and late definitions, parallel development branches, mathematical theory and DDD model, theory and experiments, theory and final documentation ... Do NOT resolve contradictions by intuition.
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires cross-step (not merely within-file) contradiction analysis across six axes -- adjacent steps, early vs late definitions, parallel development branches, mathematical theory vs DDD model, theory vs experiments, theory vs final documentation -- recording for each contradiction its two sources, exact claims, semantic interpretation, whether one supersedes the other and the evidence for supersession, and final disposition; explicitly forbids resolving contradictions by intuition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The final theory documentation must be constructed independently from the source corpus plus verified results. Do NOT simply edit the existing final document.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandates that after the 200-step verification, the final theory documentation must be independently reconstructed via a fixed 12-stage pipeline (source corpus -> 200-step traceability -> definitions -> dependencies -> derivations -> mathematical verification -> statistical verification -> computational verification -> measurement verification -> DDD/ubiquitous-language verification -> architecture verification -> contradictions/gaps -> verified theory), rather than by editing the existing final document.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Every repair or proposed refinement must be recorded separately as: PROPOSED_REFINEMENT and must never be confused with: SOURCE_CLAIM or VERIFIED_RESULT.
a_rows_sample.statement: Forbids silently repairing an ambiguous definition, silently completing an incomplete derivation, choosing between two conflicting definitions because one looks better, softening a false theorem into a vague statement, or calling an absent experiment tested; every repair or refinement must instead be recorded separately as PROPOSED_REFINEMENT and must never be confused with SOURCE_CLAIM or VERIFIED_RESULT.

a_rows_sample.anchor: At minimum distinguish: PROVEN, MATHEMATICALLY_VALID, MATHEMATICALLY_VALID_CONDITIONAL, DERIVED, DEFINITIONALLY_VALID, EMPIRICALLY_SUPPORTED, TESTED, TEST_PROPOSED, PLAUSIBLE, CONJECTURED, UNVERIFIED, INCOMPLETE, CONTRADICTED, INVALID, UNDEFINED, NOT_IDENTIFIABLE, NOT_COMPUTABLE, OPEN. Never collapse these categories.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes a required 17-item final status vocabulary that must never be collapsed: PROVEN, MATHEMATICALLY_VALID, MATHEMATICALLY_VALID_CONDITIONAL, DERIVED, DEFINITIONALLY_VALID, EMPIRICALLY_SUPPORTED, TESTED, TEST_PROPOSED, PLAUSIBLE, CONJECTURED, UNVERIFIED, INCOMPLETE, CONTRADICTED, INVALID, UNDEFINED, NOT_IDENTIFIABLE, NOT_COMPUTABLE, OPEN.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Follow this order: Phase 1 -- Corpus inventory ... Phase 12 -- Gap and uncertainty report
a_rows_sample.statement: Prescribes a 12-phase research order: (1) corpus inventory, (2) historical reconstruction, (3) step-by-step verification of Steps 1-200, (4) definition reconstruction, (5) derivation reconstruction, (6) mathematical verification, (7) measurement/statistical verification, (8) computational verification, (9) DDD/ubiquitous-language verification, (10) architecture consistency, (11) final theory reconstruction, (12) gap and uncertainty report; and mandates working in eight controlled 25-step supervisory batches, after each of which results must be persisted, traceability updated, new contradictions and unresolved predecessor questions identified, implications for the final theory drawn, the dependency graph updated, and work stopped for a checkpoint if a load-bearing contradiction is revealed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Established (TV-F-007/008): V!=empty under interpretation (M0/M1) - system is a liveness-free schema over >=12 uninterpreted predicates - fresh IDs mandatory (5x I_1, 6 IDs for Unknown!=False, swapped registries).
b_rows_sample.statement: Records three prior established findings (TV-F-007/008) that this plan builds on: the state space is non-empty under interpretation (models M0/M1); the system is a liveness-free schema over at least 12 uninterpreted predicates; and fresh IDs are mandatory because of naming collisions found in the source corpus -- five separate uses of the label 'I_1', six different IDs all covering the 'Unknown != False' family, and at least one case of swapped registries.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 1 -- Fresh-ID consolidated catalogue ... Mint KI-nnn for every distinct invariant statement across the >=10 registries (~130 statements) ... Dedup rule: semantic near-duplicates grouped, never merged -- the group is the object.
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 1 mints a fresh KI-nnn identifier for every distinct invariant statement found across at least 10 separate corpus registries (roughly 130 statements total), recording per row: the KI-ID, the canonical verbatim-anchored statement, all source IDs and locations, its semantic-duplicate group, its layer (assigned in Step 2), its modal strength (MUST/SHOULD as found, both recorded where an invariant carries dual strength, e.g. K5), and its status from prior A5/TV-F verdicts where already touched. States a deduplication rule: semantic near-duplicates are grouped, never merged into one -- the group itself, not a single representative, is treated as the object of record.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 2 -- Layer classification (per 1600 section13's demand to distinguish) Each KI classified: DEFINITIONAL ... NORMATIVE-EPISTEMIC ... NORMATIVE-GOVERNANCE (K1-K7, authority family) ... METHODOLOGICAL (I-8, no-assertion-without-evidence) ... ARCHITECTURAL/OPERATIONAL ... EMPIRICAL
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 2 classifies every consolidated invariant (KI) into one of six layers per an earlier document's ('1600 section 13') demand: DEFINITIONAL (holds by construction of the event-log/state-machinery, e.g. several of the '197' conservation laws), NORMATIVE-EPISTEMIC (the Unknown != False family), NORMATIVE-GOVERNANCE (the K1-K7 authority family), METHODOLOGICAL (e.g. I-8, no-assertion-without-evidence), ARCHITECTURAL/OPERATIONAL (test-assertion shaped), and EMPIRICAL (calibration-type); explicitly reuses a corpus-native four-constraint-kind scheme (cited as '162') as the template for this classification rather than inventing a new one.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 3 -- Per-layer satisfiability at intended semantics ... exhibit a model or a minimal unsatisfiable subset ... Expected hard spots: governance layer under multi-authority (needs the precedence device); epistemic layer's Conflicted-exit (needs adjudication signature)
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 3 requires, for each layer, once its predicates receive interpretations (from prior V2/V3 outcomes plus governance devices), exhibiting either a satisfying model or a minimal unsatisfiable subset, extending the baseline models M0/M1 per layer; names three expected hard spots in advance: the governance layer under multi-authority conditions (needing a precedence device), the epistemic layer's Conflicted-exit case (needing an adjudication signature), and anything consuming the terms 'authoritative'/'material'/'governed' (needing formal definitions for these terms).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 4 -- Independence/redundancy analysis ... Output: a minimal generating subset per layer -- PROPOSED, never a deletion of the others.
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 4 analyzes, within each layer, which KIs are logically implied by others (candidate example: several '048' items follow from the event-log construction plus provenance conservation) versus which are independent axioms; the output is a minimal generating subset per layer, explicitly framed as PROPOSED and never as a deletion or removal of the non-generating invariants.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 5 -- The liveness question (governance) The system's liveness-freeness is a theorem (TV-F-007.3). Whether KnowledgeOS should carry liveness obligations ... is a design decision -- formulate the question precisely, decide nothing.
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 5 explicitly separates a proven mathematical fact (the system's liveness-freeness is a theorem, TV-F-007.3) from a distinct, undecided governance/design question -- whether KnowledgeOS should carry liveness obligations (citing '048 section 48.9's example and K7's capability being upgraded to an occurrence obligation as illustrative material) -- with the instruction to formulate the question precisely but decide nothing under this plan.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PASS criteria: Step 1-2 complete when every statement has exactly one KI row and one layer; Step 3 per-layer PASS = explicit model; FAIL = minimal unsatisfiable subset exhibited; OPEN = named missing interpretation. Circularity check ... runs alongside Step 3.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines PASS criteria: Steps 1-2 are complete only when every invariant statement has exactly one KI row and exactly one layer assignment; per layer in Step 3, PASS requires an explicit model, FAIL requires a minimal unsatisfiable subset to be exhibited, and OPEN requires naming the specific missing interpretation. Requires a circularity check (referencing two previously-flagged circularity findings, a goal/policy recursion and an identity bootstrap circularity) to run alongside Step 3.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Prerequisites (why this stage waits) UL canonical meanings for the COLLIDING terms (plan 01) - fresh-ID invariant catalogue with layers (plan 08 steps 1-2, because the corpus's own boundary-derivation method [162] derives contexts from invariants) - the residence dispositions
b_rows_sample.statement: States why the DDD verification stage must wait on three prerequisites: canonical ubiquitous-language meanings for the terms flagged as COLLIDING in plan 01 (especially Assessment/Assertion); the fresh-ID consolidated invariant catalogue with layer assignments from plan 08 steps 1-2, explicitly because the corpus's own boundary-derivation method (step 162) derives bounded contexts FROM invariants, not the reverse; and prior residence dispositions (evidence and Zero findings), since those are themselves aggregate-boundary decisions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: L. Next attack KI-catalogue consolidation (mechanical, high-value, ungated) + derivation chain D-1 (the 8-primitive constructibility claims -- the corpus's central "everything follows" claim, never yet tested). Both executable without any governance input.
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommends the single next attack as two ungated, governance-independent tasks: the mechanical KI-catalogue consolidation (plan 08, high value) and derivation chain D-1, testing the 8-primitive constructibility claims -- described as the corpus's central 'everything follows' claim, never yet tested.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Perform the mandatory joint-satisfiability test. Given all surviving invariants: Does there exist at least one state satisfying all of them simultaneously? If not proven, mark: JOINT_SATISFIABILITY = UNVERIFIED. If a counterexample demonstrates inconsistency: JOINT_SATISFIABILITY = REFUTED.
b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a joint-satisfiability test over all surviving invariants -- does at least one state satisfy them all simultaneously -- marked JOINT_SATISFIABILITY = UNVERIFIED absent a proof, or REFUTED if a counterexample demonstrates inconsistency; explicitly forbids accepting an invariant collection merely because each invariant individually looks reasonable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Does there exist at least one valid KnowledgeOS state satisfying all mandatory invariants simultaneously? If this has not been established, mark the theory accordingly.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the mandatory joint-satisfiability requirement over all mandatory invariants (does at least one valid KnowledgeOS state satisfy them all simultaneously), explicitly forbidding verifying each invariant only independently, and requiring the theory to be marked accordingly if joint satisfiability has not been established.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KI-ID ... satisfiability status ... whether it is definitional, epistemic, governance, architectural or empirical ... Does the intended interpretation of the consolidated invariant system have at least one model? ... Do not confuse: there exists a model under arbitrary interpretations with: the intended KnowledgeOS semantics are jointly satisfiable
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires a fresh KI-ID invariant catalogue (source, exact statement, semantic meaning, duplicate group, layer, MUST/SHOULD status, assumptions, logical dependencies, satisfiability status, definitional/epistemic/governance/architectural/empirical classification) and draws a sharp distinction between a model existing under arbitrary interpretations versus the intended KnowledgeOS semantics being jointly satisfiable -- these are stated to be different claims not to be confused.

b_rows_sample.anchor: V = { x | I1(x) ∧ I2(x) ∧ ... ∧ In(x) } ... Determine whether: V is non-empty; V is empty; V is unknown; V is non-empty only under additional assumptions. If the invariant system is unsatisfiable, the theory cannot simply be declared valid
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes joint invariant satisfiability as V={x | I1(x)^...^In(x)} and requires explicitly determining whether V is non-empty, empty, unknown, or non-empty only under stated additional assumptions, with an explicit rule that an unsatisfiable invariant system blocks declaring the theory valid.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Joint satisfiability (§11) NOT YET INVESTIGATED ... The question is not open — it is currently ill-posed, and saying so is the honest result
b_rows_sample.statement: States that joint invariant satisfiability (V={x | I1(x)^...^In(x)}) cannot yet be evaluated given only 1 of roughly 500 invariants is decidable, and explicitly reclassifies this from 'open question' to 'currently ill-posed', framing that reclassification itself as the honest result rather than a gap to be filled.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Answer: NO for the formalizable core. The invariant system is INCONSISTENT ... FIVE INDEPENDENT minimal conflicting subsets
b_rows_sample.statement: Answers the standing joint-satisfiability question (can all surviving invariants hold simultaneously) for the formalizable core: NO, the system is inconsistent, decomposing into five independent minimal conflicting subsets, four of which conflict within a single step or between two steps step-100 declares closed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A naive reading concludes the satisfiability question is ill-posed. That reading is too weak, and I reject it ... yields a sound lower bound on inconsistency
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the weaker 'ill-posed' framing of joint satisfiability (given only 1 of ~500 invariants is a decidable predicate), arguing satisfiability requires only that commitments be formalizable enough to admit a truth assignment, not that every invariant be individually decidable; the resulting propositional-abstraction method yields a sound lower bound on inconsistency, since it cannot find conflicts hidden inside undefined predicates.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 14 atoms, each with a verbatim source ... atoms: 14 models enumerated: 16,384 SATISFYING MODELS: 0
b_rows_sample.statement: Constructs a 14-atom propositional abstraction of the corpus's own boxed commitments (each atom traced to a verbatim source, e.g. UnknownRepresentable from step-089's I_VerificationState, DiscardPermitted/ProofOfNonNecessity/FutureQuestionsKnowable from steps 088/098, OneOwnerPerConcept and FindingLifecycleSplit from step 138, EpistemicPartialOrder/EpistemicTotalChain from step 192, EntropyNonIncreasing/EntropyGrows from step 188, SemanticElevationGoverned/SemanticDemotionGoverned, FreezeDeletesTerms from 201-A) and exhaustively enumerates all 2^14=16,384 possible truth assignments, finding exactly zero satisfying models.

b_rows_sample.anchor: MCS-1 Unknown semantics ... The corpus's own runtime verification surface cannot express the third value its own invariant mandates ... Three defects in one artifact
b_rows_sample.statement: MCS-1: step-089's I_VerificationState mandates a runtime that supports True/False/Unknown, but step-099's actual runtime dashboard value domain is verified first-hand to be {PASS,DEGRADED,FAIL} with no Unknown -- compounded by the same dashboard also displaying I_Security (a conjunction over four non-existent conjuncts) and a never-minted I_ArchitectureConformance, three defects in one artifact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: MCS-2 Retention ... A1 ∧ A2 ⊢ ¬∃X : Discard(X), contradicting A3 ... A1 and A2 are two sections apart in the same file
b_rows_sample.statement: MCS-2: formalizes the retention conflict as three axioms (A1: discard requires provable universal non-necessity across all protected future questions; A2: future questions are generally unknowable; A3: some discarding is required or storage grows unboundedly) and derives that A1 and A2 together entail no discarding is ever provable, directly contradicting A3 -- with A1 and A2 stated two sections apart in the same file (step 088) and never reconciled, while step-100 declares both step-088 and step-098 closed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: MCS-3 Aggregate ownership ... The Finding state machine therefore has three owners under a rule demanding exactly one — within one file
b_rows_sample.statement: MCS-3: step-138's own §138.49 boxes 'exactly one authoritative owner' per concept while its own §138.26 distributes the Finding lifecycle across three bounded contexts, giving Finding three owners under a rule demanding exactly one within the same file; cross-references step-149's ownership matrix violating the same rule from a different direction (an 'Action | Action/Agent' disjunctive owner).

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 2 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: We do not derive Aggregates from nouns. We derive them from invariants, transactional atomicity, identity, lifecycle and concurrency.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the governing methodological rule for the whole step: aggregates must be derived from invariants/atomicity/identity/lifecycle/concurrency, deliberately resisting the temptation to create one aggregate per existing noun (EvidenceAggregate, AssessmentAggregate, DecisionAggregate, ...).

a_rows_sample.anchor:
Agg=(I,O,B) ... B defines what must remain consistent atomically. Therefore: Aggregate
eq DatabaseTable. And: Aggregate
eq Entity. And: Aggregate
eq BoundedContext.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines an Aggregate as (Identity, OwnedState, InvariantBoundary), with the boundary B defining what must remain atomically consistent, explicitly distinct from a database table, an entity, or a bounded context.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Owner(I_i)=Agg_j. If no aggregate can enforce the invariant locally, then one of three things is true: 1. the invariant is actually cross-context; 2. the model is missing a concept; 3. the proposed aggregate boundary is wrong.
a_rows_sample.statement: First derivation criterion (invariant ownership): for each invariant, ask which object has enough information and authority to guarantee it; if none can, the invariant is cross-context, the model is missing a concept, or the proposed boundary is wrong -- far more rigorous than grouping objects by similarity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Atomicity must be required by an invariant. ... 'usually change together' is insufficient.
a_rows_sample.statement: Second criterion (atomicity): two objects belong in one aggregate only if an actual invariant requires their atomic co-change, not merely that they usually change together.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Lifecycle(B)\subseteq Lifecycle(A). This is evidence for containment. But lifecycle dependency alone is not enough.
a_rows_sample.statement: Third criterion (lifecycle): if B cannot meaningfully exist without A, that is evidence for containment, but lifecycle dependency alone is insufficient if B has its own independent consistency boundary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ConcurrencyCost(A,B). An aggregate should be as small as possible while still protecting its invariants. Minimize aggregate size subject to Invariant preservation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Fourth criterion (concurrency): frequently-independently-modified objects placed in one aggregate create contention costs; states the optimization principle of minimizing aggregate size subject to invariant preservation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Lifecycle(Proposition) \not\subseteq Lifecycle(Assessment). ... PropositionAggregate with assessments represented as separate knowledge objects or references.
a_rows_sample.statement: Walks Proposition vs Assessment through the criteria: a proposition can exist before and receive multiple assessments over time, so its lifecycle is not contained by any one assessment's -- concluding PropositionAggregate is a candidate with assessments as separate objects/references, possibly owning only a CurrentAssessmentReference if a 'one active assessment per model/version' invariant exists.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence\neq Observation. ... EvidenceAggregate with: EvidenceSource and provenance information internally managed where the invariant requires it. ... I_E: Verified\Rightarrow Provenance\land Integrity.
a_rows_sample.statement: Walks Evidence vs Observation: evidence can exist independently and originate from non-observation sources (documents, system records, external datasets, calculations), arguing against a universal ObservationWithEvidence aggregate; instead an EvidenceAggregate can own the verification invariant (Verified requires Provenance and Integrity).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Reference is often preferable to containment.
a_rows_sample.statement: States that Observation need not be owned by the Evidence Aggregate as a child entity, since Observation can have its own independent lifecycle (Captured->Corrected->Superseded) -- reference is often preferable to containment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I_A: Assessment \rightarrow (P,E,M,U,L). ... AssessmentAggregate may contain: EvidenceRef_1,...,EvidenceRef_n. This preserves aggregate independence.
a_rows_sample.statement: Assessment is a strong aggregate candidate owning a TraceableBasis invariant (Assessment must reference Proposition, Evidence, Model, Uncertainty, Lineage), but must hold Evidence references, not embedded Evidence ownership, preserving aggregate independence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: M_v\neq M_{v+1}. Thus: VersionedModelIdentity is required for reproducibility. This is especially important for AI models.
a_rows_sample.statement: Model deserves its own independent aggregate/registry (ModelRegistry/ModelContext) rather than being embedded in Assessment, since multiple assessments can reference the same model and a referenced model version must never be silently mutated -- VersionedModelIdentity is required for reproducibility, especially for AI models.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Uncertainty is a value/semantic component of Assessment, not automatically an Aggregate.
a_rows_sample.statement: Concludes Uncertainty should not automatically become its own aggregate; at present it is a value/semantic component of Assessment, unless it independently develops its own lifecycle, calibration, or governance justifying separation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Policy should have identity/versioning independent from: Decision. A Decision should reference: PolicyVersion. It should not copy the whole mutable policy. ... ActionValid\Rightarrow ApplicablePolicyFound.
a_rows_sample.statement: Policy is an independent aggregate candidate (its own versioned lifecycle, multiple decisions can depend on one version); a governed action's validity requires an applicable policy version found at that time, not a copied mutable policy.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Authority_t\neq Authority_{t+1}. Therefore the decision record must preserve the authority basis at decision time. ... PresentAuthority\neq HistoricalAuthority.
a_rows_sample.statement: Authority has its own independent lifecycle (an actor's authority can change over time), so a decision must preserve the authority basis at the time it was made -- PresentAuthority != HistoricalAuthority, a conditional aggregate candidate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I_D: FinalDecision \Rightarrow ValidDecisionBasis. ... Decision references Assessment; it does not own Assessment.
a_rows_sample.statement: Decision is a strong aggregate candidate with invariant FinalDecision requires ValidDecisionBasis; explicitly references (never owns) Assessment, or Decision would become responsible for epistemic lifecycle, violating bounded responsibility.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Action \xrightarrow{derivedFrom} DecisionRef. This preserves the distinction: Decision\neq Action. ... Action \rightarrow OutcomeObservation. ExecutionState\neq Outcome.
a_rows_sample.statement: Action is a strong aggregate candidate (identity, target, authorization, status, execution info) that references rather than owns its originating Decision; Outcome is a low-confidence aggregate candidate since it may be produced by an external system, reinforcing ExecutionState != Outcome.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Vocabulary -> Relations -> State -> Transitions -> InvariantPreservation. The next step should therefore be not another philosophical layer. It is time to derive the actual DDD structures.
b_rows_sample.statement: Names the architecture's maturity progression (Concepts->Relations->StateSpaces->Transitions->InvariantPreservation) as complete, and declares readiness to move from theory-building to deriving actual DDD structures.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Which objects must change atomically, and therefore belong to the same Aggregate? ... Atomicity+InvariantOwnership+TransactionBoundary+Identity+Lifecycle+Concurrency. ... Vocabulary -> Relations -> State -> Transitions -> Invariants -> Aggregates -> BoundedContexts.
b_rows_sample.statement: Opens Step 205: derive candidate Aggregate boundaries using Atomicity, InvariantOwnership, TransactionBoundary, Identity, Lifecycle, and Concurrency, testing each candidate against 'why does this object own this invariant?' and 'what must be immediately vs eventually consistent?'; explicitly names and mandates preserving the full seven-stage derivation order (Vocabulary->Relations->State->Transitions->Invariants->Aggregates->BoundedContexts) in the book itself, to demonstrate how the architecture was actually derived rather than presenting a finished design as if it had been upfront.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DDD-2 | Aggregate adjudication (189's five vs 205's lists): apply 203 section34's own criterion (Same Aggregate iff shared transactional invariant requires atomicity) to the KI catalogue per candidate
b_rows_sample.statement: DDD-2 adjudicates between step 189's five candidate aggregates and step 205's aggregate lists by applying step 203 section 34's own same-aggregate criterion (Same Aggregate if and only if a shared transactional invariant requires atomicity) to the KI catalogue per candidate; produces a per-candidate verdict showing the criterion's evaluation explicitly, resolving Lineage and Determination disagreements by the criterion or marking them UNRESOLVED.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence tiers (hierarchy, strongest first) ... Reality classes
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines an 8-tier evidence hierarchy (T1 implementation code .. T8 external corroborative, e.g. perpleixity_research_on_roles.md) and a reality-class vocabulary (A IMPLEMENTED, B IMPLICIT, C PARTIAL, D WRONG-BOUNDARY, E MISSING, F CONTRADICTED, G DOCUMENTED/HYPOTHESIS, UNKNOWN). Binding rule: documentation of desired behaviour is never evidence of implementation; no B/C/G finding is promoted to A; no gap is filled to make the reconstruction coherent; contradictions are surfaced, never silently reconciled.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence classes (AIP's own) ... Quarantined -- never current-architecture evidence
a_rows_sample.statement: Class A GOVERNED (committed/registered/decided: registry.yaml, ADRs, decisions, grants); Class B UNGOVERNED (untracked diagrams, the 925-line role document, brainstorming, status authoritative:false); Class C EXTERNAL/CORROBORATIVE (never authority, e.g. perpleixity_research_on_roles.md). The proposed KnowledgeOS architecture Review Set, kernel-extraction analyses, and the Digitalization Robot are quarantined -- used in this reconstruction only as 'Not established by current AIP evidence,' never as current architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: T1 Compute does not imply State Change … T6 Lord proposes; Sārathi guides; the Knower/Agent commits … T7 K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,e_t) … T8 K_t=Replay(K_0,H_t)
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists eight 'foundational theorems' (T1-T8) as established fact, including T7 (a specific single-step transition-function form K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,e_t)) and T8 (a fold-style replay K_t=Replay(K_0,H_t)) — presented without proof, executable test, or governance act, in direct tension with the contemporaneous rigorous commission's finding that delta 'has no body' and 0 postconditions exist anywhere in the governed surface.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'T1..T8'

a_rows_sample.anchor: **Replay is a decisive differentiator**: `(𝒜,ℛ)` alone cannot express replay; adding history `H` restores it.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies replay as a decisive differentiator between the projected epistemic sub-state (A,R) and the full ratified K_t: (A,R) alone cannot express replay, but adding the append-only history H restores replay capability — offered as evidence for why (A,R) is genuinely lossy relative to K_t, not merely differently organized.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | **K-6 `𝒦=(K,H)`** | + replay invariants | + `Replay` (class-4) | `fold(δ,H,K_0)` | ✅ **restores replay** — the minimal repair to K-2 |
a_rows_sample.statement: K-6 (K=(K,H), state plus append-only history) adds replay invariants and a Replay operation (class-4), with state reconstructed as fold(delta,H,K_0); verdict: restores replay and is identified as the minimal repair needed to fix K-2's replay deficiency.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Transition \neq Overwrite ... K_{t+1} = Transition(K_t, Operation, Parameters) ... Observation, Semantic, Epistemic, Update, Comparison, Resolution, Navigation, History
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a state transition as a rule-governed operation transforming K_t into K_{t+1} (never overwriting), catalogs eight operation categories each with explicit preconditions/effects/postconditions (Observe, Detect, Parse, DiscoverDimension, DeriveProposition, Assert, Evaluate, ReEvaluate, AddEvidence, ChangeState, ReviseValue, Compare, DetectConflict, DetectGap, ResolveConflict, ResolveGap, Reframe, Prioritize, Query, Present, Preserve, Recall, Rollback).

b_rows_sample.anchor: There are actually three different concepts: Operation... Event... Transition. Operation -> Event -> StateTransition, not Operation=Transition. K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,e_t)
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the model by separating Operation (a requested transformation command), Event (a record of what actually happened), and Transition (the function mapping state+event to new state): Command -> domain validation -> Event -> delta(K_t,e_t)=K_{t+1}, an event-sourcing/DDD pattern rather than treating operations as direct mutations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Compute != Change ... Decision != Commitment ... Only committed domain events change the Knowledge State ... Zero(K_t,I_t) -> Z_t, not K_{t+1} ... Zero should not automatically mutate K.
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes Compute != Change and Decision != Commitment: analytical operations (Query, Compare, Evaluate, DetectConflict, DetectGap) must be pure computations returning results, never automatically mutating K_t; only an explicitly committed event changes the Knowledge State, reaffirming that Zero findings and Lord candidates are computed outputs, not knowledge mutations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H_t = {K_0,K_1,...,K_t} ... indexing problem... A cleaner formulation is H_{t+1}=H_t || e_t ... K_t=Replay(K_0,H_t)
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects History from a bag of full previous Knowledge-State snapshots {K_0,...,K_t} to an append-only event sequence H_t=(e_0,...,e_{t-1}), with the current state reconstructed via K_t=Replay(K_0,H_t) rather than stored redundantly -- providing auditability, reproducibility, and deterministic reconstruction as first-class properties.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rollback should NOT mean 'set current state back'... In an immutable history model you should not rewrite history... Rollback(K3,K1) creates a new transition K3->K4 where K4 approx K1 but K4 != K1 because they have different provenance/history. Rollback != TimeTravel.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Rollback's semantics: since history is immutable and append-only, rolling back cannot delete or revert history; instead it produces a new state K4 structurally resembling an earlier state K1 but distinct from it by provenance -- Rollback != TimeTravel, Rollback = NewStateDerivedFromHistoricalState.

b_rows_sample.anchor: T1: Compute does not imply State Change. T2: Only committed events change K. T3: History is append-only. T4: Rollback creates a new state. T5: Zero evaluates Knowledge; Zero does not constitute Knowledge. T6: Lord proposes; Sarathi guides; the Knower/Agent commits. T7: K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,e_t). T8: K_t=Replay(K_0,H_t).
b_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates the entire state-transition correction into eight named theorems (T1-T8) as the bridge from the Questions 1-14 ontology to a KnowledgeOS epistemic state machine, changing the operating vocabulary from 'operations transform knowledge state' to 'committed epistemic events transform knowledge state; operations compute, propose, or request those events'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q18 should distinguish discovery from revision... Discovery -> Proposal -> Evaluation -> Authorization -> Revision ... Ideal State itself should have history: H^I_t, I_t=Replay(I_0,H^I_t,Pi_I). Ideal-State revision should itself be an event: I_{t+1}=delta_I(I_t,r_t).
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes symmetry between Knowledge-State and Ideal-State evolution: Ideal-State revisions must go through the same Discovery->Proposal->Evaluation->Authorization->Revision sequence as knowledge events, be recorded as an authorized IdealStateRevisionAuthorized event r_t, accumulate in an append-only Ideal-State history H^I_t, and be reconstructible via I_t=Replay(I_0,H^I_t,Pi_I) -- giving the Ideal State the same provenance/auditability the Knowledge State already has.

b_rows_sample.anchor: S_{t+1} = T(S_t, Operation, Policy, Evidence)
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies the deepest missing mathematical point: the theory has many functions (Zero, Lord, Sārathi, DiscoverDimensions, Compare, Resolve, Present) but no algebra of state transitions. Proposes S_{t+1}=T(S_t, Operation, Policy, Evidence) with required properties: determinism where required, provenance preservation, invariant preservation, authorization, reversibility/compensation where applicable, versioning — 'where the theory becomes an actual formal system rather than a conceptual ontology'.

type_signature.domain: state x operation x policy x evidence

b_rows_sample.anchor: Question \rightarrow Intent \rightarrow Context \rightarrow Knowledge \rightarrow Understanding \rightarrow NormativeAssessment \rightarrow Discrepancy \rightarrow Guidance \rightarrow Decision \rightarrow Action \rightarrow Outcome \rightarrow Observation
b_rows_sample.statement: Replaces the old Knowledge->Gap->Action loop with a longer, cyclic loop (Question->Intent->Context->Knowledge->Understanding->NormativeAssessment->Discrepancy->Guidance->Decision->Action->Outcome->Observation), formalized as a closed epistemic control loop S_{t+1}=T(S_t,Action_t,Outcome_t,Observation_{t+1}) — action produces consequences, consequences become observations, observations update knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: S_{t+1} = T( S_t, Observation, Evidence, Guidance, Decision, Action, Outcome, Policy )
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the epistemic-only transition Σ_{t+1}=ε(Σ_t,o_t) as incomplete: Chapter 3 shows transitions across knowledge, understanding, motivation, normative orientation, decision and action, giving the principal transition equation S_{t+1}=T(S_t,Observation,Evidence,Guidance,Decision,Action,Outcome,Policy) where S_t=(K_t,U_t,N_t,A_t,D_t,X_t,...). Also validates Progress = StructuredStateChange (not Progress∈[0,1]) and introduces Trajectory=(State_0,Transition_1,...,State_n) as first-class, broader than History/Provenance/Lineage; extends the epistemic lineage chain to Observation->Assertion->Understanding->NormativeAssessment->Guidance->Decision->Action->Outcome->Observation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Chapter 3 contains a feedback/cyclic system
b_rows_sample.statement: Verses 10-16's yajña cycle (Duty->Yajña->Rain->Food->Living Beings, tied back to prescribed action and Vedic direction) is read as a feedback/cyclic system, giving Action->Effect->SystemCondition->FutureAction, so ActionSystem=DynamicalSystem rather than a linear Workflow=Step1->Step2->Step3. Notes this supports event-sourced THINKING (S_n=fold(T,e_1,...,e_n)) but explicitly refuses the leap to 'therefore KnowledgeOS should use Event Sourcing' as an implementation conclusion the source does not support.

b_rows_sample.anchor: (K_t,Q,O,E,C) \rightarrow K_{t+1}
b_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts the bare LLM view y=f_theta(x) with a richer state transition (K_t,Q,O,E,C)->K_{t+1} (current Knowledge State, intent/question, observations, evidence, context), where the LLM is only one component producing the transition — 'LLM = one cognitive instrument used by the epistemic system', not 'LLM = intelligence'. Lists LLM roles as semantic parser, hypothesis generator, evidence interpreter, code generator, with KnowledgeOS deciding afterward whether output can become knowledge/an assertion, its provenance, supporting evidence, uncertainty, and conflicts — 'the missing governance layer'.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'ar-replay-differentiator-requires-history' POSSIBLY relates to 'state-transition-formalization' (batch B0051). Note: Finding that replay is a decisive differentiator between the epistemic projection (A,R) and the full ratified K_t: (A,R) alone cannot express replay, but adding the append-only history H restores it — used as evidence that the (A,R) projection is genuinely lossy.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Up to Step 99, we have established individual dimensions... a collection of correct mechanisms does not automatically constitute a correct architecture. Do all these mechanisms form one coherent closed system?
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames Step 100's central question: whether the individually-validated Steps 1-99 dimensions (Knowledge, Evidence, Inference, Decision, Authority, Execution, Security, Privacy, Evolution, Organization, Resources, Observability) form one coherent closed system, since correct mechanisms alone don't constitute a correct architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 100.1 — The closure proposition ... Reality→Observation→Evidence→Knowledge→Reasoning→Decision→Authority→Action→Outcome→Observation while simultaneously maintaining Security, Privacy, Provenance, Versioning, Assurance, Evolution. If the loop closes without violating the invariants established in Step
a_rows_sample.statement: States the closure proposition: the core loop must close without violating any invariant established in Steps 1-99 while maintaining Security, Privacy, Provenance, Versioning, Assurance, Evolution.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 100.2 — Closure does not mean perfection ... We are not trying to prove KnowledgeOS=Perfect. We are trying to establish the architecture is internally coherent, explicitly bounded, traceable, verifiable, and capable of controlled evolution.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes closure from perfection/universal correctness; the realistic claim is internal coherence, explicit boundedness, traceability, verifiability, and capacity for controlled evolution.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 100.3 — First closure test: Requirement → Knowledge ... Represent Requirement(R). KnowledgeOS transforms this into an explicit semantic constraint Invariant(I_R). Expected: R→I_R. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment: a requirement (e.g. 'production deployment requires architecture approval') transforms into an explicit Invariant(I_R); result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 100.4 — Requirement → Invariant → Architecture ... I_R→ArchitectureConstraint. For example Deployment⇒ApprovedChange. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment: an invariant becomes an architectural rule (e.g. Deployment⇒ApprovedChange); result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 100.5 — Architecture → Implementation ... ArchitectureConstraint→DeploymentGate. Expected: the rule is not merely documented. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment: an architectural constraint becomes enforceable implementation behavior (DeploymentGate), not merely documentation; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 100.6 — Implementation → Verification ... Implementation→Test→VerificationResult. For example UnauthorizedDeployment→Denied. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment: implementation generates verification evidence (e.g. UnauthorizedDeployment→Denied); result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 100.7 — Verification → Runtime ... Deployment→RuntimeInstance. The running instance must remain identifiable. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment: the verified implementation is deployed to an identifiable RuntimeInstance; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 100.8 — Runtime → Observation ... Runtime generates Observation, e.g. DeploymentEvent, linked to ArtifactVersion. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment: runtime generates Observation (e.g. DeploymentEvent) linked to ArtifactVersion; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 100.9 — Observation → Evidence ... Observation→Evidence only with appropriate provenance: source, time, identity, version, context, confidence/quality. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment: an observation becomes Evidence only with retained provenance (source/time/identity/version/context/confidence); result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 100.10 — Evidence → Knowledge ... Evidence→KnowledgeUpdate. For example ObservedDeployment→CurrentArchitectureState. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment: evidence updates organizational knowledge (ObservedDeployment→CurrentArchitectureState); result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 100.11 — Knowledge → Decision ... Knowledge→Inference→Decision. The system preserves Evidence≠Inference≠Decision. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment: knowledge supports reasoning (Knowledge→Inference→Decision) while preserving Evidence≠Inference≠Decision; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 100.12 — Decision → Authority ... Decision→Authority. The system can answer who was authorized to make this decision. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment: a decision must be associated with an authorized actor/governance mechanism, answerable to 'who was authorized'; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 100.13 — Authority → Action ... AuthorizedDecision→PermittedAction. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment: an authorized decision becomes a permitted action (AuthorizedDecision→PermittedAction); result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 100.14 — Action → Outcome ... Action→Outcome. Outcome becomes new observation. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment: execution produces Action→Outcome, and the outcome becomes a new observation; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 100.15 — Outcome → Learning ... ExpectedOutcome≠ObservedOutcome creates new knowledge. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment: a mismatch between expected and observed outcome creates new knowledge; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 100.16 — Learning → Evolution ... Knowledge may result in ModelUpdate, PolicyProposal, ArchitectureChange, ImplementationChange, but only through authorized change mechanisms. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment: learning may produce ModelUpdate/PolicyProposal/ArchitectureChange/ImplementationChange, only through authorized change mechanisms; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 100.17 — Evolution → Verification ... every material change returns to ImpactAnalysis→Verification. Evolution→Verification→Runtime. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment: every material change re-enters ImpactAnalysis→Verification→Runtime, closing the evolution loop; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 100.18 — The loop closes ... R→I→A→C→V→D→O→E→K→R'. K→R' because new knowledge can generate new requirements. That is closure.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the full closed loop R→I→A→C→V→D→O→E→K→R' (requirement, invariant, architecture, code/config, verification, deployment, observation, evidence, knowledge, new requirement), where K→R' since new knowledge can generate new requirements — this constitutes closure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 100.19 — But there is a second closure requirement ... The system must also preserve its epistemic integrity throughout the loop. TruthStatus_{t+1} must not be stronger than what the new evidence justifies. Unknown ⇏ Verified without evidence. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: States a second, epistemic-integrity closure requirement: TruthStatus_{t+1} must not be stronger than the new evidence justifies (Unknown ⇏ Verified without evidence); result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The architecture is a set of boundaries that make the constitutional forbiddances structurally impossible.
b_rows_sample.statement: The governing design principle of the Reference Architecture: each of the eleven constitutional laws forbids a specific epistemic collapse, and the architecture places a structural boundary so the forbidden flow cannot occur regardless of implementation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Article | Architectural boundary | Kernel service (PRESERVE) | Forbidden flow ... | Serving engines / representations
b_rows_sample.statement: Maps each of the eleven constitutional articles one-to-one onto an architectural boundary, a named PRESERVE kernel service, and the specific forbidden flow it makes structurally impossible (e.g. Article 6 Verification → Verification Gate → forbids generation⇒justification, claim-without-path⇒knowledge, pseudo-evidence⇒evidence).

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Verification Gate is the architectural keystone. It is the single admission boundary between candidate and knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Names the Verification Gate as the architectural keystone: the only admission path into knowledge (claim + authentic evidence + acquisition method + inference rule + reasoning path), through which every engine, LLM, and source must pass, realizing Articles 1, 6, 7, 9, 10, and 11 simultaneously.

b_rows_sample.anchor: LLM (governed mechanism) — generates candidates ... never writes to the knowledge store; its output enters ONLY through the Verification Gate as a candidate
b_rows_sample.statement: Places the LLM in the ENGINE layer as a governed generation mechanism at the mouth of the Verification Gate; it is architecturally incapable of the two things the Constitution reserves for the kernel — persistent epistemic identity (external Identity Service) and historical belief evolution (external History Service) — 'it may propose; it may never possess.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: PROPOSAL ... PROVENANCE ... VERIFICATION GATE ... LIFE
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the canonical verification path: any claim (Proposal) generates an evidence record, provenance is captured (acquisition method, reasoning path, inference rule, intent, agency), the Validation Engine proposes a verdict and the Verification Gate decides admission (VALIDATED→ENTRY / QUESTIONABLE→HELD / REJECTED→PRESERVED), after which knowledge lives on via contradiction, revision, projection, and advisory-only decision use.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the Kernel vs Engine separation is the most important architectural decision — it prevents confusing the mechanism that manages knowledge with the meaning of knowledge itself
b_rows_sample.statement: HPA ratification verdict on Constitution v1.0: the Kernel/Engine separation prevents four category confusions (graph database ≠ knowledge · vector embedding ≠ identity · LLM reasoning ≠ justification · workflow state ≠ truth · ontology ≠ reality); the eleven laws are anti-corruption constraints, not features.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. How do constitutional laws map to architectural boundaries? ... 6. Where are validation, reasoning, contradiction management, and history engines placed?
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses the six questions the commissioned Reference Architecture must answer (law→boundary mapping, kernel services, engine responsibilities, representation models, LLM placement, and the placement of validation/reasoning/contradiction/history engines) — later answered in full in S0243.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Design an architecture that satisfies the Constitution. Do not extend the Constitution.
b_rows_sample.statement: The strict standing instruction governing the architectural engineering phase: architecture must satisfy the frozen Constitution and never extend it (no new laws/concepts/rows; implementation choices out of scope).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero function (HPA) | Reference Architecture instantiation | Resolution ... Zero is therefore not a missing component — it is the property of the boundary design.
b_rows_sample.statement: Shows Zero is already distributed across the frozen Reference Architecture's kernel services (Verification Gate=neutral admission, Contradiction Registry=neutral suspension, Dimension Registry=comparison baseline, Identity+History=continuity, Decision Interlock+Projection+Agency=perspective without collapse, Authority Service=authority separation) rather than being a missing component.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 100.48 — The core architecture ... 8-layer diagram: Organization (Roles/Authority/Responsibility) -> Knowledge (Evidence/Claims/Context/Provenance) -> Reasoning (Rules/Models/AI/Uncertainty) -> Decision (Rationale/Scope/Dissent/Confidence) -> Governance (Authority/Policy/Approval/Exception) -> Execu
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents the canonical 8-layer core architecture diagram: Organization→Knowledge→Reasoning→Decision→Governance→Execution→Runtime→Evidence→(cyclic back to)Knowledge, wrapped by six cross-cutting concerns Security+Privacy+Versioning+Provenance+Assurance+ResourceGovernance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CF-001 · Worktree divergence (triage, T-1 check of the plan)
b_rows_sample.statement: The worktree .claude/worktrees/kos-v11-ddd/docs/knowledgeos/ holds 340 files vs main tree's 1,119 (881 divergent lines), including a Reference Architecture v1.1 document, an Expression-Meaning Port Contract, and an ADR absent from main; main holds EKS-05/07/09/10/11 backlog items the worktree lacks; which tree is authoritative for the KnowledgeOS reference architecture is not established by any record found in scope (later disposed RESOLVE-BEFORE-FINAL-ARCHITECTURE, then RESOLVED per GN-27, see phase-3c-dispositions-resolution.md).

b_rows_sample.anchor: CF-001 · RESOLVED — the worktree is a parallel authorized branch, not a rival tree
b_rows_sample.statement: Git evidence (2026-08-28): main tree is branch knowelegeos-modelling (HEAD f24edf31), worktree is branch kos-v11-ddd-refinement (HEAD 22e8e1f1, 2026-08-25, unmerged); fork point 6ef5d288 on 2026-08-22, with 66 commits on main vs 53 on the branch since, in parallel; Reference Architecture v1.1 is committed on the branch under explicit HPA authorization and verified against all six criteria (2026-08-23). Resolution: main branch is authoritative for the synthesis programme; kos-v11-ddd-refinement is a parallel authorized lane whose artifacts (including RA v1.1) are not part of this programme's record until a governed intake act — RA v1.1 must be either consumed via explicit intake or explicitly scoped out, named as a binding Final-Architecture input.

b_rows_sample.anchor: D-FA-2 · RA v1.1: RETAIN AS PARALLEL LANE / DEFER INTAKE
b_rows_sample.statement: Decision: neither INTAKE nor SCOPE OUT for RA v1.1 — deferred, retained as the parallel authorized lane. Evidence [E]: v1.1 is PROPOSED/NON-AUTHORITATIVE by its own status block even within its lane (r3 header read 2026-08-28); lives on unmerged branch kos-v11-ddd-refinement (GN-27/CF-001); is 705 lines of DDD refinement never conformance-tested against v0.2. Rationale: intake without a dedicated conformance pass would be silent merging (forbidden); scope-out would discard HPA-authorized lane work (also silent). Consequences: a named future 'RA v1.1 intake conformance pass' gate is the only path to intake; two v1.1 readings were taken as EVIDENCE not intake (section 14 Zero placement corroborates D-FA-3; section 9 UNKNOWN-initial lifecycle corroborates D-FA-1's evidence layer). Needs ratification: YES.

b_rows_sample.anchor: L3 — the repository architecture
b_rows_sample.statement: Describes L3 as the Reference Architecture v1.0: eleven kernel services (gates and records, never reasoners), an engine layer that proposes but never admits, and representation models; states L3 realizes L1 by construction, each article mapping to one boundary, one kernel service, one structurally impossible forbidden flow.

a_rows_sample.statement: Because the (mistaken) belief was that START would be a separate act, the --human-act text passed to the appointment carried a caveat denying it authorizes START; that same text is now recorded as the humanAct of seq 8, a START transition -- so the record contains a START whose own prose denies being a START authorization. a_rows_sample.anchor: AST-018 appoint collapses appointment and activation
a_rows_sample.statement: Finding O-6: one human act produces REGISTER+HANDOFF+START with no appoint-without-activate path through AST-018 appoint, and the same --human-act string serves as both the appointment authority and the START authority; judged not a defect but documented business intent (the tool's purpose is to remove UUID/REGISTER/HANDOFF/START mechanics from the human), yet worth recording because a person authorizing an appointment thereby also authorizes the start, and the estate's own vocabulary/prompts had treated these as two separate gates -- 'the vocabulary and the mechanisms disagree.' Status: RECORDED - NOT PROMOTED - NOT DECIDED (ES-006.1, first clean occurrence, methodology frozen), explicitly not a proposal to change AST-018 and not in REPAIR-001's scope.

a_rows_sample.statement: Independence bars differ by role and are kept separate deliberately: the REPAIR-001 implementer is barred only from being the verifier (must not repair what it verified, R-34/EP-02) or the governance process that scoped the slice, while the original AST-019 producer is explicitly NOT categorically barred from implementing (repairing one's own code is ordinary engineering); re-verification afterwards bars the first verifier, the producer, the scoping governance process, AND whoever implements REPAIR-001, since independence from the work under check is what makes the check worth anything -- collapsing verification-role bars onto implementation-role bars would shrink the eligible pool for no governed reason.

Substantive reason: defect F-1 was invisible to the entire prior 25-test contract suite, and the new tests certifying the fix (GO-26..GO-30) were written by the same process that wrote the fix, so the only present evidence of a cure comes from the party being certified -- explicitly NOT generalized into a rule that every implementation requires fresh verification, resting on this one named condition attached to this one named asset plus a blocking FAIL whose defect the existing suite could not see.
