a_rows_sample.statement: AI architecture principle: an AI agent should not be the source of wisdom; it discovers evidence, formulates questions, constructs causal hypotheses, identifies assumptions, runs analyses, exposes uncertainty, generates options and simulates consequences, but human/governed judgment produces the decision -- the platform supplies epistemic scaffolding, governance supplies legitimate authority, the agent supplies reasoning assistance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q1 — what problem was the model created to solve? ... "this model says what decisions an Engineer resolves with them"
b_rows_sample.statement: The Engineering Decision Model was created because standards say what the rules are, while the model says what decisions an engineer resolves with them: rules existed but the decisions they answer were unindexed. Its anti-problem: it is a decision INDEX, never a second rulebook (ARB, 2026-07-11) — created to prevent duplicated authority, not to add a layer. Its birth act included a vocabulary correction (2026-07-11): a DDD Domain Service is executable, a decision is a specification. Its adoption bar: one real engineering cycle must show consistent resolution through the model; it is DRAFT until earned.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q2 — which decisions does it explicitly model? ... Eight — all of one family
b_rows_sample.statement: Eight decisions are explicitly modeled, all of one family (the flow of knowledge and artifacts through governed work), grouped by question: 'Where does it belong?' (DetermineConcern, DeterminePlacement - mechanized by doc-placement.php); 'What is it/does it live?' (DetermineArtifactLifecycle - deletion litmus, DetermineArtifactType); 'Is it worth keeping/raising?' (DetermineReusePotential - Harvest, DeterminePromotionPath - ladder entry); 'What governs/verifies it?' (DetermineApplicableStandards, DetermineQualificationMethod). Deliberately excluded: ADR-making, capability approval, authority acts, promotion rulings — 'promotion is a human governance act and is never automated'; 'the AI evaluates and recommends — authority remains with governance.' The absence of governance decisions from the catalog is design, not gap.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q3 — which discovered decisions are not represented? ... FREEZE and RETIRE extend nothing in the catalog
b_rows_sample.statement: Answered in a prior Discovery pass and carried forward unchanged: FREEZE (n>=3, undeclared authority) and RETIRE (PM-6) extend nothing in the catalog, submitted as insufficiency evidence per the model's own stopping rule. Implicit but exercised: the challenge-commissioning trigger and terminology adoption. Nothing further found in this pass, which per the stopping rule is the correct amount.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q4 — does it govern the full ladder, or only architecture decisions? ... NEITHER — and the answer is the INVERSE of the commission's suspicion
b_rows_sample.statement: The model governs zero architecture decisions (no DetermineArchitectureDecision exists; ADRs are governance acts, outside the catalog by design). What it governs on the ladder Observation->Hypothesis->Evidence->Principle->Architecture is the entry points, not the rungs: DetermineReusePotential opens the ladder (observation->candidate); DeterminePromotionPath routes onto it (candidate->pilot->qualification->ARB decides). The rungs belong to ES-006.1, and the model correctly refuses to own them since it is an index, never a second rulebook.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q5 — Knowledge Governance or only Engineering Governance? ... Engineering Governance NOW; Knowledge Governance ANTICIPATED
b_rows_sample.statement: The model's own Decision Catalogs table states Engineering Standards answer the catalog's Engineering Decisions, while Project-Knowledge-class Knowledge Decisions (DetermineKnowledgeNeed, Source, Representation, Qualification, Promotion) are 'pilot-gated candidates — arrive only with pilot evidence; same pattern, different domain.' Engineering Governance is present now; Knowledge Governance is anticipated with the arrival condition already stated, and the entire ontology/meta-model corpus of this programme is exactly the kind of pilot evidence the anticipated catalog says it is waiting for.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q6 — extend the model, or map onto it? ... MAP. Tested element by element
b_rows_sample.statement: Ontology/meta-model elements map onto the existing decision model rather than extending it: archetype classification extends DetermineArtifactType (same question, richer vocabulary); KNOWLEDGE != ARTIFACT (I-1) is presupposed by DetermineArtifactLifecycle's deletion litmus; AUTHORITY-SCOPE/CONTAINER boundary maps to DetermineConcern/DeterminePlacement; GOVERNANCE-STATUS/EVIDENCE-STATUS maps to DeterminePromotionPath; NATURE (normative force) maps to DetermineApplicableStandards. Nothing in the ontology requires a new decision; the only extension pressure (FREEZE/RETIRE) is not ontology-driven, but comes from the enacted governance record. Verdict: the ontology supplies the vocabulary the catalog's procedures presuppose; the catalog supplies the purpose the ontology elements must serve — they interlock, neither extends the other.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q7 — would a second decision model violate ubiquitous language? ... YES — three times over
b_rows_sample.statement: A second decision model would violate ubiquitous language three times over: (1) the model's charter states it is 'a decision INDEX, never a second rulebook' — a v2 is exactly what it exists to prevent; (2) I-5, lint-enforced, requires one authoritative artifact per topic+context, so a second model is a literal violation; (3) ES-005.4 requires one rule -> one home. A competing 'KnowledgeOS Decision Model' would have been the UL violation and was not created; the Discovery and Validation passes are readings of the one model, not rivals to it.

Success criterion: every major engineering term gets one meaning, one owner, one place.

b_rows_sample.anchor: RESULT: THE MODEL DOES NOT SURVIVE INTACT. One claim FALSIFIED · two WEAKENED · two SURVIVED · two unchanged
b_rows_sample.statement: Overall falsification result: of the domain model's claims, one is falsified, two weakened, two survived, two unchanged; the strongest claim in the model (D-2) was among those weakened, by evidence the model itself had cited. Method: every test executed against artifacts, not reasoned from the model, using the repository's own instruments (Round47-OP's nine admissible justifications, the R16 Workbook Strong/Medium/Weak scale); four falsifiers were sought, three landed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: W-1 · D-2's "own decision series" is a shared authority — two of four grounds fall
b_rows_sample.statement: D-2's claim of 'its own decision series, ADR-M distinct from ADR-AIP' is weakened: Round39-D6's header states decision authority for all ADRs is 'sponsor + ARB' and amendment requires sponsor+ARB approval, so ADR-M is a scoping device under a shared authority, not a separate authority. Its claim of 'independent evolution' is falsified: Round39-D6 states the ADRs 'were authored together on 2026-06-25' — a series written in one sitting evidences independent subject, never independent evolution over time. This matches the ARB Chair's named falsifier 'ADR separation is historical rather than semantic' — half true: separation is real in subject, absent in time.

b_rows_sample.anchor: S-1 · D-2 survives on a ground I had not weighted — an explicit mutual scope exclusion
b_rows_sample.statement: D-2 survives on a new ground: Round39-D6's verbatim rule 'Governance discoveries (constitutional/capability) MUST NOT appear here. No DDD concepts here' is a deliberately maintained boundary (not an accident of filing), bidirectional in effect (ADR-M excludes governance, ADR-AIP carries no methodology rules), and survives the shared-authority finding since a shared authority that forbids itself from mixing two subjects is evidence FOR two models, not against. D-2 remains a boundary, but on subject exclusion, not on decision-series separation or independent evolution.

b_rows_sample.anchor: S-3 · D-1 survives every falsifier
b_rows_sample.statement: D-1 survives every falsifier sought: no multiple owners of the same concept found (DA/ARB throughout), no changes that fail to co-occur (ES set moves under STANDARDS_INDEX), no forced co-evolution with a product (ratification and freeze are product-independent), no absent invariants (append-only rulings, R-46).

b_rows_sample.anchor: U-1 | Was Round39-MC adopted by sponsor authority BECAUSE D-2 is independent, or DESPITE it being part of D-1?
b_rows_sample.statement: U-1: was Round39-MC adopted because D-2 is independent, or despite it being part of D-1 — the artifacts record the act but never the reason; only the sponsor and ARB know, and the model's validity turns on it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: U-4 | Is Round39-D6's scope exclusion still enforced, or was it stated once?
b_rows_sample.statement: U-4: is Round39-D6's scope exclusion still enforced or was it stated once — stated 2026-06-25, no subsequent enforcement event found.

b_rows_sample.anchor: U-6 | Does D-1 authorize D-2, or are they peers?
b_rows_sample.statement: U-6: does D-1 authorize D-2, or are they peers — carried forward, now sharper: shared ARB suggests peers-under-one-authority, not hierarchy.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Confidence — R16 Workbook scale, scored independently ... falsified ≠ unevidenced
b_rows_sample.statement: Per-domain confidence after falsification (R16 Strong/Medium/Weak scale): D-1 Strong->STRONG; D-2 Strong->MEDIUM; D-3 Strong->WEAK; D-6a (Evidence Protocol) new->MEDIUM; D-6b (Product Evidence) new->STRONG; D-5 (Engineering Capability, not a context) Medium->MEDIUM (unchanged, H-CAT-1 stands); D-4 (Workflow, rejected) ->STRONG as a rejection; D-7 (PKS, a context type) new->WEAK. Distinction drawn: falsified is worse than unevidenced — D-3 and D-7 carry contradicting evidence (falsified); D-6a carries no evidence (unevidenced).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Recommendation — per domain ... The model as a whole | REVISE, then re-test ... NOT canonical
b_rows_sample.statement: Per-domain recommendations: D-1 ACCEPT; D-2 REVISE (restate the boundary on the one surviving ground, Round39-D6's scope exclusion; delete 'own decision series' and 'independent evolution' as grounds); D-3 DEFER (untestable at n=1, revisit when a second runtime adapter exists); D-6a DEFER, D-6b ACCEPT; D-5 ACCEPT the demotion (do not promote until ARB overturns H-CAT-1 on evidence); D-4 ACCEPT the rejection; D-7 REVISE (restate as an observation of one instance, record PKS-as-projection as falsified). Overall the model as a whole: REVISE then re-test, NOT canonical — 2 of 8 accept, 3 revise, 2 defer, 1 accept-as-rejection.

group_evidence.why_grouped: an UNKNOWN-OBJECT-CANDIDATE row (batch B0006, source S0202) named these as alternative candidates for one piece of evidence. why_uncertain: External AKM/ADR literature finding about decision-history-as-asset; not clearly the same object as the corpus's own Engineering Decision Model or Decision Authority/ARB.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A decision-ready state is a Knowledge State that is sufficiently complete, coherent, and adequate for the current purpose, such that the Knower can make an informed decision with acceptable confidence.
a_rows_sample.statement: Original Q23 definition: a decision-ready state is a Knowledge State sufficiently complete, coherent and adequate for the current purpose, such that the Knower can make an informed decision with acceptable confidence. Boxed: Decision-Ready ≠ Complete; Decision-Ready = Sufficient for Purpose; Stop Condition = f(Sufficiency, Cost, Urgency, Risk, Policy).

a_rows_sample.anchor: ShouldStop(S_t, P_t, C_t, Policy_t) \in \{\text{True}, \text{False}\}
a_rows_sample.statement: The Stop Condition Framework: ShouldStop(S_t,P_t,C_t,Policy_t) is a boolean function of six criteria (Sufficiency S_u, Diminishing Returns D_r, Time/Cost T_c, Urgency U_r, Risk R_i, Policy P_o), combined as ShouldStop = Sufficient(S_t,P_t) ∨ BudgetExhausted(S_t,T_c) ∨ UrgencyThreshold(S_t,U_r) ∨ PolicyStop(S_t,P_o).

type_signature.domain: system state x purpose x context x policy

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sufficient(S_t, P_t) = \text{KnowledgeSufficient}(K_t, I^K_t) \land \text{UnderstandingSufficient}(U_t, I^U_t) \land \text{DomainSufficient}(X_t, I^D_t)
a_rows_sample.statement: Sufficiency is decomposed into Knowledge, Understanding and Domain sufficiency: Knowledge sufficient requires all ideal dimensions represented (D_I ⊆ D_Kt), all critical values known, all critical epistemic states meeting a threshold Σ_I, all critical relationships represented, and coherence maintained. Understanding sufficient requires conceptual understanding, implications understanding, uncertainty and conflict-resolution each meeting thresholds. Domain sufficient requires reality meeting constraints (X_t ⊨ C_I) and performance meeting a threshold.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \text{DiminishingReturns}(S_t) = \text{ExpectedValue}(\text{NextInvestigation}) < \text{Cost}(\text{NextInvestigation})
a_rows_sample.statement: Diminishing returns occur when the expected value of the next investigation step is less than its cost; ExpectedValue(d) = Impact(d) x Probability(d is actionable) x Severity(d); Cost(d) = Time(d) + Effort(d) + Resources(d).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Readiness = w_K \cdot K_c + w_U \cdot U_d + w_C \cdot C_r + w_{U_l} \cdot (1 - U_l) + w_D \cdot D_i + w_R \cdot R_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Original Readiness function: a weighted scalar in [0,1] over six factors (Knowledge Completeness K_c, Understanding Depth U_d, Conflict Resolution C_r, Uncertainty Level U_l, Decision Impact D_i, Risk Tolerance R_t); DecisionReady(S_t,P_t) iff Readiness(S_t,P_t) >= Threshold(P_t).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 8. The Arjuna Example: Stop Decision
a_rows_sample.statement: Walkthrough of Arjuna's decision states S0 (insufficient knowledge/understanding/domain, continue), S1 (partially sufficient after observation, continue), S2 (sufficient after moral resolution, STOP and present decision-ready state); stop criteria table shows sufficiency, diminishing returns, urgency and risk all favoring Stop.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DecisionReady \neq ShouldStop
a_rows_sample.statement: Correction to Q23: the original equation ShouldStop = Sufficient ∨ BudgetExhausted ∨ UrgencyThreshold ∨ PolicyStop is 'too permissive' because it implies exhausting budget or reaching urgency can make a state decision-ready, which is not epistemically correct. Fundamental distinction established: DecisionReady ≠ ShouldStop, and a forced stop does not mean the system is decision-ready (Stop ⇏ DecisionReady). Three outcomes of investigation identified: Decision-Ready→STOP, Not Ready→Continue, Not Ready→Forced Stop.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Unknown \neq Not\ Decision\ Ready
a_rows_sample.statement: Correction: the requirement that all critical dimension values be 'known' is too strong — some values can remain unknown while the decision is still valid if the uncertainty is decision-irrelevant (example: not knowing whether a probability is 17% or 18% when both lead to the same decision). Replaces with DecisionRelevantUncertainty(S_t,D) ≤ T_D, a policy-defined tolerance T_D.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Case C — Decision-critical unresolved conflict
a_rows_sample.statement: Refines 'conflicts resolved or accepted' into three ConflictStatus cases: (A) Resolved; (B) Accepted as unresolved (Knower explicitly accepts the uncertainty/conflict); (C) Active and decision-critical unresolved conflict, in which case DecisionReady = False. 'Accepted' therefore cannot automatically mean readiness.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
Knowledge = 95%
Understanding = 95%
Conflict Resolution = 95%
Critical unresolved safety conflict = YES
a_rows_sample.statement: The weighted-average Readiness score assumes all dimensions are compensable: a hypothetical case with 95% knowledge/understanding/conflict-resolution but an unresolved critical safety conflict could still average to Readiness=0.9 and incorrectly declare the state decision-ready. Presented as the counterexample motivating replacement of the scalar formula.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DecisionReady = \bigwedge_i G_i \land SoftCriteriaSatisfied
a_rows_sample.statement: Replaces the compensable weighted scalar with a hard-gates-plus-soft-indicators architecture: non-negotiable hard constraints G_1..G_n (e.g. G1=Coherent(K_t), G2=NoDecisionCriticalConflict, G3=CriticalEvidenceSatisfied, G4=CriticalDimensionsSatisfied) must all hold, DecisionReady = (⋀_i G_i) ∧ SoftCriteriaSatisfied. Readiness is redefined as a structured triple (HardGates, SoftIndicators, RemainingDeficiencies) rather than a scalar in [0,1]; a scalar R_score=f(SoftIndicators) may still be derived for UI purposes but must never override hard constraints. States the principle: 'Structured state is fundamental; scalar measurements are derived,' attributed as following from Q19/Q22.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EVSI = Expected\ Value\ of\ Information
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the diminishing-returns formula to account for decision impact via the Expected Value of Sample/Information (EVSI): EVSI(a) = E[decision quality after information] − decision quality now; continue investigation when expected decision benefit exceeds cost/risk. Flagged as an optional decision-theoretic mechanism, not a universal mathematical truth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Status = ForcedStopNotReady
a_rows_sample.statement: Urgency must not produce false readiness: 'Not sufficient + Urgent = STOP' is operationally fine but must produce Status = ForcedStopNotReady, not DecisionReady = True.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Discrepancy \rightarrow Findings \rightarrow Resolution Opportunities \rightarrow Prioritization \rightarrow Investigation \rightarrow Decision Sufficiency \rightarrow Decision Posture
a_rows_sample.statement: Overall assessment gives the original Q23 scores Conceptual 8/10, Mathematical 6.5/10, DDD 7.5/10, expecting 9.5/9/9.5 after corrections. States the central architectural insight: KnowledgeOS does not decide when 'enough knowledge' exists in the abstract, but whether enough decision-relevant knowledge exists for this Knower, this purpose, this context, and this decision — giving a progression chain from Discrepancy through Findings, Resolution Opportunities, Prioritization, Investigation, Decision Sufficiency, to Decision Posture (Q19→Q22→Q23).

a_rows_sample.anchor: A decision-ready state exists before presentation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrected definition: 'A decision-ready state is an evaluated system state in which the knowledge relevant to a specific decision satisfies the applicable decision criteria. Presentation is the projection of that state into a form usable by the Knower.' Formalized as DecisionReady(S_t,D,P,C) followed by P_t = Present(DecisionReadyState, Knower, Format), preserving the Q23 distinction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Resolution \neq \Delta=\emptyset
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the previous Arjuna example's claim 'After Moral Resolution -> Δ=∅' as a very important correction: even after normative resolution, uncertainty/risk/incomplete domain knowledge/emotional difficulty/consequences may remain, so Resolution ≠ Δ=∅; DecisionReady(Δ,P) may hold even though Δ≠∅. Generalized to abandon 'Δ=∅ ⇒ Success' entirely: DecisionReady=CriteriaSatisfied, not DecisionReady=NoRemainingGaps, so CompleteKnowledge is unnecessary for action — 'a very important property for a real engineering system'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DecisionReady(S,C) \iff DecisionCriteria(S,C)
a_rows_sample.statement: Clarifies that 'DecisionReady does not require Δ=∅' remains architecturally correct but is the theory's own engineering inference, not a theorem Chapter 3 itself establishes: DecisionReady(S,C) ⟺ DecisionCriteria(S,C), not DecisionReady ⟺ Δ=∅ — a design principle derived from the case, not a claim about the text.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Question 20 — What is the complete system state, and how does it evolve?
a_rows_sample.statement: Fragment listing question prompts without worked answers: Q16 'How do observation, evidence, inference, contradiction, uncertainty and resolution change epistemic status?'; Q17/Q19 (duplicated) 'How do we mathematically measure the difference between K_t and the relevant Ideal State without reducing fundamentally different deficiencies to an arbitrary scalar?'; a differently-numbered 'Question 17 — How do Zero, Lord, and Sārathi interact with the transition system?'; Question 20 'What is the complete system state, and how does it evolve?'; Question 21 'How do we prioritize which deficiencies to address first?'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero != Lord != Sarathi != Transition ... K_t -Zero-> Z_t -Lord-> L_t -Sarathi-> a_t -Commit-> e_t -delta-> K_{t+1} ... Zero, Lord, and Sarathi do not change K
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the initial Zero/Lord/Sarathi/Commit/Transition pipeline as a linear sequence culminating in a state change, with explicit invariants that Zero, Lord and Sarathi are each analytical (never transformational) and none of their outputs alone entail K_{t+1}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sarathi should not 'recommend Commit'... Commitment is not an epistemic action. It is an authorization/governance action... a_t -Authorize-> c_t -Execute-> e_t. Guidance != Authorization != Execution != Transition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Removes 'Commit' from Sarathi's action vocabulary and inserts an explicit Authorization boundary between recommendation and execution: Sarathi produces a recommendation a_t, Authorize(Knower,a_t,Policy) produces a command c_t, Execute(c_t) produces an event e_t, and only then does delta(K_t,e_t) fire -- Guidance != Authorization != Execution != Transition, with the missing Authorize function explicitly making the Knower's authority mathematically visible.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Execute: C -> E is too deterministic. Execution can fail... Execute(c_t) -> ExecutionResult in {Success(e),Failure(f),Partial(e,f)} ... ExecutionResult != DomainEvent.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Execute from a total deterministic function C->E to one returning a structured ExecutionResult (Success/Failure/Partial), and similarly Authorize to return an AuthorizationResult (Authorized/Rejected/Deferred/Modified) rather than assuming every recommendation becomes a command; ExecutionResult is explicitly distinguished from the DomainEvent that actually triggers a transition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the epistemic cycle is actually not always a cycle... External observation -> Event -> Transition can update the state directly... Guidance is optional; Transition is fundamental. G5 - Guidance is not a prerequisite for transition.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the closing theorem G5: Guidance (Zero/Lord/Sarathi) is not a prerequisite for every Knowledge-State transition -- a raw external observation event or a scheduled validity check can trigger delta(K_t,e_t) directly, so the lenses must never be modelled as mandatory middleware sitting between every event and the transition function; renames the pipeline from 'Epistemic Cycle' to 'Epistemic Guidance-and-Transition Cycle' to reflect this.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I strongly recommend introducing: I-hat_t = Candidate Ideal State and I_t = Approved Ideal State ... KnowledgeOS -> I-hat_{t+1} (proposal); Authorize(I-hat_{t+1}) -> I_{t+1}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a Candidate Ideal State (I-hat) vs Approved Ideal State (I) split mirroring the Q17 recommendation/authorization boundary: KnowledgeOS may only ever produce a candidate revision proposal, and only an explicit Authorize step (by the Knower/governance authority under applicable norms) produces the actually approved I_{t+1}; KnowledgeOS != I_{t+1} but KnowledgeOS -> I-hat_{t+1}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sārathi \rightarrow DecisionPosture
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Sarathi's output from a binary Stop/Continue decision to a richer DecisionPosture ∈ {Proceed, Investigate, ProceedWithCaveats, Defer, Escalate, UnableToDecide}, argued to be closer to Sarathi's actual role.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Recommendation \neq Assertion
b_rows_sample.statement: Strict boundary: Recommendation ≠ Assertion, Recommendation ≠ Fact, Recommendation ≠ Decision. Sārathi may say 'Investigate the moral obligation dimension' but KnowledgeOS must not silently convert that into 'Therefore Arjuna should fight' — the Knower remains the decision authority unless the domain explicitly delegates that authority. Marked as extremely important for the DDD model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate \neq Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Lord needs a stronger boundary too: Candidate ≠ Knowledge, Candidate ≠ Evidence, Candidate ≠ Assertion. A presentation should visually distinguish KNOWN / INFERRED / UNKNOWN / CANDIDATE / RECOMMENDED to prevent semantic contamination.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(S_t) \rightarrow EpistemicFindings
b_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms Zero's role as boundary-finder, not belief-decider: Zero(S_t) -> EpistemicFindings, Presentation ⊇ DecisionRelevant(EpistemicFindings); 'Zero does not decide what the Knower should believe. Zero says: Here is where the state has a boundary.' Also strengthens provenance: EveryDecisionRelevantClaim -> Provenance, with a worked claim-level provenance record example (Acquisition/Evidence/Observed-at/Validity/Conflict/Source).

b_rows_sample.anchor:
Unknown 
eq Absent 
eq NotApplicable 
eq NotObserved 
eq NotYetInvestigated
b_rows_sample.statement: Elevates 'unknown' to a fundamental principle already implicit in Zero: Unknown ≠ Absent ≠ NotApplicable ≠ NotObserved ≠ NotYetInvestigated, illustrated by Version=UNKNOWN not meaning Version=ABSENT, and SecurityStatus=NOT_ASSESSED not meaning SecurityStatus=SAFE.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero \neq UniversalValidator
b_rows_sample.statement: DDD warning that Zero risks becoming a 'god object' by owning detection of gaps, conflicts, type problems, temporal problems and epistemic boundaries all at once: Zero ≠ UniversalValidator. Zero is redefined narrowly as detecting epistemic boundaries/deficiencies relevant to current state and purpose, aggregating epistemic consequences of findings from separate domain validators (schema, type, policy, security violations).

b_rows_sample.anchor: LordCandidate \neq Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: LordCandidate ≠ Knowledge and LordCandidate ≠ Evidence: Lord can propose 'there may be a moral-obligation dimension' but it becomes knowledge only after investigation; critical to prevent AI-generated hypotheses entering the Knowledge State as facts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: S\bar{a}rathiRecommendation \neq Decision
b_rows_sample.statement: Sārathi needs a constitutional policy boundary: SārathiRecommendation ≠ Decision, SārathiAction ≠ HumanAuthorization — Sārathi may determine the next best investigation, but the Knower decides whether to accept it unless the system has explicitly delegated authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sārathi: (K,U,N,\Delta,P,Role) \rightarrow Guidance
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Sārathi(K,I,Δ)->Action as too simplistic: Sārathi:(K,U,N,Δ,P,Role) -> Guidance, which may then produce Decision, which may then authorize Action, giving Guidance ≠ Decision ≠ Action (confirming an earlier DDD warning). Also reframes Zero/Lord/Sārathi as three functions/lenses over the state rather than three sequential stages: Zero=Diagnose, Lord=Reason/Synthesize/Orient, Sārathi=Guide, with Decision->Action occurring outside those lenses; explicitly an architectural abstraction, not a literal theological equivalence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sārathi: (State, Norms, Role, Context, Discrepancies) \rightarrow Guidance
b_rows_sample.statement: Revises Sārathi(K,I,Δ)->Action (too direct) to Sārathi:(State,Norms,Role,Context,Discrepancies)->Guidance -> CandidateActions -> Decision -> Action, giving proper separation of concerns. Reaffirms Zero as a pure DiagnosticFunction that must not itself decide ('therefore do X'). Corrects Lord from 'merely a reasoning engine/LLM reasoning' to AuthoritativeKnowledge+NormativeOrientation+InterpretiveResolution, since Krishna in the text functions as an authoritative source of teaching, not just an inference engine — called crucial for KnowledgeOS governance. Confirms Sārathi = ContextualGuidance, distinguishing Lord ('what is authoritative/true/normative') from Sārathi ('how does that apply here') from Decision ('what will I choose') from Action ('what will I actually do').

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(K,I,C,P) \rightarrow \text{Epistemic Boundaries}
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes Zero/Lord/Sārathi as product capabilities rather than domain entities: Zero(K,I,C,P)->Epistemic Boundaries acts as an 'epistemic diagnostic engine' (missing dimensions, unknown values, missing/weak/conflicting evidence, logical contradictions, stale knowledge, contextual mismatches, unresolved questions, unsupported assumptions, Ideal-State discrepancies); Lord asks 'what else might matter?' enabling 'horizon expansion' beyond gap-checking; Sārathi:(K,I,Z,L,Q,C)->NextAction performs 'epistemic navigation', worked through a Bhīṣma-relationship example (Zero flags unknown relationship, Lord flags kinship as material, Sārathi recommends investigating it before evaluating the decision).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Can we migrate this Nexus installation?
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: asked 'Can we migrate this Nexus installation?', a conventional AI answers directly, while KnowledgeOS first constructs required dimensions (version, repository inventory, blob stores, storage, network, DNS, firewall, certificates, backup, dependencies, authentication, operational constraints), runs Zero to find missing items (backup verification, firewall confirmation, certificate ownership, dependency inventory), and has Sārathi respond 'Do not decide migration readiness yet. Investigate these four items.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: perform justified action given epistemic state
b_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts a conventional agent optimizing 'complete task' against KnowledgeOS optimizing 'perform justified action given epistemic state', worked through a deploy-approval example: required knowledge checklist (code reviewed✓, tests passed✓, architecture approved✓, security assessment✗, production configuration✗, rollback strategy✗) yields Zero='3 critical gaps' and Sārathi='DO NOT DEPLOY. Investigate security, configuration and rollback.' Also frames the agent loop as Understand Intent->Construct Knowledge State->Discover Dimensions->Zero->Identify Gaps/Conflicts->Lord->Expand Possible Investigation->Sārathi->Select Next Epistemic Action->Agent/Tool->Observation->Update Knowledge State->Repeat, called 'an epistemically governed autonomous agent architecture'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Retrieve(Q,K_t,I_t,C) \rightarrow EvidenceCandidates
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects plain Retrieve(Query)->Documents to a goal-directed Retrieve(Q,K_t,I_t,C)->EvidenceCandidates: the retrieval system 'knows why it is retrieving', discovering relevant dimensions (e.g. version, repository topology, blob stores, firewall, certificates for a migration decision) before retrieving. Zero can drive retrieval: given a partially-filled knowledge-state checklist, Zero reports specific gaps (backup verification, firewall rules, certificate ownership) and Sārathi generates a concrete investigation plan (search infrastructure docs for backup configuration, etc.), giving Zero -> Gap -> Sārathi -> Retrieval as part of the investigation loop, not a one-shot lookup.

type_signature.domain: question x knowledge state x ideal state x context

b_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Zero}(K_t)\rightarrow\text{epistemic boundary}
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero continuously reveals 'what is still unknown' (Zero(K_t)->G_t, G_0->G_1->...); ideally G_t->∅, but if the knowledge space is genuinely unbounded Zero may never establish G_t=∅. The stronger concept is Zero(K_t)->epistemic boundary, with Moksha representing the boundary itself being transcended rather than merely all currently detected gaps being filled — judged 'much more profound'.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'decision-readiness-stop-condition-model' POSSIBLY relates to 'zero-lord-sarathi-guidance-cycle' (batch B0020). Note: Question 23's formal model of when investigation should stop and a decision-ready state be presented, including the original stop/readiness equations and the in-file corrected version (hard gates, decision-relative sufficiency).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Avoiding hindsight contamination: evaluate decisions using knowledge/model available at decision time
a_rows_sample.statement: If Model_1 made a bad prediction and a later Model_2 would have predicted correctly, the original decision must not be evaluated using Model_2 -- 'hindsight contamination'. States: evaluate decisions using the knowledge and model available at decision time. Formalizes DecisionBasis(d_t) = K_t + M_t + Policy_t, never K_future + M_future -- 'this allows genuine historical audit'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: BadDecision vs ReasonableDecisionWithUnfortunateOutcome; ex ante vs ex post; decision quality != outcome
a_rows_sample.statement: A reasonable decision given K_t that later fails does not automatically mean DecisionWasWrong -- distinguishes BadDecision from ReasonableDecisionWithUnfortunateOutcome, and Ex ante ('what could reasonably be concluded at decision time') from Ex post ('what do we know after the outcome'), which must remain separate. Decomposes DecisionQuality = f(InformationAvailable, ReasoningQuality, PolicyCompliance, Outcome) -- outcome alone is insufficient. Worked examples: choosing an action with P(Success)=0.9 that then fails does not make the decision irrational (a well-justified decision can suffer a low-probability adverse outcome); conversely an action can succeed despite poor reasoning, so SuccessfulOutcome != GoodDecision -- 'a crucial learning safeguard'. KnowledgeOS should learn from Decision + DecisionBasis + Outcome, not merely Outcome.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Adaptive governance and decision reproducibility contract
a_rows_sample.statement: Policies evolve Policy_t -> Policy_{t+1}, but old decisions retain PolicyVersion_t, giving DecisionBasis=(K_t,M_t,Policy_t) as 'a complete historical decision snapshot'. Defines DecisionReproducibility: given K_t,M_t,Policy_t,Input_t we should ideally reproduce Decision_t; for a deterministic engine Decision_t=F(K_t,M_t,Policy_t,Input_t), and if identical inputs produce different results the cause (nondeterministic model, changed dependency, hidden state, external service, random seed) must be identifiable and recorded when reproducibility matters.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Stochastic AI reproducibility: Decision=F_theta,r(...); traceability instead of exact reproduction
a_rows_sample.statement: For LLM-based reasoning, Decision = F_theta,r(K,M,Policy,Input) where r is randomness/sampling; for auditability KnowledgeOS may need ModelVersion, PromptVersion, ToolVersions, EvidenceSnapshot. But reproducibility does not require deterministic AI: Traceability can be required instead of exact byte-for-byte reproduction -- the system should be able to explain which knowledge, model, policy and evidence were available.

a_rows_sample.anchor: LearningContext and GovernanceContext DDD boundaries; AI/Learning != GovernanceAuthority
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a DDD LearningContext boundary responsible for evaluating outcomes, detecting drift, updating models and proposing revisions -- but never silently mutating governance policy or domain facts. A separate GovernanceContext owns Policy; Learning can only propose a PolicyChangeCandidate, since AI/Learning != GovernanceAuthority.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Twelve falsification experiments for Step 45 adaptive-learning model (all PASS)
a_rows_sample.statement: Runs twelve falsification tests, all PASS: (1) new evidence contradicts an old interpretation => interpretation revised, original evidence unchanged; (2) a model becomes obsolete => historical decisions retain the old model version; (3) a new model performs better => does not automatically replace the active model unless promotion policy allows it; (4) input distribution changes but decision-relevant behavior does not => distribution drift recorded without declaring causal/model failure; (5) statistically significant drift has negligible operational impact => no automatic critical escalation from statistical significance alone; (6) a model predicts poorly despite good historical calibration => performance reevaluated, calibration alone does not protect the model; (7) a successful outcome follows a poor decision => outcome success does not automatically validate decision quality; (8) a justified decision produces an adverse low-probability outcome => not automatically classified as irrational; (9) a governance policy changes => future decisions use the new policy, historical decisions retain the old policy version; (10) a new interpretation of old evidence is created => both historical and current interpretations remain traceable; (11) a model trained on one bounded context detects drift => impact stays scoped to relevant contexts unless evidence supports broader generalization; (12) a candidate model performs well in shadow mode but violates a safety constraint => cannot be promoted.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 45 verdict and six deepest principles of safe knowledge evolution
a_rows_sample.statement: Declares STEP 45 -- PASS and states: Immutable evidence + Versioned interpretation + Governed learning = Safe knowledge evolution; new knowledge may invalidate old conclusions but must not invalidate the historical fact that those conclusions were once justified; Learning != rewriting history; Outcome != proof of decision quality; Drift detection != automatic model invalidation; Model improvement != automatic model promotion; Historical reproducibility requires preserving the knowledge, model, policy, and evidence state used at decision time.
