b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Quantity \neq Knowledge Completeness
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects 'Moksha = nearly infinite knowledge' as too narrow (equating it with maximal information). |𝒦|=∞ and |K_t|->∞ does not imply K_t->𝒦: an infinite subset can still miss infinitely much (ℕ⊂ℝ analogy — knowing every natural number is not knowing every real number), giving Knowledge Quantity ≠ Knowledge Completeness, 'exactly consistent with the Zero theory'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Moksha represents an epistemic condition in which the Knowledge Ātma has transcended the relevant epistemic boundaries of its journey, such that the discrepancy between its current understanding and its relevant Ideal State approaches zero.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Moksha as a limiting epistemic condition: lim_{t->T_M} Δ_t -> 0, provided Δ is defined relative to the relevant epistemic horizon rather than an assumed finite 'all knowledge' set. Suggests a stronger reading: Moksha as a change of 'epistemic regime' (Epistemic Regime_1 -> Epistemic Regime_M), closer to a mathematical phase transition than 'more data'; the Knowledge Ātma persists through this transformation (𝒜_K persists while its epistemic relationship with 𝒦 fundamentally changes).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Moksha\neq\text{achievement of one finite Ideal State}
b_rows_sample.statement: Moksha ≠ K_t=I_t, because the Ideal State itself can evolve (I_0->I_1->I_2->...); Moksha is instead 'transcendence of the ordinary finite epistemic journey'. Formalizes a Moksha transition object M=(K_{T_M},T_M,𝒜_K,𝒦,Γ_M) where T_M is the transition point, K_{T_M} the knowledge state there, 𝒜_K the Knowledge Ātma, 𝒦 the Knowledge Space, and Γ_M the epistemic regime/condition defining Moksha: K_{T_M} 'is not merely large; it is epistemically transformed'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Gītā concept \rightarrow conceptual abstraction \rightarrow mathematical hypothesis \rightarrow architecture only if validated
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommends NOT implementing Moksha as a literal software state; model it as a theoretical/metaphorical upper-bound concept unless later Gītā examination gives sufficiently precise reason to make it architectural. States the governing discipline: Gītā concept -> conceptual abstraction -> mathematical hypothesis -> architecture only if validated — 'the Gītā generates hypotheses for KnowledgeOS; mathematics tests their coherence; DDD determines whether they deserve to become domain concepts.' Also provides a nine-row terminology table (Ātman/Knowledge Ātma/Knowledge Space/Knowledge State/Ideal State/Zero/Lord/Sārathi/Moksha) and a mathematical-hierarchy summary 𝒜_K persists through K_t⊆𝒦, with K_t --Zero--> Δ_t --Lord--> H_t --Sārathi--> K_{t+1}.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'moksha-epistemic-limit-concept' POSSIBLY relates to 'knowledge-atma-identity-concept' (batch B0020). Note: A theoretical/metaphorical upper-bound epistemic condition: the Knowledge Ātma transcending its relevant epistemic boundaries such that discrepancy against the relevant Ideal State approaches zero, possibly via a change of 'epistemic regime' rather than accumulation of more data; explicitly not recommended as a literal software state without further validation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K=(D,R) where D = dimensions/factors, R = relations among those factors. ... Knowledge emerges from distinguishable factors + relations between them.
a_rows_sample.statement: Replaces K=(d_1,...,d_n) with K=(D,R): a factor by itself is not yet knowledge; a relation such as R(d_1,d_2|Q) is required for epistemic significance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: d_3=0 doesn't mean that d_3 has no existence or meaning. It means, for the current inquiry: R(d_3,d_j)\approx 0 for the relevant relationships.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reinterprets dimensional zeroing as neutralizing a dimension's relational influence rather than asserting its non-existence, so activating another dimension can change the relational structure even though d_3 itself has not changed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A distinguishable factor becomes epistemically informative only through a relation to something else under a question or purpose. ... No distinction without relation.
a_rows_sample.statement: States (with an explicit exception for internally-structured single factors, e.g. a temporal sequence) the deeper principle 'no epistemically meaningful distinction without a relation that makes the distinction relevant', and proposes a relational Knowledge Algebra KA=(D,R,Q,T,O,I) instead of an object algebra (K,+).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Focus_S(K) = activate a selected relational subspace while neutralizing other influences.
a_rows_sample.statement: Redefines Focus as activating a relational subspace (what can emerge from the relationship between chosen dimensions while others are held neutral) rather than merely 'looking at fewer dimensions', yielding the chain Factor->Relation->Interaction->Determination->Knowledge alongside Zero->neutralize influence->isolate relation->Focus->observe what emerges.

a_rows_sample.anchor: After we separate the concerns of a knowledge system using DDD, where does "śūnya" appear as a property of the knowledge system? ... Knowledge Śūnya may be the absence of inherent, context-independent determination.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the guiding hypothesis: no knowledge claim is self-sufficiently determined outside the relations (question, context, evidence, standards, time) that give it meaning -- Status(C)=f(C,Q,Context,E,Standards,t), not Status(C)=f(C).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Śūnya may occur not in the object, but in the missing relation. ... Claim \setminus Question ... Claim \setminus Evidence ... Claim \setminus Context
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues that removing one supporting relation (question, evidence, or context) from a claim can empty its epistemic determination while the claim itself syntactically survives -- Sunya located in the missing relation, not the object.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Object Śūnya \neq Knowledge Śūnya \neq Contribution Zero
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three non-equivalent emptiness notions: object emptiness (x=empty), determination emptiness (Determine(x,K_t)=empty), and relational emptiness (Contribution(x|Q,C,E)=0).

a_rows_sample.anchor: H-SUNYA-01 -- Relational Epistemic Emptiness ... Empty_{Q,C,E,S}(x,K_t) \iff \neg\exists d\; Determine(d\mid x,Q,C,E,S,K_t)
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes hypothesis H-SUNYA-01 with two explicit non-implications (Empty does not imply not-True(x), and does not imply x=empty), and explicitly declines to identify this with the existing Knowledge Algebra Zero until a common structure is discovered.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Śūnya appears where an assumed intrinsic meaning disappears once context boundaries are respected. ... Relation not established \Rightarrow no legitimate inference.
a_rows_sample.statement: States that DDD's bounded-context non-inheritance rule (e.g. Evidence.supports != Determination.justified != Governance.accepted) itself creates possible semantic emptiness at each un-crossed boundary, offered as possibly the most useful KnowledgeOS reading of Sunya.

b_rows_sample.anchor: After we separate the concerns of a knowledge system using DDD, where does 'sunya' appear as a property of the knowledge system? Knowledge Sunya may be the absence of inherent, context-independent determination. Not 'knowledge is nothing.' Rather: No knowledge claim is self-sufficiently determined o
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses the central question of where 'sunya' appears once a knowledge system's concerns are DDD-separated, answering that Knowledge Sunya is the absence of inherent, context-independent determination -- no knowledge claim is self-sufficiently determined outside the relations that give it meaning -- not that knowledge is nothing.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Question Context: What are we trying to determine? Claim Context: What is being asserted? Evidence Context: What supports or challenges the assertion? Challenge Context: What could invalidate, restrict, contradict or qualify it? Determination Context: What can currently be justified? Revision Contex
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies DDD separation of concerns to a knowledge system, defining six bounded contexts (Question, Claim, Evidence, Challenge, Determination, Revision) each with a distinct responsibility, preventing the conflation of claim, truth, evidence, determination, and knowledge into one object.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Status(C) != f(C) but rather: Status(C) = f(C, Q, Context, E, Standards, t). This is where I think Knowledge Sunya begins to appear.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes that a claim's status is never a function of the claim alone (Status(C)!=f(C)) but of the claim together with question, context, evidence, standards, and time (Status(C)=f(C,Q,Context,E,Standards,t)), identifying this as the entry point where Knowledge Sunya begins to appear.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Sunya does not mean Claim=empty-set. It means something more subtle: Claim not-equiv Knowledge and Claim not-equiv Determination. A claim by itself does not carry its complete epistemic status. It requires relations.
b_rows_sample.statement: Clarifies that Knowledge Sunya does not mean the claim object is empty, but rather that a claim is not equivalent to knowledge and not equivalent to determination -- a claim by itself does not carry its complete epistemic status, which requires relations to other contexts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Claim \ Question. The claim still syntactically exists. But its epistemic determination may disappear. Claim \ Evidence. The assertion remains, but justification may disappear. Claim \ Context. Its applicability may disappear. Sunya may occur not in the object, but in the missing relation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues, via three worked removals (Claim minus Question, minus Evidence, minus Context), that Sunya occurs not in the object itself but in a missing relation: removing the question can erase epistemic determination, removing evidence can erase justification, and removing context can erase applicability, even though the claim syntactically persists.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeSunya(C|Q,X,E,S,t) when the claim has no justified determination under the specified epistemic relations. KnowledgeSunya(C|Q,E,t) if not-exists d Determine(d,C,Q,E,t). But crucially KnowledgeSunya(C|Q,E,t) does not mean C=false, and does not mean C=nonexistent. It means: the epistemic syste
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the research predicate KnowledgeSunya(C|Q,X,E,S,t): the claim has no justified determination under the specified epistemic relations (not-exists d such that Determine(d,C,Q,E,t)), explicitly not implying the claim is false or nonexistent, only that the epistemic system currently has no justified determination of it under that frame.

b_rows_sample.anchor: D(C1) != D(C2). The claim itself didn't change. Its relational determination changed. This is extremely close to our earlier finding with Zero: Zero(x|D1) != Zero(x|D2).
b_rows_sample.statement: Shows via a worked context-change example (the same claim C determined under context C1 but undetermined under context C2, D(C1)!=D(C2), with the claim itself unchanged) that relational determination is context-relative, drawing a direct parallel to the already-established contextual-Zero finding Zero(x|D1)!=Zero(x|D2).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Object emptiness: X=empty-set. There is literally no object/content. 2. Determination emptiness: Determine(X,K_t)=empty-set. There is no justified determination. 3. Relational emptiness: Contribution(X|Q,C,E)=0. The object contributes nothing under a specified epistemic relation. These are not eq
b_rows_sample.statement: Fixes a Knowledge Sunya triangle of three explicitly non-equivalent emptiness notions: Object emptiness (X=empty-set), Determination emptiness (Determine(X,K_t)=empty-set), and Relational emptiness (Contribution(X|Q,C,E)=0) -- Object Sunya != Knowledge Sunya != Contribution Zero.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence Context: 'supports' != Claim Context: 'asserts' != Determination Context: 'justified' != Governance Context: 'accepted' != Execution Context: 'authorized'. A piece of information can exist in one context while having no determination in another. Meaning is bounded by context. Sunya appears
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues that Sunya is a boundary concept between bounded contexts (Evidence's 'supports', Claim's 'asserts', Determination's 'justified', Governance's 'accepted', Execution's 'authorized' are all distinct meanings), since information existing in one context can have no determination in another -- meaning is bounded by context, and Sunya appears exactly where an assumed intrinsic meaning disappears once context boundaries are respected.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence.supports(C) does not automatically imply Determination.justified(C). And Determination.justified(C) does not automatically imply Governance.accepted(C). And Governance.accepted(C) does not imply C=True, unless the relevant contract explicitly establishes that relationship. So every boundary
b_rows_sample.statement: Chains three explicit non-implications across bounded contexts (Evidence.supports does not imply Determination.justified; Determination.justified does not imply Governance.accepted; Governance.accepted does not imply True, absent an explicit contract), concluding every inter-context boundary creates a possible semantic emptiness: a relation not established implies no legitimate inference -- possibly the most useful KnowledgeOS interpretation of Sunya.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We should not say 'DDD proves Nagarjuna.' It does not. Madhyamaka gives us a philosophical hypothesis: things do not possess independent inherent existence; their determination depends upon relations. DDD gives us an architectural method: separate contexts according to different semantic responsibil
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly refuses to claim 'DDD proves Nagarjuna', instead assigning each tradition its proper role: Madhyamaka supplies a philosophical hypothesis (things lack independent inherent existence; determination depends on relations), DDD supplies an architectural method (separate contexts by semantic responsibility, never assume universal validity of one context's meaning), and KnowledgeOS supplies the actual epistemic research question (does context-relative determination produce meaningful epistemic emptiness when determining relations are removed).

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t = (C_t, E_t, Ch_t, D_t, Q_t, R_t, H_t) where C_t=claims, E_t=evidence, Ch_t=challenges, D_t=determinations, Q_t=questions, R_t=revisions, H_t=history/provenance. Knowledge Sunya could occur when a required relational path to determination is absent: C_t -?-> D_t. There is a claim. But no valid p
b_rows_sample.statement: Restructures the knowledge state K_t into seven explicit relational components (claims, evidence, challenges, determinations, questions, revisions, history/provenance), locating Knowledge Sunya as the absence of a required relational path from claims to determination (C_t != empty-set while D_t(C_t)=empty-set), a very different kind of emptiness from an empty claim set.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t: C='X always causes Y.' Challenge: counterexample. Determine_t(C)=Universal becomes Determine_{t+1}(C)=Conditional. The previous determination becomes empty with respect to the universal claim, but not empty with respect to the qualified claim. Universal(C) -> Sunya -> Conditional(C). Sunya can
b_rows_sample.statement: Illustrates Sunya as a transitional epistemic space via a worked example: a universal claim challenged by a counterexample transitions Universal(C)->Sunya->Conditional(C), where the prior universal determination becomes empty while a qualified determination has not yet been established -- not 'there is nothing' but a state between two determinations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Determination -> Challenge -> Sunya -> Revision -> New Determination. The negative contribution can create a temporary epistemic Sunya from which a better determination emerges. ... Argument -> Challenge -> Sunya -> Qualification -> Purified Knowledge. The challenge removes the false certainty, not
b_rows_sample.statement: Inserts Sunya into the purification cycle as an intermediate transitional stage (Determination->Challenge->Sunya->Revision->New Determination, equivalently Argument->Challenge->Sunya->Qualification->Purified Knowledge), proposing the candidate interpretation that Knowledge Sunya is not the absence of knowledge but the absence of unjustified determination -- the challenge removes false certainty, not the underlying subject matter -- kept as a candidate interpretation pending testing.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H-SUNYA-01 -- Relational Epistemic Emptiness. A knowledge claim has no inherent epistemic determination independent of the question, context, evidence, standards and temporal state through which it is evaluated. ... Empty_{Q,C,E,S}(x,K_t) iff not-exists d Determine(d|x,Q,C,E,S,K_t), while explicitly
b_rows_sample.statement: States the formal research hypothesis H-SUNYA-01 (Relational Epistemic Emptiness): a knowledge claim has no inherent epistemic determination independent of question, context, evidence, standards, and time, formalized as Empty_{Q,C,E,S}(x,K_t) iff no determination exists under those relations, with the two required non-implications explicitly preserved (never implies the claim is false, never implies the claim is the empty object).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Elimination Zero: representation. Balance Zero: contribution. Knowledge Sunya: determination. Purification: transition. They interact, but we don't yet know whether they are manifestations of one deeper mathematical structure. That should be discovered, not assumed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates the four Zero-adjacent research threads by their domain -- Elimination Zero (representation), Balance Zero (contribution), Knowledge Sunya (determination), Purification (transition) -- explicitly leaving open, as a discovery question rather than an assumption, whether they are manifestations of one deeper mathematical structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t --challenge--> Sunya --inquiry--> K_{t+1} may become the epistemic purification cycle. Knowledge Sunya is not 'nothingness in knowledge'; it is the state in which a determination has no valid grounding within a specified epistemic frame. And DDD gives us the machinery to locate which relation is
b_rows_sample.statement: States the strongest current hypothesis and closing architecture: K_t--challenge-->Sunya--inquiry-->K_{t+1} as the epistemic purification cycle, with Knowledge Sunya defined as the state in which a determination has no valid grounding within a specified epistemic frame, observable precisely at the DDD boundary where a claim's assumed inherent determination disappears once its supporting relations are separated and made explicit.

a_aliases: K as dimensions plus relations (not a bare tuple)
b_aliases: Where Sunya appears after DDD separation of concerns

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_{t+1} = Learn( K_t, Observations_t, Events_t, Policies_t, Outcomes_t )... the source states the decision and world equations (A_t = Decision(K_t, S_t, Policy_t); S_{t+1} = F(S_t, A_t, U_t)), keeping three evolutions -- of knowledge, of choices, of the world -- as three different functions.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the knowledge state's time-indexed dynamics as three separate evolution functions: K_{t+1}=Learn(K_t, Observations_t, Events_t, Policies_t, Outcomes_t) for knowledge, A_t=Decision(K_t, S_t, Policy_t) for choices, and S_{t+1}=F(S_t, A_t, U_t) for the world -- kept as three distinct functions, with time-indexing meaning there is no bare "the knowledge," only knowledge-as-of-t.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CORE: Entity, State, Event, Observation / EPISTEMIC: Evidence, Claim, Uncertainty / SEMANTIC:... / RELATIONAL:... / GOVERNANCE:... / OPERATIONAL:... / EVOLUTION:... Then, family by family, the source interrogates each concept -- is this primitive, or constructible? -- and most collapse... What survives... K = (E, S, T, O, P, R, Pi, A)
a_rows_sample.statement: Reproduces the source's reduction derivation from an initial seven-family stratification (Core/Epistemic/Semantic/Relational/Governance/Operational/Evolution) to the frozen eight-tuple candidate kernel K=(E,S,T,O,P,R,Pi,A) -- entities, states, temporal/event structure, observations, propositions, typed relations, policies, actions -- by showing most non-core concepts (Evidence, Claim, Identity, Provenance, Causality/Dependency, Uncertainty, Authority/Decision, Outcome, Learning/Revision/Drift) individually reduce to typed structure over the four cores plus the four surviving structure-carriers (Proposition, Relation, Policy, Action).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence = QualifiedObservation... Claim = Proposition... Identity = EntityIdentityRelation... Uncertainty = epistemic annotation U(C) (probabilistic OR not -- 49.10's Probability != EpistemicConfidence)... Authority = governance structure over decisions (Authority(actor, d))... resist inventing primitives -- the reduction's whole yield is that richer notions are TYPED STRUCTURE
a_rows_sample.statement: Lists the derived-structure layer -- the equations by which richer concepts are expressed as typed structure over the eight primitives rather than as new primitives themselves (Evidence=QualifiedObservation; Claim=Proposition; Identity=EntityIdentityRelation; Provenance=TypedDependencyRelation; Uncertainty=epistemic annotation U(C), explicitly not assumed probabilistic -- Probability != EpistemicConfidence; Authority=governance structure over decisions; Decision=structure over K,S,Policy with Proposal kept distinct from AuthorizedDecision; Outcome=observed consequence of Action; Learning/Revision/Drift=evolution structure) and states the modelling discipline this yields: resist inventing new primitives, since typed structure can be checked/queried/governed in ways ad-hoc primitives cannot.

a_rows_sample.anchor: stress-tested by twelve falsification experiments (49.78-49.89... What the argument does not and cannot claim, and the source itself refuses to claim: completeness... minimality... and uniqueness... The source's own word is the governing one: a candidate mathematical kernel.
a_rows_sample.statement: Teaches PF-2 in place at its exact strength: the eight-primitive reduction argument is RECONSTRUCTABLE, stress-tested by twelve falsification experiments (each attempting to express a rich concept in Structure(primitives) and failing the kernel if it cannot be done) plus Step 050's fifty-attack consistency audit; but completeness (no needed concept will ever fail to reduce), minimality (no seven-element basis would suffice -- the source concedes Entity is "arguably" Identity+State, kept for DDD-pragmatic reasons), and uniqueness (no alternative basis exists) remain explicitly NOT ESTABLISHED, matching the source's own characterization of it as a "candidate" kernel and a design result, not a theorem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Collapse the typed relation set into a single generic RelatedTo(A, B) and semantics die: an AI consumer, seeing RelatedTo everywhere, infers RelatedTo => Causes -- recreating "one of the fundamental problems we eliminated in Step 43." One typed set, seven meanings; one generic edge, license to hallucinate causality.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reproduces the source's own worked failure case for mis-typing the Relation primitive: collapsing the seven typed relations (Supports, DependsOn, Causes, Identifies, MapsTo, Contradicts, Precedes) into a single generic RelatedTo(A,B) edge causes an AI consumer to infer RelatedTo implies Causes, recreating a causal-hallucination failure mode the architecture had previously eliminated; extended to the election running example (DerivedFrom(wireSummary,wireReport) and Supports blurred into RelatedTo would let a derived summary quietly become a second independent witness) as the same dependency failure seen at the primitive-typing layer.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Theory is the formal theory ... to answer: How can a system represent, transform, evaluate, preserve, revise, and act upon knowledge without confusing reality, information, evidence, truth, determination, decision, and action? It is not yet a finished universal 'Knowledge Algebra.' The strongest current form is a theory of epistemic state, representation, evidence, inquiry, propositions, and transformations, with some parts still explicitly research-stage.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the central question KnowledgeOS Theory answers and its current honest scope: a theory of epistemic state/representation/evidence/inquiry/propositions/transformations, explicitly not yet a finished universal Knowledge Algebra.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reality -> Observation -> Information -> Representation -> Proposition -> Evidence -> Warrant/Reasoning -> KnowledgeState -> Determination -> Decision -> Authorization -> Action -> Outcome -> NewEvidence. Evidence is not Truth. Observation is not Evidence. Representation is not Ontology. Determination is not Truth unless a soundness bridge has been established. Decision is not Determination. Decision is not Action. Unknown is not False. Correlation is not Causation. A graph is not automatically a Knowledge State. A path is not automatically an inference. Hash equality is not semantic identity. These distinctions prevent the system from making epistemic category errors.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the fourteen-stage conceptual chain from Reality to NewEvidence and eleven protective non-identities (Evidence!=Truth, Observation!=Evidence, Representation!=Ontology, Determination!=Truth without a soundness bridge, Decision!=Determination, Decision!=Action, Unknown!=False, Correlation!=Causation, graph!=KnowledgeState, path!=inference, hash-equality!=semantic-identity), framed as preventing epistemic category errors.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t = (Content,Support,Uncertainty,Model,Alternatives,History,Identity,Context,Inquiry,Status), but this is currently treated as a semantic decomposition, not necessarily a mandatory implementation tuple. Knowledge State != Representation. Different representations may potentially represent the same semantic state. But the theory is deliberately cautious: semantic equivalence of arbitrary representations has not been universally established.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the K_t semantic decomposition (explicitly non-mandatory) and the Knowledge State != Representation principle, cautioning that semantic equivalence of arbitrary representations is not universally established -- directly consistent with this same batch's F4 audit findings on equiv_sem.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [[s]]_Gamma = p where s is a representation/sentence and p is the proposition interpreted under context Gamma. Truth(p,w,Gamma,t) in {0,1}. This allows the theory to distinguish assertion != determination != truth.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the proposition-interpretation formalization [[s]]_Gamma=p and truth evaluation Truth(p,w,Gamma,t), supporting the three-way distinction assertion != determination != truth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ev(e,p,Gamma,t) meaning that evidence e bears upon proposition p under context Gamma at time t. Evidence != Truth and Evidence != Knowledge. two pieces of evidence != two independent pieces of evidence. Two documents may simply copy the same original source. path != independent evidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates evidence as a relational predicate Ev(e,p,Gamma,t) rather than a property of an object, deriving Evidence!=Truth, Evidence!=Knowledge, and the independence warning that multiple evidence items copying the same source do not constitute independent corroboration, nor does a mere graph path constitute independent evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: q=<X,Y,Gamma,tau,Pi,Lambda> and more fundamentally an inquiry can be understood as an answer-producing function q:W->Y. This leads to the concept of inquiry-relative adequacy. A representation does not have to preserve everything. It has to preserve what is necessary to answer the inquiry correctly.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the inquiry formalization as a six-tuple and as an answer-producing function q:W->Y, grounding the concept of inquiry-relative adequacy (a representation need only preserve what answers the inquiry correctly, not everything).

b_rows_sample.anchor: T:X->X' transforms a representation. Q=g o T where Q is the inquiry-relevant observable. The preservation condition can be expressed as Pi o T = Pi o T o E_S for an appropriate elimination/reduction structure. This provides the foundation for reasoning about reduction, elimination, equivalence, sufficient representations, preservation, semantic invariants, and Zero.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the transformation and preservation formalization (T:X->X', Q=g∘T, the preservation condition Pi∘T=Pi∘T∘E_S), naming it the foundation for the whole reduction/elimination/equivalence/Zero research family already covered extensively in this batch's kr-rep-reduction-related documents.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero is not simply the number 0. A Knowledge Gap can be represented as a set of unsatisfied requirements: Delta_t = {r in R_t: not Sat(K_t,r)}. Then Delta_t=empty means that there is no remaining requirement gap under the relevant satisfaction semantics. Zero equiv empty gap rather than merely numerical zero. This connects your algebraic work with the epistemic theory.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates Zero as structurally equivalent to an empty requirement gap (Delta_t=empty) rather than numerical zero, explicitly connecting the algebraic Zero research line to the epistemic Delta_t/Sat theory just extensively audited in this same batch.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_{t+1} = T(K_t,E_{t+1},Q_t,C_t,EC_t,A_t). H_{t+1}=H_t union {transition_t}. current candidate operation nucleus includes ASSERT, LINK, REVISE, RETRACT, ISOLATE. But importantly, these are not all canonically frozen as the final minimal operation set. Operation minimality remains an open research problem.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the state-evolution transition formula and history-append formula, listing a five-operation candidate nucleus (ASSERT/LINK/REVISE/RETRACT/ISOLATE) while explicitly flagging operation minimality as an open research problem, not a frozen final set.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS does not adopt the simplistic rule P, not-P => everything. Instead, contradiction is represented and isolated. real knowledge systems routinely contain conflicting observations, competing hypotheses, outdated information, incompatible sources, different contextual truths. So contradiction is an epistemic state to manage, not a reason to destroy the entire knowledge state.
b_rows_sample.statement: States KnowledgeOS's explicit rejection of classical explosion (P, not-P => everything) in favor of representing and isolating contradiction as a manageable epistemic state, motivated by five named real-world sources of conflicting information.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Status table (15 rows): K_t as epistemic state RESOLVED/RATIFIED; Reality!=knowledge state ESTABLISHED; Evidence!=truth ESTABLISHED; Truth!=determination!=decision ADOPTED/FOUNDATIONAL; Contradiction/non-explosion RESOLVED/ADOPTED; Representation theory SUBSTANTIALLY DEVELOPED; Inquiry semantics DEVELOPED; Proposition semantics DEVELOPED; Evidence semantics DEVELOPED; Transformation theory SUBSTANTIALLY DEVELOPED; Universal Knowledge Algebra NOT ESTABLISHED; Canonical minimal operations OPEN RESEARCH; Complete F4 Sat(K_t,r) semantics NOT ESTABLISHED; Universal semantic equivalence r1 equiv_sem r2 NOT ESTABLISHED; F3<->F4 semantic bridge OPEN.
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives a comprehensive fifteen-item status table for the whole theory, distinguishing resolved/established/adopted foundations from explicitly open items (universal Knowledge Algebra, canonical minimal operations, complete F4 Sat semantics, universal equiv_sem, F3<->F4 bridge), the last three matching exactly the open items just extensively audited in this same batch's F4/Model-B series.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The existence and role of Sat are present in the historical corpus, but a fully operational, corpus-native definition of Sat(K_t,r) has not yet been recovered. The later Sat* construction is therefore a candidate construction, not proof that the corpus already contained that exact semantics.
b_rows_sample.statement: Directly cross-references and restates the same-day F4/Model-B audit series' central finding (S2888-S2897): Sat's existence/role are corpus-present but its full operational semantics are not recovered, and Sat* remains a candidate construction rather than recovered corpus semantics.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not design what the corpus has not established. Where the corpus is insufficient, the correct result is NOT ESTABLISHED / RESEARCH REQUIRED, not an invented definition.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the closing methodological rule underlying the whole KnowledgeOS research programme: never design what the corpus has not established; an insufficient corpus should yield the honest classification NOT ESTABLISHED/RESEARCH REQUIRED rather than an invented definition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Delta_t = {r in R_t | Sat(K_t,r)=0}. Therefore Delta_t=empty is the KnowledgeOS notion of Zero Gap. Zero means that there are no unsatisfied requirements remaining within the defined requirement set and satisfaction semantics.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the core Zero-Gap definition as Delta_t=empty over the requirement set R_t and satisfaction predicate Sat(K_t,r), consistent with the F4/Model-B and kr-rep-reduction lines already covered in this batch.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 0 != empty in general. Numerical zero means a quantity has value zero. KnowledgeOS Zero is closer to: empty residual requirement set.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes numerical zero from KnowledgeOS Zero (an empty residual requirement set), a set-theoretic rather than quantitative notion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero is always relative to the defined requirement/inquiry scope. ... Zero Gap != Complete Knowledge. It means only: There is no remaining gap with respect to the requirements currently being evaluated.
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against conflating Zero Gap with Complete Knowledge or Complete Reality: satisfying all requirements in a scoped requirement set says nothing about knowledge outside that scope.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the same K_t can be Zero relative to R_t while simultaneously being Non-zero relative to a larger R'_t. This makes Zero inquiry- and contract-relative, rather than absolute.
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example showing the identical knowledge state K_t can simultaneously be Zero (empty gap) relative to a smaller requirement set and non-Zero relative to a larger superset, establishing Zero as inherently inquiry- and contract-relative rather than an absolute property of K_t.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If a transformation T removes irrelevant information while preserving everything needed to answer the inquiry, then the resulting representation may still have the same gap: Delta(T(K_t))=Delta(K_t). If the gap was already empty, then a valid inquiry-preserving transformation can maintain Delta(T(K_t))=empty. So Zero can function as a preserved semantic condition, not merely as a terminal numerical value.
b_rows_sample.statement: Connects Zero to the transformation/preservation theory: an inquiry-preserving transformation T maintains the gap Delta(T(K_t))=Delta(K_t), so an already-empty gap remains empty under valid transformations, framing Zero as a preserved semantic condition across the reduction/elimination research family.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero_{R,C}(K_t) iff Delta_{R,C}(K_t)=empty, where the subscript reminds us that Zero depends on the relevant requirements R and contract/context C. This is much stronger and safer than saying 'Zero means absence.' It means: There is no unresolved requirement in the specified epistemic task.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the strongest current formulation Zero_{R,C}(K_t) iff Delta_{R,C}(K_t)=empty, explicitly parameterized by requirements R and contract/context C, as a safer and stronger statement than an unparameterized 'Zero means absence.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: the full operational semantics of Sat(K_t,r) is not yet completely established, especially in the historical F4/Model-B work we just discussed. Therefore Delta_t=empty is theoretically meaningful, but we cannot yet claim that every real KnowledgeOS implementation can compute Zero correctly. Zero definition != Zero computation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Self-applies the same day's F4/Model-B audit finding (Sat(K_t,r)'s operational semantics not yet established) to the Zero-Gap concept itself, distinguishing Zero definition (theoretically meaningful) from Zero computation (not currently guaranteed correct in any real implementation).

a_aliases: The Knowledge State and Its Eight Primitives (book III.3)

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'K_t'

a_rows_sample.anchor: At least the following relations must be separated: = representation/structural equality; ≡ semantic equality; ≈ observational equivalence; ≅_I identity equivalence; ≅_P provenance-sensitive equivalence; ≅_H historical equivalence.
a_rows_sample.statement: The overloaded notation K1=K2 is decomposed into (at least) six distinct relations that must not be conflated: structural equality (=), semantic equality (equiv), observational equivalence (approx), identity equivalence (cong_I), provenance-sensitive equivalence (cong_P), and historical equivalence (cong_H); the corpus is said to explicitly record the first four distinctions and warn they are not interchangeable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Same proposition ⇏ Same evidence identity. ... two observations can concern the same proposition while remaining distinct evidence objects.
a_rows_sample.statement: Preserved historical result: identity is not equality — two evidence objects e1,e2 can both support the same proposition p (Supports(e1,p) and Supports(e2,p)) without e1=e2; this affects provenance, deduplication, replay, validation, audit and merge, and is attributed to an earlier corpus reconstruction rather than newly derived here.

a_rows_sample.anchor: x =_str y iff their representations are structurally identical. ... =_str ≠ semantic equality unless the representation has already been proven canonical.
a_rows_sample.statement: Structural equality x=_str y (representations structurally identical) is computationally convenient but is warned to not equal semantic equality unless the representation is already proven canonical — two structurally different representations can denote the same semantic state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: x ≡_sem y iff Semantics(x)=Semantics(y). ... Semantic equality is conceptually appropriate, but currently underdefined.
a_rows_sample.statement: Semantic equality x equiv_sem y is defined via a semantic interpretation function Sem:Representation->Meaning being equal on x and y, but is flagged as not computationally decidable while Sem itself remains formally undefined — conceptually appropriate but currently underdefined.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H1 ≈ H2 iff every permitted observation produces the same result: ∀O∈𝒪: O(H1)=O(H2). ... This is the relation already underlying Step 260's behavioral quotient.
a_rows_sample.statement: Observational equivalence for histories (H1 approx H2 iff every permitted observation O produces the same result) and for states (K1 approx K2 iff every permitted state observation agrees) is identified as the same relation already underlying Step 260's behavioral quotient; notably it does not require internal representations to be identical.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SameId(x,y) ... Identity tracks denotation; equality compares values. This formulation is a reconstruction, not yet a corpus-proven final definition.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identity (SameId(x,y)) answers whether two references denote the same domain object, independent of value equality: x=_str y can hold with SameId false (two separately created records with identical content but distinct observations), and SameId can hold while representations differ (the same domain object having evolved) — 'identity tracks denotation; equality compares values', explicitly flagged as a reconstruction, not a corpus-proven final definition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Historical equality asks: Are these states the same point or condition in an evolution history? ... Semantic equality ⇏ Historical equality.
a_rows_sample.statement: Historical equality asks whether two states are the same point in an evolution history, distinct from current semantic equality: K0 -Revise-> K1 can have K0 equiv_sem K1 (representation changed, semantics didn't) while K0 !=_H K1 (distinct historical states) — semantic equality does not imply historical equality; matters especially for Replay and audit.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance is semantically relevant: K1 ≢ K2. Provenance is metadata only: K1 ≡ K2. ... equality cannot be resolved until the theory determines which information is semantically essential. This is a key dependency for Step 265.
a_rows_sample.statement: Provenance equality is genuinely ambiguous: given K1={p,e1}, K2={p,e2} with e1!=e2 both supporting p, either provenance is semantically relevant (K1 not-equiv K2) or metadata only (K1 equiv K2); the earlier corpus is said to identify this ambiguity explicitly and conclude it cannot be resolved until the theory determines which information is semantically essential — flagged as a key dependency for Step 265 (provenance placement).

a_rows_sample.anchor: No universal equality hierarchy has yet been proven. ... Identity and Provenance equality are independent dimensions.
a_rows_sample.statement: A candidate implication chain (structural => semantic => observational equivalence) is proposed but explicitly not declared universally valid without further assumptions; identity and provenance equality are treated as independent dimensions from this chain; current position: no universal equality hierarchy has yet been proven.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Explicit assertion membership ≠ semantic entailment. ... a∈_exp K ... K⊨a ... Stored fact ≠ logically derived fact.
a_rows_sample.statement: Membership in an assertion-based state K is typed into explicit assertion membership (a in_exp K, a is literally one of K's stored assertions) versus semantic consequence (K models a, semantically entailed but not necessarily stored) — a proposed formal distinction (not yet a theorem) preventing the category error of treating a stored fact as identical to a logically derived one; flagged as essential for Step 262's assertion type.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Merge equality: semantic + identity + provenance dependent. Exact final semantics remain unresolved.
a_rows_sample.statement: Operation test — Merge: Merge(K1,K2) cannot be specified using structural equality alone, since a1=(p,e1) and a2=(p,e2) sharing proposition p could legitimately merge to {a1,a2} (kept separate) or to a single combined-evidence assertion depending on ontology; Merge equality is semantic+identity+provenance dependent, with exact final semantics unresolved.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Supersession requires identity/version distinction. ... collapsing them under semantic equality would destroy the very relation x2 ≻ x1.
a_rows_sample.statement: Operation test — Supersede: if Meaning(x1)=Meaning(x2) but Identity(x1)!=Identity(x2) and x2 supersedes x1, collapsing x1,x2 under semantic equality would destroy the supersession relation x2 succ x1 itself; supersession therefore requires an identity/version distinction, strongly suggesting semantic equality alone cannot serve as the sole equality relation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Replay requires historical identity/equality independent of current state equality. ... Replay(H1)=K and Replay(H2)=K yet H1 ≠_H H2.
a_rows_sample.statement: Operation test — Replay: two distinct histories H1,H2 (H1 !=_H H2) can replay to the same current state K (Replay(H1)=Replay(H2)=K); Replay is treated by the corpus as a history/audit operation rather than another state transformation, and requires historical identity/equality independent of current-state equality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | Operation | Structural equality | Semantic equality | Identity | Historical equality | Provenance | Current assessment | Merge...Supersede...Replay...Remove...Revise...Deduplicate...Validate
a_rows_sample.statement: The full operation/equality matrix across Merge, Supersede, Replay, Remove, Revise, Deduplicate, Validate rates each of structural/semantic/identity/historical/provenance equality as insufficient, required, relevant, potentially-required, or context-dependent per operation, with every row's overall status UNRESOLVED, NORMATIVE/DOMAIN-DEPENDENT (Deduplicate), or 'Assessment relation' (Validate); Remove requires identity for correct object targeting (must not remove a2 when removing a1 despite structural identity), Revise cannot use semantic equality as its sole target selector (must not implicitly revise x2 when revising x1 despite x1 equiv_sem x2), Deduplicate cannot be specified until its preservation policy is known (structural/semantic/identity/provenance criteria can each give different results), and Validate shows semantic state equality does not imply identical validation results because validation is a relation over (K,E) pairs, not K alone — reinforcing that not every operation is a state transformation T:K->K.

a_rows_sample.anchor: No single equality relation is adequate for all KnowledgeOS operations. ... KnowledgeOS requires a typed family of relations.
a_rows_sample.statement: Major correction to the kernel concept: rejects the implicit assumption 'KnowledgeOS needs one equality operator', replacing it with 'KnowledgeOS requires a typed family of relations' (=_str, equiv_sem, approx_obs, SameId, equiv_H, equiv_P) that may be connected by formally established implications but must not be conflated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K1 ≡_K K2 ⟺ ∀O∈𝒪_K: O(K1)=O(K2) ... 𝒪_K is not yet completely closed. Therefore this is a candidate formal definition, not a completed theorem.
a_rows_sample.statement: Candidate formal definition of Knowledge-State equality as purely observational/behavioral: K1 equiv_K K2 iff every permitted state observation O in the (not-yet-closed) set O_K agrees on K1 and K2; explicitly a candidate, not a completed theorem, because O_K is not yet closed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Equality → Congruence → Quotient → Minimality. This is the correct dependency direction.
a_rows_sample.statement: If K1 equiv_K K2 (no permitted observation distinguishes them) and all mandatory operations preserve that equivalence, equiv_K becomes the congruence relation needed for the minimal quotient K*=H/equiv (Step 260) — establishing the dependency direction Equality -> Congruence -> Quotient -> Minimality as correct.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the observation set is not fully closed; the operation registry is not fully closed; provenance placement remains unresolved; assertion semantics remain unresolved; temporal semantics remain unresolved; identity semantics remain unresolved. The governing prompt explicitly says that final kernel sele
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit refusal to overclaim equiv_K as final: six named open dependencies remain (observation-set closure, operation-registry closure, provenance placement, assertion semantics, temporal semantics, identity semantics); the governing prompt is cited as requiring final kernel selection to halt while equality remains ambiguous, and this gate is obeyed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: bounded contexts may legitimately require different relations: same assertion / same evidence / same domain identity / same version / same semantic meaning / same observable state ... PRIMARY KEY must therefore not automatically be interpreted as SemanticIdentity. ... content hash must not automatic
a_rows_sample.statement: DDD interpretation: rather than one generic 'Equality' concept used everywhere, different bounded contexts legitimately require different named relations (same assertion, same evidence, same domain identity, same version, same semantic meaning, same observable state); a database PRIMARY KEY must not automatically be interpreted as SemanticIdentity, and a content hash must not automatically become DomainIdentity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 𝔎=(K,=_str,≡_sem,≈_obs,SameId,≡_H,≡_P). The next question is not 'Which one is the equality?' It is 'Which relation is the appropriate congruence relation for each operation and which relation defines semantic equality of Knowledge States?'
a_rows_sample.statement: Mathematical reframing: KnowledgeOS's state carries a relational structure 𝔎=(K,=_str,equiv_sem,approx_obs,SameId,equiv_H,equiv_P) rather than a single equality; the research question shifts from 'which relation is THE equality' to 'which relation is the appropriate congruence for each operation, and which defines semantic equality of Knowledge States'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Proposition | A meaningful statement that can be true or false. | P=(Entity,Dimension,Value) ... Assertion | A proposition put forward as true, with a specific epistemic status... Knowledge | An assertion that satisfies the epistemic criteria for knowledge (justified true belief)
b_rows_sample.statement: Splits the Knowledge Atom into a three-level hierarchy Proposition subset-of Assertion subset-of Knowledge: Proposition=(E,D,V) is content without commitment; Assertion=(P,Sigma,Evidence,tau,Provenance) is a proposition put forward as true; Knowledge=(A,Justification,True) is a justified-true assertion; corrects the earlier Knowledge Atom to actually be an Assertion, not raw Knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Who determines True? KnowledgeOS observes, reconstructs, compares, challenges and guides. It generally cannot access Truth itself... Truth \neq Truth Assessment
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects making absolute Truth an internal primitive of Knowledge, since KnowledgeOS cannot access Truth directly; replaces the three-level model with four levels (Proposition -> Assertion -> Epistemically Accepted -> Reality/Omega), where 'Knowledge' becomes K=(A,Justification,TruthAssessment) rather than requiring literal correspondence to reality.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observation \rightarrow Candidate Proposition(s) ... because an observation can be ambiguous. ... 'Host responds on port 8081' -> P1/P2/P3
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects 'Observe -> Proposition' to 'Observation -> Candidate Proposition(s)', since one observation (e.g. a host responding on a port) can support multiple distinct, non-exclusive candidate propositions requiring Zero/Lord/Semantic-Reconstruction to disambiguate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t = \mathcal{E}_t(\mathcal{A}_t) ... Knowledge isn't necessarily one object. It is a state of knowledge over many propositions and assertions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes Knowledge from a single giant tuple to a Knowledge State K_t = E_t(A_t), an epistemic evaluation function over the set of currently available assertions A_t, foreshadowing K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,Observation_t,Zero_t,Lord_t,Evidence_t).

b_rows_sample.anchor: X_t \rightarrow O_t \rightarrow R_t \rightarrow A_t \rightarrow K_t
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the too-simple Reality->Observation->Knowledge pipeline into X_t (domain/reality) -> O_t (observation) -> R_t (semantic reconstruction/interpretation) -> A_t (assertion) -> K_t (knowledge state), with the critical point Observation ≠ Interpretation ≠ Assertion ≠ Knowledge, illustrated with the Bhīṣma example (seeing him = observation; 'Bhīṣma is a person' = interpretation; 'Bhīṣma is Arjuna's grandfather' = assertion; the same claim with provenance and epistemic qualification = knowledge).

b_rows_sample.anchor: P = \text{a semantically evaluable claim about entities, relationships, states or events}
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Proposition as a semantically evaluable claim (examples: IsOnBattlefield(Bhishma), GrandfatherOf(Bhishma,Arjuna), OpponentOf(Bhishma,Arjuna)), distinguished from Assertion: Proposition ≠ Assertion, and Assertion = Proposition + Epistemic Qualification + Provenance. Flagged as a distinction that 'should be frozen'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A_3 = Inference( A_1,A_2,\ldots, Rule, Assumptions, Provenance )
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends Infer(A_1,A_2,Rule)->A_3 to require every derived assertion to carry Rule, Assumptions, and Provenance so KnowledgeOS can explain 'why do you believe this?': every derived assertion traceable to source assertions + inference rule + assumptions + context, called essential for deterministic assurance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Document \neq Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the naive Documents->Chunk->Embedding->VectorDB->RAG->LLM architecture as 'not KnowledgeOS' because it bypasses the epistemic model: a document is not knowledge but an information-bearing source from which observations/assertions may be constructed — Document ≠ Knowledge, Document ≠ Evidence — illustrated by Document->Observation->Candidate Assertion->Evidence->Knowledge State.

b_rows_sample.anchor: LLM\ Output \neq Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Names three constitutional invariants for sources: (1) Source ≠ Knowledge (Document/API Response/Git Repository ≠ Knowledge); (2) LLM Output ≠ Knowledge — LLM Output -> Candidate Interpretation -> Epistemic Processing -> Knowledge; (3) Retrieval ≠ Knowledge Creation — Retrieve(Q) -> EvidenceCandidates -> Evaluate -> Knowledge. Overarching principle: 'Sources provide information; KnowledgeOS constructs governed knowledge from it. LLMs interpret; KnowledgeOS evaluates and governs. Retrieval supplies evidence candidates; it does not automatically create knowledge.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Interpret: Observation \times Context \rightarrow CandidateMeaning
b_rows_sample.statement: Interpret:Observation×Context->CandidateMeaning is where the structural parser, semantic parser, domain model, and LLM participate, worked through 'those with whom I have to fight' -> structural parsing -> semantic parsing -> candidate semantic structure -> candidate dimensions {Actor,Target,Action,Relationship,Obligation,Context} — explicitly 'not yet accepted knowledge'. CandidateAssertion=(Proposition,Sources,Interpretation,Context), e.g. 'Bhīṣma is Arjuna's grandfather' becomes a candidate proposition via Interpret->CandidateAssertions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assess: CandidateAssertion \times Evidence \times Rules \times Context \rightarrow EpistemicAssessment
b_rows_sample.statement: Assess:CandidateAssertion×Evidence×Rules×Context->EpistemicAssessment produces Σ_A=(Acquisition,Support,Uncertainty,Validity) per explicit policy, contrasting e.g. (Acquisition=Reported,Support=Moderate,Uncertainty=Moderate,Validity=Current) against (Acquisition=AI-Generated,Support=None,Uncertainty=High,Validity=Unknown) depending on what actually supports the proposition. CandidateAssertion --Assessment--> Assertion=(P,E,Σ,Π,τ,C,ID); K_{t+1}=δ(K_t,A). Full acquisition chain: X->Artifact->Observation->Interpretation->CandidateAssertion->Assessment->Assertion->K_{t+1}, stated to be 'already a computable architecture'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal P = \mathcal P_F \cup \mathcal P_N \cup \mathcal P_Q \cup \mathcal P_H \cup \mathcal P_I \ldots
b_rows_sample.statement: After ten tests, provisionally establishes 'Source Observation is computationally realizable' across documents, DB results, internet resources, human statements, LLM outputs, code, rules, ADRs, constitutions and instructions, preserving Source event ≠ Meaning ≠ Assertion. Surfaces two explicit unresolved theoretical points without deciding them: Open Point A — whether one Proposition abstraction P_F∪P_N∪P_Q∪P_H∪P_I∪... (factual/normative/definitional/instructional/question/hypothesis/interpretation) with an explicit semantic type suffices, versus needing genuinely distinct object types; Open Point B — whether the Observation model should stay unified (with acquisition method/type recording measurement vs statement vs database vs LLM etc.) rather than creating separate Observation concepts per source class.

b_rows_sample.anchor: one Proposition abstraction, with explicit semantic type.
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses two explicit architectural-fork questions to the domain authority rather than deciding unilaterally: Question 1 — should factual/normative/definitional/instructional/hypothetical/interrogative content be different TYPES of semantic proposition under one common Proposition abstraction (recommended: Yes — one Proposition abstraction with explicit semantic type, rather than unrelated objects)? Question 2 — should the observation model stay unified, with acquisition method/type recording whether it came from measurement/database/document/human/LLM/API/parser (recommended: Yes)? If both are agreed, proposes formally closing Observation and moving to 'Computational Closure 2 — Interpretation', testing whether parsing+ontology+rules+LLM+human interpretation can transform arbitrary source observations into candidate semantic structures 'without pretending that interpretation is truth'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Should KnowledgeOS be allowed to create an Assertion with an explicitly unresolved epistemic state
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses and then answers the pivotal admission-boundary design choice: should an Assertion require passing a minimum admission threshold, or may it hold an explicitly unresolved epistemic state (Unknown/Hypothesized/WeaklySupported)? Recommends and then (in a 'Domain Authority' voice) DECIDES the latter: Assertion ≠ Proven Truth. Rationale given for rejecting the threshold alternative: it would remove Zero's ability to detect gaps (no representation for Unknown/Hypothesized), remove Lord's ability to generate candidates (no place for them to reside), sever the Observation->Interpretation->Candidate->Assertion provenance chain, damage auditability (no record of 'what we considered but did not accept'), make the incomplete-question problem unsolvable, collapse the Unknown-vs-Absent distinction, and break the learning trajectory Hypothesized->WeaklySupported->StronglySupported.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Truth = "This is what we currently represent, with this degree of support, uncertainty, and validity."
b_rows_sample.statement: Re-runs all eight test cases (DB result -> StronglySupported; unstructured document -> WeaklySupported; internet page -> WeaklySupported with caveats; human statement -> Reported; LLM output -> Hypothesized; incomplete question -> no assertion created, Zero detects gap, clarification requested; conflicting sources -> both assertions remain in the Knowledge State with a detected Conflict; unknown value -> Assertion(Unknown)) through the new admission model. States the redefined meaning of 'the single source of truth': Truth = 'this is what we currently represent, with this degree of support, uncertainty, and validity', NOT 'this is factually correct in reality' — the formalization of Knowledge ≠ Reality. Six constitutional invariants listed: Assertion≠Proven Truth; admission does not require verification; Unknown is a valid epistemic state (not absence of an assertion); epistemic status can evolve; multiple epistemic states can coexist (Conflicting is valid); provenance is preserved. Declares the Epistemic Admission Boundary computationally closed and proceeds to 'Computational Closure 3 — The Knowledge State'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A \not\equiv Truth(P)
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Assertion A=(P,E,Σ,Π,τ,C,ID) with A≢Truth(P): A is 'KnowledgeOS's governed representation of P'. Two assertions of the identical proposition 'Nexus.version=3.69' can carry different epistemic states (Σ_A=(Observed,Strong,Low,Current) vs Σ_B=(Reported,Weak,High,Unknown)) and are 'not epistemically equivalent', giving Assertion⇏StrongEvidence, Assertion⇏Certainty, Assertion⇏Truth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Admit(P,\Pi_1) \neq Admit(P,\Pi_2)
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces admission policy Π_adm with Admit(P_c,E,C,Π_adm)->{Assertion|Reject|Defer|RequestMoreEvidence}; admission is purpose-dependent, Admit(P,Π_1)≠Admit(P,Π_2) (an exploration policy may allow Weak support, a production-migration policy may require Strong support) — connecting directly to the Ideal State theory: an assertion can exist with Σ_K=Weak while the Ideal State requires Σ_I=Strong, producing a discrepancy rather than an invalid assertion. Distinguishes Admission ('may this proposition exist as governed knowledge?', Candidate->Assertion) from Validation ('does this assertion satisfy a particular requirement?', Assertion×Constraint->ValidationResult): Admission ≠ Validation — an assertion can be admitted (e.g. during discovery) yet later FAIL a validation (e.g. a migration requiring verified version) WITHOUT being deleted; it 'remains useful historical knowledge'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assertion \in KnowledgeState ... KnowledgeState \neq SetOfAssertions
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects an earlier equation Assertion=Knowledge (too strong) to Assertion∈KnowledgeState while KnowledgeState≠SetOfAssertions: the Knowledge State is a structured object K_t=(Assertions,Evidence,Relationships,Conflicts,Gaps,Provenance,Context,History,Constraints), 'a structured state, not simply a bag of claims' — called 'an important DDD correction'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Evidence is not a property of a document.}
b_rows_sample.statement: Central correction: Evidence is not a property of a document but 'a relationship between an observation and a proposition under a context and an evaluation rule' — Evidence(O,P,C,R). Prevents the mistake 'the document says X, therefore X is evidence [for whatever P]'. Gives Evidence≠Observation, Evidence≠Source, Evidence≠Support, Evidence≠Truth as four fundamental distinctions, and shows the SAME observation can be evidence for one proposition and not another (Evidence(O,P_1)≠Evidence(O,P_2)) — 'evidence is therefore relational'. E=(O,P,R,C,T,Q,Π): observation, target proposition, evaluation rule, context, temporal applicability, quality assessment, provenance.

type_signature.domain: observation x proposition x context x rule

b_rows_sample.anchor: Conclusion = Inference(Premises,Rule,Context)
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects 'the evidence voted for 3.69' informal aggregation, requiring Conclusion=Inference(Premises,Rule,Context) via an explicit inference rule (worked example: APIResponse.version=3.69 plus rule 'APIResponse(source=NexusProduction)=>CurrentVersion(NexusProduction)' yields the conclusion). Distinguishes four conclusion kinds: Deductive (Γ⊨P, entailed), Inductive (evidence increases support for a generalization without entailing it), Abductive (select the best explanation among hypotheses {H_1,...,H_n} — 'extremely relevant to KnowledgeOS'), Computational/derived (e.g. a version-vs-required-version comparison rule). Formalizes Conclusion object C_n=(P,Γ,R,κ,Σ,Π,t) (proposition, premises/evidence, inference rule, inference method, epistemic assessment, provenance, derivation time), letting KnowledgeOS answer 'why did you reach this conclusion?' not just 'what did you conclude?'.

a_notations: K1 equiv_K K2 iff forall O in O_K: O(K1)=O(K2)

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 4 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: We have now reached the point where the reconstruction must become empirical. Conceptual Reconstruction→Evidence Extraction. The objective is to construct the actual graph G_actual=(V_actual,E_actual) from the existing KnowledgeOS/EKS material.
a_rows_sample.statement: States Step 116's shift Conceptual Reconstruction->Evidence Extraction, aiming to construct the actual graph G_actual=(V_actual,E_actual) from existing material.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 116.1 — The extraction rule ... No architectural relationship is accepted merely because it is desirable or conceptually logical. Claim_architecture⇒Evidence_implementation. If evidence is missing: Status=UNKNOWN. Not Status=FALSE.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the strict extraction rule Claim_architecture⇒Evidence_implementation, defaulting missing evidence to Status=UNKNOWN, never Status=FALSE.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 116.2 — Evidence hierarchy ... E0 No evidence, E1 Terminology, E2 Static implementation, E3 Behavioral evidence, E4 Verification evidence, E5 Runtime evidence, E6 Governance evidence. E0<E1<E2<E3<E4<E5<E6.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a seven-level evidence hierarchy E0 (no evidence) through E6 (governance evidence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 116.3 — Node extraction ... SemanticObject: ID, Type, Meaning, Representation, Owner, Lifecycle, Authority, Provenance, EvidenceLevel, Source.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the SemanticObject node-extraction schema with ten fields (ID/Type/Meaning/Representation/Owner/Lifecycle/Authority/Provenance/EvidenceLevel/Source).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 116.4 — Relationship extraction ... SemanticRelationship: Source, Target, Type, Direction, Evidence, Confidence, Status. Evidence_42-supports->Decision_17. The evidence must demonstrate both the relationship and its meaning.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the SemanticRelationship edge-extraction schema (Source/Target/Type/Direction/Evidence/Confidence/Status), requiring evidence for both relationship and meaning.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 116.5 — First graph layer: implementation graph ... G_I=(C,D,I) where C=components, D=dependencies, I=interfaces. This is the result of Step 111.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the implementation graph G_I=(C,D,I), the result of Step 111.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 116.6 — Second graph layer: data graph ... G_D=(Data,Relations). Entities, tables, documents, records, metadata, events, indexes, caches.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the data graph G_D=(Data,Relations) over entities/tables/documents/records/metadata/events/indexes/caches.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 116.7 — Third graph layer: semantic graph ... G_S=(Concepts,SemanticRelations). The important point is: G_I≠G_D≠G_S. They are related graphs.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the semantic graph G_S=(Concepts,SemanticRelations), stating G_I≠G_D≠G_S as related but distinct graphs.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 116.8 — Fourth graph layer: governance graph ... G_G=(Actors,Authorities,Decisions,Policies). This allows us to ask: Who is allowed to establish or change this knowledge?
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the governance graph G_G=(Actors,Authorities,Decisions,Policies), enabling the question of who may establish or change knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 116.9 — The combined model ... Governance Graph → Semantic Graph → Data Graph → Implementation Graph. This layered representation is more accurate than trying to force everything into one architecture diagram.
a_rows_sample.statement: Presents the four-layer stack (Governance->Semantic->Data->Implementation) as more accurate than forcing everything into one architecture diagram.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 116.10 — Experiment 1: component → semantic concept ... EvidenceRepository. What semantic concept does it represent? Evidence, Document, Artifact, Observation. We do not infer the answer from the class name alone. Result: requires semantic evidence
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 1: an EvidenceRepository component's actual semantic concept (Evidence/Document/Artifact/Observation) cannot be inferred from class name alone, requiring semantic evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 116.11 — Experiment 2: table → domain object ... knowledge_items table. If it contains content, embedding, source URL, chunk number, it may actually represent IndexedDocumentChunk. The database name alone is insufficient. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 2: a knowledge_items table containing content/embedding/source-URL/chunk-number fields may actually represent IndexedDocumentChunk, since the table name alone is insufficient; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 116.12 — Experiment 3: API → semantic capability ... POST /knowledge exists. This does not prove CreateKnowledgeObject. It may actually perform IndexDocument. We inspect the behavior. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 3: a POST /knowledge endpoint does not prove CreateKnowledgeObject; it may actually perform IndexDocument, requiring behavioral inspection; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 116.13 — The implementation-to-semantic mapping ... ImplementationElement→SemanticMeaning. Class↓Service↓Capability↓Domain concept. Each arrow requires evidence.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the implementation-to-semantic mapping chain Class->Service->Capability->Domain concept, each arrow requiring independent evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 116.14 — Semantic extraction from tests ... Tests are particularly valuable because they often reveal the intended semantics more precisely than implementation names. shouldRejectDecisionWithoutAuthority() is strong evidence for Decision-requires->Authority.
a_rows_sample.statement: States tests are particularly strong semantic evidence, illustrated by a test name directly encoding Decision-requires->Authority.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 116.15 — Experiment 4 ... Documentation says every decision must have an authority. No test exists. Expected: E1. If code enforces it: E3. If a test verifies it: E4. This gives us a precise confidence ladder.
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 4: a documented-only rule is E1, code-enforced is E3, test-verified is E4, forming a precise confidence ladder.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 116.16 — Event extraction ... DecisionApproved, EvidenceVerified, ActionExecuted, FindingCreated. An event name is evidence of a semantic concept only if its behavior supports that meaning.
a_rows_sample.statement: States event names (e.g. DecisionApproved, EvidenceVerified) are evidence of a semantic concept only if their actual behavior supports that meaning.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 116.17 — Experiment 5 ... Event KnowledgeUpdated. What changed? If it merely means search index updated, then it is not necessarily SemanticKnowledgeUpdated. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 5: a KnowledgeUpdated event meaning only 'search index updated' is not necessarily SemanticKnowledgeUpdated; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 116.18 — Workflow extraction ... Draft→Review→Approve→Publish. This suggests lifecycle semantics. But we must determine: is this a technical publishing workflow or an authoritative governance workflow?
a_rows_sample.statement: States workflow extraction (e.g. Draft->Review->Approve->Publish) must distinguish technical publishing workflow from authoritative governance workflow.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 116.19 — Experiment 6 ... Workflow contains Review→Publish. No authority check exists. Expected: technical lifecycle established, governance lifecycle unproven. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 6: a Review->Publish transition with no authority check establishes only technical, not governance, lifecycle; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We now test the semantic-core hypothesis against the actual KnowledgeOS implementation. Which of these concepts are actually first-class concepts in the current system? Only evidence of actual implementation counts as implementation evidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: States Step 114's strict test: only actual-implementation evidence counts for judging whether the Step 113 candidate concepts are first-class in the current system.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 114.1 — The evidence test ... T(C)=(Code,Schema,API,Tests,Runtime,Owner,Relations). S0 Terminology only, S1 Represented, S2 Behavioral, S3 Verified, S4 Operational, S5 Governed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines T(C)=(Code,Schema,API,Tests,Runtime,Owner,Relations) as the seven-dimension per-concept evidence test, classified into six grades S0-S5.

type_signature.codomain: Code x Schema x API x Tests x Runtime x Owner x Relations

b_rows_sample.anchor: 114.2 — The important distinction ... A concept can therefore be S1 without being S5. For example, a Decision table may exist without the system having a genuine decision-governance model.
b_rows_sample.statement: States S1 (represented) does not imply S5 (governed), illustrated by a Decision table existing without genuine decision-governance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 114.3 — Evidence concept ... Code: is there an explicit evidence representation? Schema: can evidence be persisted independently? API: created/retrieved? Tests: invariants tested? Runtime: objects generated? Ownership: who decides what qualifies as evidence? Relations: can evidence support a claim,
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists the seven concrete evidentiary questions for testing whether Evidence is a first-class concept.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 114.4 — Evidence verdict rule ... Only if several of these dimensions align can we say Evidence=FirstClassSemanticConcept. Otherwise Evidence=TechnicalMetadata/Artifact.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the Evidence verdict rule: several aligned dimensions yield Evidence=FirstClassSemanticConcept, otherwise Evidence=TechnicalMetadata/Artifact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 114.5 — Observation ... Potential sources Runtime, CI, Git, Agent, Human. The critical question is whether the system distinguishes ObservedFact from Interpretation.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the critical Observation test is whether the system distinguishes ObservedFact from Interpretation, across five potential sources.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 114.6 — Experiment 1 ... System records 'test failed.' Is this an observation? Potentially. But if it stores only status=FAILED without source, time or context, its evidentiary value is limited. Expected: Observation=Partial unless richer semantics exist. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 1: a bare status=FAILED value without source/time/context yields Observation=Partial; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 114.7 — Claim ... A claim should be distinguishable from raw document, observation, recommendation, decision. Claim: Component A violates Rule B. This claim can then be supported by Evidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: States a Claim must be distinguishable from raw document/observation/recommendation/decision, illustrated by a component-violates-rule claim supportable by evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 114.8 — Experiment 2 ... An AI agent produces 'The implementation violates the architecture.' No claim object exists. Expected: this is an assertion produced by the agent, not necessarily a first-class KnowledgeOS claim. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 2: an AI agent's assertion without a backing claim object is merely an agent assertion, not a first-class KnowledgeOS claim; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 114.9 — Decision ... We need to determine whether the implementation distinguishes Recommendation from Decision. This is one of the most important semantic boundaries.
b_rows_sample.statement: States distinguishing Recommendation from Decision as one of the most important semantic boundaries to test for.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 114.10 — Experiment 3 ... A generated architecture recommendation is stored in the same table as an approved architecture decision. No type, authority or lifecycle distinguishes them. Expected: DecisionSemantics=Weak. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 3: a recommendation and an approved decision sharing one undifferentiated table with no type/authority/lifecycle distinction yields DecisionSemantics=Weak; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 114.11 — Authority ... A system may have user_id and role without implementing decision authority. We need Authority→Scope→Permission→DecisionType.
b_rows_sample.statement: States Authority is harder to establish than role, requiring Authority->Scope->Permission->DecisionType beyond a bare user_id/role pair.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 114.12 — Experiment 4 ... User has ROLE_ARCHITECT but the system does not restrict which decisions that user may make. Expected: role exists, authority semantics are not established. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 4: a ROLE_ARCHITECT role without decision-type restriction shows role exists but authority semantics do not; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 114.13 — Action ... we ask whether the system can reconstruct Who+What+Why+When+AgainstWhat+UnderWhichAuthority. This is particularly important for AI agents.
b_rows_sample.statement: States Action testing requires reconstructing Who+What+Why+When+AgainstWhat+UnderWhichAuthority, particularly important for AI agents.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 114.14 — Experiment 5 ... Session logs show 'file changed' but not agent identity, command, intent, authorization. Expected: ActionProvenance=Partial. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 5: session logs recording only 'file changed' without identity/command/intent/authorization yield ActionProvenance=Partial; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 114.15 — Provenance ... This may be the most important cross-cutting semantic concept. Provenance(X)=Source+Actor+Time+Transformation+Context. The actual implementation may support only some of these.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Provenance(X)=Source+Actor+Time+Transformation+Context, called possibly the most important cross-cutting semantic concept.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 114.16 — Experiment 6 ... Document has source_url. Expected: source attribution exists, but this does not establish complete provenance. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 6: a source_url field establishes partial source attribution, short of complete provenance; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 114.17 — Temporal validity ... We need to distinguish CreatedAt from ValidFrom. These are not the same. A decision can be created today but become effective next month.
b_rows_sample.statement: States CreatedAt≠ValidFrom, illustrated by a decision created today but becoming effective next month.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 114.18 — Experiment 7 ... Object contains created_at but no effective/supersession semantics. Expected: creation timestamp exists, temporal validity remains unproven. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 7: an object with only created_at and no effective/supersession fields leaves temporal validity unproven; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 114.19 — Semantic relationship test ... The concepts themselves are not enough. We need relationships. Evidence-supports->Claim. Claim-informs->Decision. Decision-authorizes->Action.
b_rows_sample.statement: States concept-level evidence is insufficient; relationships (Evidence-supports->Claim, Claim-informs->Decision, Decision-authorizes->Action) must also be tested.
