a_rows_sample.anchor: We now consolidate the previous experiments. The objective is to identify the smallest set of invariants whose violation would fundamentally change the nature of KnowledgeOS. Provenance+Authority+EpistemicStatus+TemporalValidity+DeterministicVerification+Traceability+Feedback.
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames Step 120's objective: identifying the smallest invariant set whose violation would fundamentally change KnowledgeOS, starting from a seven-part candidate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.1 — What makes an invariant constitutional? A constitutional invariant says: if this property is violated, the system no longer has the intended semantic character. ConstitutionalInvariant≠CodingConvention. 'Use PostgreSQL' is not necessarily constitutional. 'Authoritative knowledge must have id
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines ConstitutionalInvariant≠CodingConvention: a constitutional invariant's violation changes the system's intended semantic character, illustrated by contrasting a technology preference with a provenance requirement.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.2 — Invariant K1: Provenance ... Every authoritative knowledge object MUST have provenance. Provenance should answer where did it originate, when, through which process, who/what produced it, from which source material.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes candidate invariant K1: every authoritative knowledge object must have provenance answering five questions (origin/when/process/producer/source material).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.3 — Why provenance is constitutional ... Without provenance, Knowledge becomes indistinguishable from GeneratedText. That destroys the ability to answer: Why should I trust this?
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues without provenance, Knowledge becomes indistinguishable from GeneratedText, destroying trust justification.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.4 — Experiment K1.1 ... KnowledgeOS contains 'The architecture requires rootless containers.' No source, author, decision, timestamp or provenance exists. Can the system establish that it is authoritative? No. Verdict: K1 VIOLATED
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment K1.1: a sourceless/authorless/timestampless architecture statement cannot be established as authoritative; verdict K1 VIOLATED.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.5 — Provenance does not equal source URL ... SourceURL does not tell us WhoApproved or WhenDidItBecomeValid. Source≠CompleteProvenance.
a_rows_sample.statement: States Source≠CompleteProvenance: a URL alone does not establish approval or validity onset.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.6 — Invariant K2: Authority ... Every authoritative governance change MUST have identifiable authority. Decision→Authority.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes candidate invariant K2: every authoritative governance change must have identifiable authority (Decision->Authority).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.7 — Why authority is constitutional ... Without authority, Recommendation can silently become Decision. And AgentOutput can silently become OrganizationalTruth. That is unacceptable.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues without authority, Recommendation can silently become Decision and AgentOutput can silently become OrganizationalTruth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.8 — Experiment K2.1 ... Agent generates 'Architecture standard changed to X.' No authorized decision exists. Expected: Status=Proposed. Not Status=Authoritative. Verdict: K2 VIOLATION if promoted
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment K2.1: an unauthorized agent-declared standard change must remain Status=Proposed; K2 VIOLATION if promoted to Authoritative.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.9 — Authority is not identity ... Actor≠Authority. Credential≠Authority. Role≠Authority unless the governance model explicitly establishes the mapping.
a_rows_sample.statement: States Actor≠Authority, Credential≠Authority, Role≠Authority unless the governance model explicitly maps them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.10 — Invariant K3: Epistemic status ... KnowledgeOS MUST distinguish observed, verified, inferred, proposed and authoritative information. This is perhaps the most important AI-specific invariant.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes candidate invariant K3, called perhaps the most important AI-specific invariant: distinguishing observed/verified/inferred/proposed/authoritative information.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.11 — Why epistemic status matters ... 'The service probably owns this database' versus 'The Architecture Board decided that this service owns this database.' The textual similarity may be high. Their epistemic status is radically different.
a_rows_sample.statement: Illustrates why epistemic status matters via a textually-similar but epistemically-radically-different sentence pair.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.12 — Experiment K3.1 ... LLM generates Inference(X). System stores it identically to AuthoritativeDecision(X). Expected: K3 VIOLATION
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment K3.1: storing an LLM inference identically to an authoritative decision is K3 VIOLATION.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.13 — Candidate epistemic states ... Observed, Imported, Asserted, Inferred, Proposed, Verified, Approved, Superseded. But we should only implement states that have real semantic value.
a_rows_sample.statement: Lists an eight-value candidate epistemic vocabulary, cautioning only states with real semantic value should be implemented.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.14 — Invariant K4: Temporal validity ... Authoritative knowledge MUST have determinable temporal validity. At minimum Current versus Superseded.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes candidate invariant K4: authoritative knowledge must have determinable temporal validity, at minimum Current vs Superseded.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.15 — Why time is constitutional ... An architecture decision from 2024 may not represent the current architecture in 2026. Therefore HistoricalTruth≠CurrentTruth.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues HistoricalTruth≠CurrentTruth, illustrated by a 2024 decision potentially not representing 2026's current architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.16 — Experiment K4.1 ... Two decisions exist: D1 use architecture A, D2 use architecture B. No relationship identifies which supersedes which. Expected: agent cannot safely determine current architecture. Verdict: K4 VIOLATION
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment K4.1: two competing, unlinked decisions leave an agent unable to safely determine current architecture; verdict K4 VIOLATION.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.17 — Creation time versus validity ... We must explicitly distinguish CreatedAt from ValidFrom. And potentially ValidUntil.
a_rows_sample.statement: States CreatedAt must be distinguished from ValidFrom (and potentially ValidUntil).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.18 — Experiment K4.2 ... Decision created 2026-08-01 but effective 2026-09-01. If the system only knows created_at, it cannot correctly answer is this decision currently effective. Verdict: K4 PARTIAL
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment K4.2: a decision created before its effective date cannot be correctly evaluated by a created_at-only system; verdict K4 PARTIAL.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 120.19 — Invariant K5: Deterministic verification ... Where a claim is deterministically testable, authoritative assurance MUST be based on reproducible verification evidence. This does not eliminate human judgment. It prevents LLMConfidence from becoming Verification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes candidate invariant K5: deterministically testable claims must be assured via reproducible evidence, preventing LLMConfidence from becoming Verification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Research Exploration -> Invariant Consolidation -> Constitutional Invariant Map (P4) -> Evidence Validation (P5) -> Kernel Definition
b_rows_sample.statement: HPA transition statement: the research/exploration phase has reached sufficient maturity; the next step is a controlled transition (not another philosophical investigation): Research Exploration -> Invariant Consolidation -> Constitutional Invariant Map (P4) -> Evidence Validation (P5) -> Kernel Definition. The main danger named is 'research drift': continuing to collect ideas instead of freezing what has been extracted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rule 1 -- No new research concepts ... Rule 2 -- Preserve identity discipline ... Rule 3 -- Separate the three layers
b_rows_sample.statement: Three Mandatory Discipline Rules for P4: (1) No new research concepts -- anything not already extracted is marked Candidate, never admitted as established; the map consolidates, it does not collect. (2) Preserve identity discipline -- Similarity != Identity; every invariant is validated by its ID, evidence lineage, original registration, and validation state; no look-alike row is accepted on resemblance. (3) Separate the three layers -- Kernel Invariant (constitutional, PRESERVE), Reasoning Mechanism (operational, GOVERN -- engines: LLM, TMS, AGM, logic solver), Representation (Vani/expression layer); a row must not blur its layer.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Required Output Structure (7 parts)
b_rows_sample.statement: The P4 deliverable's required 7-part structure: (1) Character Definition; (2) What KnowledgeOS Is NOT (5 non-identities); (3) Constitutional Invariant Map (7-column schema: Invariant | Dimensions | Forbidden Collapse | Evidence | Strength | Validation Target | Notes, across families Identity/Evidence/Authority/Transformation/Temporal/Reasoning/Contradiction/Agent); (4) Kernel vs Reasoning Engine Boundary; (5) Mathematical Lens Consolidation; (6) KnowledgeOS vs LLM comparison; (7) Final Kernel Definition ('KnowledgeOS is a ___ that ___ while protecting ___').

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not make KnowledgeOS bigger. Make it clearer.
b_rows_sample.statement: Governing instruction (HPA, verbatim): 'Do not make KnowledgeOS bigger. Make it clearer. The objective is to identify the smallest set of constitutional rules that allow trustworthy knowledge evolution.' Final Gate: 'Has research ended?' -- Expected answer: Yes. Next phase: P4 -> P5 (Evidence Validation / domain-independence) -> Kernel Definition.

b_rows_sample.statement: Primary Objective, stated as the definition of the Constitutional Invariant Map's purpose: it must define what must remain protected so that knowledge can evolve, transform, reason, and support truth discovery without losing identity, provenance, or epistemic integrity.

explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'knowledgeos-architecture-constitution-v01' POSSIBLY relates to 'kos-constitutional-invariant-map' (batch B0025). Note: REUSE NOTE (recorded in B0025, not first proposed here): this label was first proposed in the immediately preceding batch B0024 (Step 120's frozen C1-C7 constitution) but had not yet been merged into the master 11-OBJECT-INDEX.jsonl snapshot given to this batch. B0025 (Steps 122-124, 130, 136, 141) extensively references and extends this same object (bypass-test matrix, graph integrity invariants, runtime invariants) -- re-registering it here purely so the batch's own unregistered-label self-check passes; the canonical definition and note remain B0024's.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Claim → Locate → Inspect → Trace → Test → Observe → Classify → Report
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines EEP = {E1..E8}: an eight-stage mandatory pipeline (Claim, Locate, Inspect, Trace, Test, Observe, Classify, Report) that an agent must explicitly state it performed (not necessarily at equal depth) before making an architectural claim; the governing principle is 'an agent must prove an architectural claim from evidence; it must not prove it from plausibility.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Structural / Behavioral / Governance / Temporal / Assurance / Operational
a_rows_sample.statement: E1 Claim requires a precise, falsifiable proposition (contrasts 'Understand KnowledgeOS' [bad] with a typed claim like 'AuthoritativeDecision -> Provenance' [good]) and distinguishes six claim types: Structural (component depends on component), Behavioral (creating an authoritative object requires provenance), Governance (only an authorized actor can approve), Temporal (superseded decisions excluded from current knowledge), Assurance (rule X deterministically verified), Operational (runtime state fed back into KnowledgeOS).

a_rows_sample.anchor: NotFound(Location) ≠ Absent(System)
a_rows_sample.statement: E2 Locate names search targets (README, docs/, ADR/, architecture/, src/, tests/, schemas/, migrations/, config/, CI/CD, hooks/, agents/, runtime configuration) and states the negative-evidence rule: finding nothing in one location does not prove system-wide absence; the agent must report 'no evidence found in the inspected locations' rather than 'the capability does not exist.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: DeclaredArchitecture ... ImplementedArchitecture ... VerifiedBehavior
a_rows_sample.statement: E3 Inspect distinguishes evidence types by artifact kind: documentation establishes DeclaredArchitecture, source code establishes ImplementedArchitecture, tests establish VerifiedBehavior — these are different evidence types and must not be conflated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The objective is not simply finding matching names. It is establishing semantic linkage.
a_rows_sample.statement: E4 Trace: given a claim Decision -> Implementation, the agent follows the chain Decision -> ADR/record -> change request -> PR -> commit -> artifact -> deployment, aiming at semantic linkage rather than textual name-matching; defines traceability-strength scale T0 (no link) < T1 (textual similarity) < T2 (explicit reference) < T3 (machine-readable identifier) < T4 (verified causal/implementation relationship), e.g. an ADR-042 identifier appearing in a commit is stronger evidence than shared wording.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Static / Unit / Integration / Architecture / Deployment / Runtime
a_rows_sample.statement: E5 Test: for a behavioral claim (e.g. 'authoritative knowledge cannot be created without provenance'), execute a concrete test (create(authoritative=true, provenance=null) expecting Reject) and classify it on a six-level test hierarchy (Static, Unit, Integration, Architecture, Deployment, Runtime) since the test type affects what the result actually proves.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Static code is not enough for operational claims.
a_rows_sample.statement: E6 Observe: operational claims (e.g. 'Nexus runs rootless') require inspecting actual runtime/deployment/logs/metrics/events, not merely a static configuration file such as a Podman config.

a_rows_sample.anchor: FACT | INFERENCE | TARGET | GAP
a_rows_sample.statement: E7 Classify: every finding receives one of four epistemic classifications — FACT (directly evidenced, e.g. a Containerfile using a specified base image, via E2/E3), INFERENCE (a reasoned interpretation that must not be presented as established fact without stronger evidence, e.g. 'this repo appears to implement the Evidence bounded context'), TARGET (intended future architecture unless implementation proves otherwise, e.g. 'KnowledgeOS should provide closed-loop governance'), GAP (Expected ≠ Observed, e.g. architecture requires provenance but authoritative records can currently be created without it).

a_rows_sample.anchor: CLAIM / FACTS / EVIDENCE / INFERENCE / VERIFICATION / GAP / TARGET / CONFIDENCE
a_rows_sample.statement: E8 Report: the final report must never collapse evidence into one narrative; it uses a fixed section format (Claim, Facts, Evidence, Inference, Verification, Gap, Target, Confidence) 'to prevent architectural contamination,' illustrated with a worked standard-agent-output example ending in STATUS: CONFORMANT / CONFIDENCE: HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C0=Unknown, C1=Weak, C2=Moderate, C3=Strong, C4=Verified
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a five-level ordinal confidence scale (C0 Unknown .. C4 Verified) as superior to arbitrary percentages; argues LLMConfidence ≠ EvidenceConfidence because an LLM stating '95% confident' does not establish a quantitative probability, whereas evidence-derived confidence must derive from evidence quality; also distinguishes EvidenceStrength from Confidence (strong evidence can still leave interpretive ambiguity).

a_rows_sample.anchor: If evidence is insufficient, the agent MUST preserve UNKNOWN.
a_rows_sample.statement: States an agent stopping rule / anti-hallucination rule: when evidence is insufficient the agent must preserve UNKNOWN rather than fill the gap from general knowledge; explicitly frames stopping with disclosed uncertainty (e.g. 'implementation is supported, enforcement is unverified') as a successful investigation, not a failure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Mode A — Architecture reconstruction ... Mode E — Knowledge reconstruction
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines five repository investigation modes with distinct evidence focus — A Architecture reconstruction (Structure+Dependencies), B Governance verification (Authority+Decision+Process), C Assurance verification (Rule+Test+Evidence), D Runtime verification (Deployment+Observation), E Knowledge reconstruction (Meaning+Provenance+Validity) — and requires the agent to select the mode before searching, and to follow a Broad->Narrow->Exact->Trace search strategy (e.g. 'provenance' -> 'source_id' -> 'createKnowledge' -> tests -> runtime).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Can the invariant be bypassed?
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns against name-based conclusions (e.g. a class named ProvenanceService does not itself prove provenance is enforced — the agent must ask who calls it, when, what happens on failure, whether the result is persisted, and whether it can be bypassed); defines the enforcement test 'can the invariant be bypassed? If yes, Enforcement<Strong,' illustrated by Experiment 2 where a ProvenanceService exists but developers can insert DB records without provenance, yielding Declared=Yes, Enforced=No, verdict PARTIAL.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C1 ... provenance required ... direct persistence | C7 ... feedback path exists ... finding dead-end
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends the Step 120 C1-C7 constitution with a bypass-question and bypass-test matrix per invariant: C1 can authoritative knowledge bypass provenance via direct persistence; C2 can approval bypass authority via unauthorized promotion; C3 can inference be promoted to authority without validation; C4 can stale knowledge appear current via stale retrieval; C5 can verification results be fabricated/irreproducible via inconsistent rerun; C6 can governed actions occur without traceability via untracked action; C7 can findings disappear without governance closure via finding dead-end — presented as a practical assurance test suite.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1. State the claim. ... 10. Never promote inference to authority.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a ten-item 'agent execution contract' every KnowledgeOS-aware engineering agent must follow: state the claim; identify evidence sources; inspect implementation; trace relationships; execute relevant tests where possible; inspect runtime where required; separate fact from inference; report uncertainty; identify gaps; never promote inference to authority.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SameAuthority / SameEvidenceRules / SameConstitution / SameEpistemicDiscipline
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes that Claude and Codex should share the Evidence Execution Protocol as a common agent-instruction layer: the important symmetry is not identical configuration but SameAuthority, SameEvidenceRules, SameConstitution, SameEpistemicDiscipline, while Claude and Codex harnesses remain operationally different — diagrammed as KnowledgeOS -> Evidence Protocol -> {Claude Harness, Codex Harness} -> Same Truth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This is a pointer/behavior contract, not a duplicate knowledge repository.
a_rows_sample.statement: Sketches a minimal KnowledgeOS-aware AGENTS.md operating contract (consult authoritative sources, verify current validity, preserve provenance, distinguish fact from inference, use deterministic checks where available, record material engineering actions against authorization, never treat local agent memory as authoritative) and states that .claude/ and .codex/ should likewise hold tools/hooks/workflow/session-behavior/verification-procedures/pointers-to-KnowledgeOS but must not become the enterprise architecture authority themselves — the goal is OperationalSymmetry without KnowledgeDuplication.

a_rows_sample.anchor: # Evidence Execution Report ... Open questions: ...
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a standard 'Evidence Execution Report' template with fields Claim, Scope, Evidence inspected, Implementation, Tests executed, Runtime observations, FACT, INFERENCE, TARGET, GAP, Conformance, Confidence, Open questions, as the mandatory end-of-investigation deliverable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AgentAssuranceScore = f(EvidenceCompleteness, Traceability, Verification, EpistemicDiscipline)
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes judging an agent by EvidenceQuality rather than AnswerQuality: an articulate but unsupported answer should score poorly, a cautious evidence-backed answer highly; defines AgentAssuranceScore = f(EvidenceCompleteness, Traceability, Verification, EpistemicDiscipline), explicitly preferable to measuring only LLMAnswerSimilarity; further defines Completeness = VerifiedLinks/RequiredLinks for a claim needing n evidence links, notes critical missing links should carry higher weight (WeightedCompleteness preferable to plain Completeness), and gives Authority as an example of a critical link whose absence should not be masked by ten present technical links.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Claim ├── supportedBy → Evidence ... └── classifiedAs → Status
a_rows_sample.statement: Observes that an agent's own investigation becomes graph data (Claim -supportedBy-> Evidence, -verifiedBy-> Test, -observedAt-> Runtime, -interpretedAs-> Finding, -classifiedAs-> Status), so the process of understanding the architecture itself becomes part of KnowledgeOS knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence before Architecture Claims
b_rows_sample.statement: States the governing rule for this phase, 'Evidence before Architecture Claims,' and defines five current-state categories (Existing/Partial/Missing/Misaligned/Unknown) plus a five-question reconstruction model per capability (what should exist=target, what actually exists=current, what proves it=evidence, does it conform=assessment, what must happen next=delta), emphasizing an architecture statement without evidence is only a hypothesis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: | Capability | Target | Current | Evidence | Status |
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents a deliberately conservative Current->Target matrix across thirteen capabilities (Knowledge model, Provenance, Governance, Evidence, Assurance, Agent integration, Agent memory, Registry, Hooks, Context construction, Authorization, Runtime evidence, Assurance graph), most marked Unknown/Partial pending reconstruction, and lists known existing mechanisms (AI Engineering Platform, KnowledgeOS/EKS, governance mechanisms, registry, hooks, .claude/, .codex/, .claude/memory/, AGENTS.md, deterministic assurance, session/change logging) — the current system is 'not a blank-slate knowledge platform.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Registry ≠ AssuranceGraph. Memory ≠ AuthoritativeKnowledge. Hook ≠ Governance. Check ≠ CompleteAssuranceModel.
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns that the presence of mechanisms does not mean the target architecture is fully implemented — a registry is not automatically an assurance graph, memory is not automatically authoritative knowledge, a hook is not automatically governance, a check is not automatically a complete assurance model — the actual semantics must be established.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Does .claude/ own knowledge, or does it point to knowledge?
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines per-component reconstruction targets and their critical tests: repository topology (do application/domain/infrastructure/governance/knowledge/evidence/assurance/agents directories exist — must not be assumed); package boundary tests (Domain->Infrastructure=FAIL if direct/inappropriate; Agent->Domain potentially valid through application contracts; Agent->Database needs scrutiny; Governance->Agent implementation generally suspicious; Assurance->External systems expected through ports/adapters); .claude/ and .codex/ each tested by 'does it own knowledge, or point to knowledge?' with the desired symmetry (.claude/ and .codex/ hold agent behavior/integration, KnowledgeOS holds governed engineering knowledge); AGENTS.md tested against AGENTS.md=Pointer+OperatingContract (not =EnterpriseKnowledgeBase); .claude/memory/ tested by 'what epistemic status does memory have?' (potentially valid: session hints/workflow state/preferences/temporary context/pointers; potentially problematic: authoritative architecture/binding governance decisions/enterprise policies/unverified claims).

b_rows_sample.anchor: TechnicalRegistry or KnowledgeRegistry or something broader.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the registry reconstruction target (what exactly is registered — repositories/agents/knowledge objects/architecture artifacts/services/policies/tools/checks — determining whether it is a TechnicalRegistry, KnowledgeRegistry, or broader) and the hook reconstruction target (each hook classified by Trigger->Action->Evidence, e.g. Git event->Hook->Validation->Evidence vs. Agent event->Hook->Session logging; a blocking hook is not automatically governance — Hook->Policy traceability is required to know which policy authorizes the block).

b_rows_sample.anchor: What is checked? Where are the rules defined? Who owns the rules? ... Are failures connected to governance?
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the deterministic-assurance reconstruction target via eight questions (what is checked, where rules are defined, who owns them, how results are recorded, whether versioned, whether evidence preserved, reproducibility, connection to governance), distinguishing CollectionOfChecks from AssuranceSystem; provisionally classifies current assurance maturity as AssuranceCapability=Existing/Partial rather than CompleteAssuranceContext, with semantic integration as the missing question; requires the full chain Rule->Checker->Execution->Result->Evidence->Finding as strong evidence of an assurance architecture (a bare 'a checker exists' is weak evidence).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Existence, SemanticMaturity, Enforcement, Traceability
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a four-dimension capability assessment framework (Existence, SemanticMaturity, Enforcement, Traceability) with a worked example table (Agent hooks, Registry, Memory, Assurance checks, Governance decisions, Evidence model, Assurance graph rows), most cells marked '?' pending reconstruction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Runtime/Code > Executable Configuration > Tests/Checks > Structured Data > Architecture Documents > Narrative Statements.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an evidence-strength hierarchy for current-state claims (documents remain important, but the stronger the claim, the stronger the required evidence should be).

b_rows_sample.anchor: FACT / DERIVED / HYPOTHESIS / TARGET
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a four-way architecture-claim classification (FACT: directly observed; DERIVED: logically derived from observed facts; HYPOTHESIS: architectural interpretation requiring validation; TARGET: desired future architecture), worked example — FACT '.claude/ contains a memory directory,' DERIVED 'Claude has persistent local memory mechanisms,' HYPOTHESIS 'the memory mechanism is intended as non-authoritative context,' TARGET 'all authoritative engineering knowledge should resolve through KnowledgeOS' — preventing accidental blending of current and target architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KEEP, STRENGTHEN, REFACTOR, INTRODUCE, REMOVE, REPLACE, INVESTIGATE
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines seven current-to-target delta categories; specifically warns that uncertainty (e.g. 'the registry might already provide evidence lineage') should be marked INVESTIGATE, not prematurely INTRODUCE EvidenceSystem — we should not turn uncertainty into architecture work prematurely.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Repository → Modules/Packages → Data Model → APIs → Agent Harnesses → Hooks → Registry → Assurance → Governance → Integrations → Runtime → Current Architecture → Target Delta
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the safest architecture-reconstruction sequence (repository first, target delta last) to prevent designing features that already exist, reframing the central question from 'what should KnowledgeOS be' to 'how much of the target is already present, under what names, with what guarantees' — the actual archaeology problem; gives an expected-output reconstruction-matrix template (target capability / existing implementation / evidence / architectural assessment / delta).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Never introduce a target component merely because its conceptual counterpart has not yet been found.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the architecture-reconstruction rule: first determine whether a component exists under another name before introducing it as new, particularly important because the platform evolved incrementally.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Design Mode → Evidence Mode
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 132 verdict: the reconstruction formally switches from Design Mode to Evidence Mode (Current->Evidence->Assessment->Delta->Target), since the target architecture is now sufficiently developed to serve as a reference model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: WHAT EXISTS TODAY vs WHAT THE TARGET ARCHITECTURE REQUIRES.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reopens Step 132 (Current-State Reconstruction) here, listing a fifteen-item inspection scope (repository/package structure, .claude/, .codex/, AGENTS.md, registry, governance artifacts, hooks, deterministic assurance, memory, persistence, APIs, integration boundaries, existing context/knowledge model, evidence model, current deployment) producing a Current->Target Architecture Delta Matrix classified Already Exists/Partially Exists/Missing/Architecturally Wrong/Unknown — this preview is elaborated in full detail in the separately-processed Step 132 file (S1031).

b_rows_sample.anchor: CURRENT ≠ TARGET. FACT/DERIVED/HYPOTHESIS/TARGET/UNKNOWN.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the CURRENT/TARGET/DELTA/CONFIDENCE reconstruction format and the five-way claim classification, requiring FACT->DERIVED chains while HYPOTHESIS cannot become CURRENT without evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AgentRuntimeContext ⊃ RepositoryArtifacts — desirable for reproducible agent behavior, not inherently wrong.
b_rows_sample.statement: Current-state observation 1: the agent integration layer is already repository-local, which is desirable for reproducibility; the architectural question is what those artifacts are allowed to own, not whether they exist.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Same semantic contract ≠ same technical implementation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Current-state observation 2: Claude (.claude/) and Codex (.codex/) are evolving toward symmetry, technically different but consuming the same KnowledgeOS authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AGENTS.md → KnowledgeOS → Authoritative Knowledge (not AGENTS.md → KnowledgeOS replacement).
b_rows_sample.statement: Current-state observation 3: AGENTS.md functions as an important agent entry/pointer mechanism with high architectural value, provided it points to rather than replaces KnowledgeOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Agent Contextual Memory unless a governed promotion mechanism explicitly elevates a memory item.
b_rows_sample.statement: Current-state observation 4: .claude/memory/ gives agents cross-session persistence, but its semantic status must remain Agent Contextual Memory absent explicit governed promotion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rule → Checker → Result already exists; the architecture has not evolved around LLM → judgment.
b_rows_sample.statement: Current-state observation 5, called 'one of the most significant findings': the platform already contains deterministic assurance mechanisms, a strong foundation for the target Assurance Context.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'kos-current-state-reconstruction-model' POSSIBLY relates to 'knowledgeos-evidence-execution-protocol' (batch B0025). Note: Step 132's Design-Mode-to-Evidence-Mode reconstruction methodology: five current-state categories, per-capability current/target/evidence/status matrix, evidence-strength hierarchy, four-way FACT/DERIVED/HYPOTHESIS/TARGET claim discipline, seven delta categories (including INVESTIGATE to prevent premature INTRODUCE), and the never-introduce-without-searching rule.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This is not a ratification of Theory v1.3. It is a reviewed, consolidated theory draft / research synthesis ... Theory v1.2 remains frozen ... KNOWLEDGEOS-INFORMATION-TRANSFORMATION-THEORY-CONSOLIDATED-DRAFT-2026-09 ... use it as the adjudication baseline against which the existing Theory v1.2, KR-Z
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes this document explicitly as a research synthesis / candidate theory draft (KNOWLEDGEOS-INFORMATION-TRANSFORMATION-THEORY-CONSOLIDATED-DRAFT-2026-09), not a ratification of Theory v1.3, with Theory v1.2 remaining the frozen baseline; the draft is to be used as an adjudication baseline against which Theory v1.2 and the KR-ZERO, KR-REP-REDUCTION, and KR-BRIDGE-01 artifacts are compared, rather than replacing them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Pattern -> Candidate representation/operator -> Preservation test -> Algebraic-law test. A candidate becomes part of the theory only if it survives explicit experimentation and audit.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the theory's scientific workflow as Pattern -> Candidate representation/operator -> Preservation test -> Algebraic-law test, with a candidate entering the theory only once it survives explicit experimentation and audit.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Representation: D -> R ... Transformation: T: D -> R ... Observation: Pi: R -> O, or Q: D -> Y ... Preservation: a preservation requirement specifies what the transformation is required to retain ... C = (Q,Pi,R,...) rather than being an intrinsic property of a representation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines the theory's four fundamental layers that must not be collapsed prematurely: Representation (D->R, how information is encoded), Transformation (T:D->R, what operation changes the representation), Observation (Pi:R->O or Q:D->Y, what aspect we care about), and Preservation (a contract C=(Q,Pi,R,...) specifying what must remain unchanged, rather than an intrinsic representation property).

a_rows_sample.anchor: A representation is adequate only relative to a defined inquiry and preservation requirement. ... Information matters relative to a specified purpose.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the theory's central principle: a representation is adequate only relative to a defined inquiry and preservation requirement, so information should never be described as mattering absolutely but only relative to a specified purpose -- the basis of the contract-relative view of information.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H(Q(D)|T(D))=0 ... H(T(D)|Q(D)) ... H(T(D)) = H(Q(D)) + H(T(D)|Q(D)) ... A representation can therefore be adequate but large, adequate and reduced, inadequate but compact, or highly detailed yet still unsuitable for the required inquiry.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes representation adequacy as H(Q(D)|T(D))=0 and a second quantity H(T(D)|Q(D)) measuring information beyond what the inquiry determines, related by the decomposition H(T(D))=H(Q(D))+H(T(D)|Q(D)) hence H(T(D))>=H(Q(D)); notes these are different dimensions, so a representation can be adequate-but-large, adequate-and-reduced, inadequate-but-compact, or detailed-yet-unsuitable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(x|D1) != Zero(x|D2) ... Question: Does the same information behave differently in different contexts? ... Can Zero(S) be derived from Zero-status of proper subsets? These are different questions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates and formalizes the two separate dimensions of Zero (Dimension A: context dependence, Zero(x|D1)!=Zero(x|D2); Dimension B: determination order, whether Zero(S) can be derived from proper-subset Zero-status) as genuinely different questions whose relationship (whether contextual Zero causes higher-order Zero) remains open.

a_rows_sample.anchor: An invariant describes something that remains unchanged under transformation: Inv_T(D) = Inv_T(T(D)). Zero asks a different question: Pi(T(D)) = Pi(T(E_S(D))). The first asks: What survives transformation? The second asks: What can be eliminated without changing the observation? Invariant != Zero.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a new formal distinction between an invariant (Inv_T(D)=Inv_T(T(D)), asking what survives transformation) and Zero (Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))), asking what can be eliminated without changing the observation), concluding Invariant != Zero even though the two may interact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: E_S(D) removes S. It should not automatically be called a projection. A projection normally carries algebraic properties such as idempotence: P(P(D))=P(D). Unless those properties are established, the safer terminology is: elimination operator rather than projection.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a new terminological discipline: the elimination operator E_S(D) should not automatically be called a 'projection' since projections normally carry algebraic properties such as idempotence (P(P(D))=P(D)) that have not been established for E_S, so the safer term 'elimination operator' should be used instead.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Redundancy Zero: Information can be removed because equivalent information remains. Contextual Zero: Information is Zero in one context but not another. Cancellation Zero: A group becomes Zero because its combined effect cancels, even though individual members are not Zero. These should currently be
a_rows_sample.statement: Names three descriptive Zero-mechanism categories -- Redundancy Zero (removal because equivalent information remains), Contextual Zero (Zero(x|D1)!=Zero(x|D2)), and Cancellation Zero (a group becomes Zero via combined-effect cancellation despite individual members not being Zero) -- explicitly warning these are descriptive categories/hypotheses, not established ontological kinds, and that the ~90% singleton-determined empirical result does not prove all such cases are 'Redundancy Zero'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero was neither necessary nor sufficient for adequacy in the tested regime. The four cells were populated: Z+A, Z+I, NZ+A, NZ+I. ... Zero !=> Adequacy and Adequacy !=> Zero. This is one of the strongest current separations in the theory.
a_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates the KR-BRIDGE-01 result into a canonical theory statement: Zero was neither necessary nor sufficient for adequacy in the tested regime (all four cells Z+A, Z+I, NZ+A, NZ+I were populated), giving Zero!=>Adequacy and Adequacy!=>Zero as one of the strongest current separations in the theory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Within the tested deduplication regime, redundancy behaved as a common structural factor associated with both Zero occurrence and loss of adequacy. ... Observed correlation != established mechanism. ... an AI system must not convert an observed correlation into a knowledge rule without controlling f
a_rows_sample.statement: Draws the general methodological principle 'observed correlation != established mechanism' from the BRIDGE redundancy finding, arguing this is directly relevant to KnowledgeOS because an AI system must not convert an observed correlation into a knowledge rule without controlling for structural factors.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Only one redundancy stratum was genuinely informative for the direct within-transformation association. Other strata were structurally uninformative because adequacy or Zero was saturated. ... The natural imbalance should not simply be 'fixed' after the fact because that would alter the experimental
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the single-informative-stratum limitation of KR-BRIDGE-01 as a general experimental-design lesson: a natural stratum imbalance (other strata structurally uninformative due to saturation) should not be 'fixed' after the fact, since doing so would alter the experimental design rather than genuinely address the limitation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KR-ZERO _|_ KR-REP-REDUCTION. Here _|_ means: analytically separated / not unified by current evidence. This does not mean the two areas can never interact. It means: We currently have no sufficient evidence to define a single common reduction operator or common algebra containing both.
a_rows_sample.statement: Clarifies precisely what the KR-ZERO _|_ KR-REP-REDUCTION governance conclusion means: analytically separated / not unified by current evidence, i.e. there is currently no sufficient evidence to define a single common reduction operator or algebra containing both -- explicitly not a claim that the two areas can never interact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: T_R(D) = Inv_T(D) oplus Delta_R(D) oplus Rem_T(D). This should not be retained as a universal law. There is insufficient evidence for the direct-sum structure, the algebraic carrier, or the semantics of each component. A safer representation is a tuple: T_R(D) |-> (Inv_T(D), Delta_T(D), Rem_T(D)). E
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly rejects an earlier proposed universal decomposition T_R(D)=Inv_T(D) oplus Delta_R(D) oplus Rem_T(D) as a universal law, citing insufficient evidence for the direct-sum structure, algebraic carrier, or component semantics, replacing it with a safer tuple T_R(D) |-> (Inv_T(D), Delta_T(D), Rem_T(D)) whose entries remain candidate observables rather than established algebraic components.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Delta_R(D) = D - R should not be assumed. The difference between source and representation may require a typed operator: Delta_T(D,R). The representation may not even live in the same algebraic space as the source. Difference requires a defined type and operation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects assuming the difference between source and representation is simple subtraction (Delta_R(D)=D-R), requiring instead a typed operator Delta_T(D,R) since the representation may not live in the same algebraic space as the source, establishing the general principle that difference requires a defined type and operation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Vedic transformations provide examples of systematic representation changes that can be formalized and empirically tested. ... Historical pattern -> formal candidate -> controlled experiment -> audit -> possible theory. Historical interpretation and mathematical validation therefore remain separate.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates Vedic Mathematics's role as a generator of candidate transformation patterns (never proof of the theory), formalizing the research architecture Historical pattern -> formal candidate -> controlled experiment -> audit -> possible theory, keeping historical interpretation and mathematical validation strictly separate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: encode_B(K) = (B, delta_K) ... We do not assume that K = B - delta_K. ... Q(decode(B,delta_K)) === Q(K). The base-selection rule must be predeclared. Otherwise dynamic optimization can overfit the test data. ... f(a otimes_A b) = f(a) otimes_B f(b). If this fails, define a homomorphic defect ... P(x
a_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates four candidate Vedic-inspired operators into formal notation: reference-relative encoding encode_B(K)=(B,delta_K) with predeclared base-selection to avoid overfitting and correctness condition Q(decode(B,delta_K))=Q(K); structure-preserving composition f(a otimes_A b)=f(a) otimes_B f(b), with a 'homomorphic defect' quantity defined when it fails rather than assuming structure preservation; guarded specialized rewrite operators P(x)=>O_special(x)===O_general(x); and local transformation T(D)=Reconstruct(T(W_1(D)),...,T(W_n(D))) testing whether no information crosses locality boundaries.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Claim + not-Claim = 0 [rejected as a simplistic rule]. Cancellation is valid only when an appropriate inverse or observational cancellation structure has been demonstrated. ... Cancellation is a specialized emergent property, not a universal primitive.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms that cancellation must remain conservative: the simplistic rule Claim+notClaim=0 is rejected, cancellation being valid only once an appropriate inverse or observational cancellation structure is demonstrated, establishing cancellation as a specialized emergent property rather than a universal primitive.

a_rows_sample.anchor: An attractive interpretation must yield to an audit finding. ... the representation-reduction audit found: the bootstrap confidence interval procedure was invalid for the sparse conditional-entropy estimator; the rank invertibility claim failed because of tie handling. Those failures did not invalid
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports that the representation-reduction audit found two specific problems -- the bootstrap confidence-interval procedure was invalid for the sparse conditional-entropy estimator, and the rank-invertibility claim failed due to tie handling (matching the desc=(n+1)-asc falsification) -- neither of which invalidated the main structural conclusions (which rested on exact violation counts and train/test agreement), but both of which forced withdrawal of the affected claims, establishing the principle that an attractive interpretation must yield to an audit finding, essential if KnowledgeOS is to govern AI-generated knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 'Ascending and descending rank are merely invertible recodings.' The audit showed that deterministic tie-breaking makes this claim false in the implemented experiment.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally records the rejection of the claim that ascending and descending rank encodings are merely invertible recodings, since the audit showed deterministic tie-breaking makes this false in the implemented experiment -- the theory-level record of the desc=(n+1)-asc falsification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose P(C)=0.9 and P(O(T(D))=Q(D)|C)=1. The representation could be completely wrong when C is false. ... conditional zero loss => all representations satisfy constraints is invalid.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies an invalid step in a submitted proof: a definition of zero loss conditioned on a valid region (P(O(T(D))=Q(D) | AND_i c_i(T(D))=1)=1) does not imply the necessity claim that the representation's support lies entirely within that valid region, since the representation could be arbitrarily wrong when the condition is false; repairs it by defining zero loss as two separate unconditional requirements (P(C(T(D)))=1 and P(O(T(D))=Q(D))=1) or by restricting the theorem to an explicit valid domain X_Pi={D: for all i, c_i(T(D))=1}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Probabilistic zero loss: Q(D)=O(T(D)) P-a.s. ... Structural / pointwise zero loss: T(D1)=T(D2) => Q(D1)=Q(D2) for all D1,D2.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes two versions of a fiber-preservation condition that a submitted proof had conflated: probabilistic zero loss (Q(D)=O(T(D)) almost surely) versus structural/pointwise zero loss (deterministic fiber preservation for all D1,D2, not merely almost-surely); shows for deterministic Q that I(D;Q(D)|T(D))=0 is equivalent to H(Q(D)|T(D))=0, so the submitted proof's two stated conditions are not independent unless a pointwise (not merely a.s.) theorem is specifically wanted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: kernel normally belongs to a structure where such a notion is defined ... For now I would use Null_Pi(T) = {S: Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(D\S))} or ZeroSet_{T,Pi}(D) = {S subseteq D: Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D)}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Judges a submitted 'kernel' notation S in ker(T_Pi) premature since no ambient algebraic structure (homomorphism, distinguished zero element) has yet been established for the representation-reduction setting, proposing Null_Pi(T) / ZeroSet_{T,Pi}(D) as neutral placeholders pending discovery of whether kernel-like properties actually hold -- preserving the discipline of not assuming algebraic structure before observing it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H(R*) >= H(Q(D)) + H(C(D)|Q(D)) ... If the contract requires c_i(R)=1 with probability 1, then C_R=(1,...,1) is constant and H(C_R)=0. So the bound becomes simply H(R*) >= H(Q(D)).
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a submitted entropy lower bound: the constraint term should be the vector of realized predicate outcomes C_R=(c_1(R),...,c_k(R)) rather than the abstract predicate set C(D), and since a contract requiring c_i(R)=1 with probability 1 makes C_R a constant (H(C_R)=0), the bound collapses to the clean H(R*)>=H(Q(D)); also recommends separating Shannon entropy (for probabilistic experiments) from Kolmogorov complexity (for structural representations) as two distinct later research tracks rather than mixing them in one definition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: So 5 digits -> 2 digits is indeed the right intuition -- but the mathematical object we are searching for is not digit reduction. It is contract-relative representation reduction.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the '5 digits->2 digits' intuition rigorously: the question is not digit count but whether Q(D)=O(R2), i.e. whether the reduced representation R2 is zero-loss RELATIVE to (Q,Pi); if adequate and no smaller representation works, R2=R*_Pi is a candidate minimal adequate representation -- proposing 'can Vedic transformations discover minimal adequate representations?' as the sharpened research question, and renaming the target object 'Entropy-Minimal Adequate Representation' to distinguish it from other minimality notions (description/dimension/cardinality/structural/computational).

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'H(Q(D)|T(D))=0'

a_rows_sample.anchor: The kernel creates the ecosystem; the company creates value around the ecosystem.
a_rows_sample.statement: Uses the Linux/Red Hat precedent to argue KnowledgeOS's moat is the kernel plus governance plus evidence model (not the AI model, which is commoditized), proposing a Community/Professional/Enterprise revenue-tier structure and a 10-year IPO roadmap.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel = the minimal system responsible for creating, identifying, relating, governing, and preserving organizational knowledge objects.
a_rows_sample.statement: The proposed load-bearing definition of the 'KnowledgeOS Kernel', explicitly modeled after the Linux kernel's separation from applications: the kernel provides knowledge primitives (Identity, Lifecycle, Evidence, Authority) and must not know about specific technologies (SAP, Kubernetes, Jira).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Linus did not start by designing 'the operating system of the world.' He started by solving a concrete problem, created a small working kernel ... 'Can we create a trusted kernel that allows digitalization robots to operate safely?'
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues KnowledgeOS should not start with an AI-driven Digitalization Robot ambition; the correct starting question is the smallest trusted kernel that later allows robots to operate safely, mirroring Linux's incremental 0.01-kernel-first history.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Open-source the KnowledgeOS Kernel. Commercialize the Digitalization Robot Platform.
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommends an open-core business model (open KnowledgeOS Kernel for trust/ecosystem, commercial Digitalization Robot/Enterprise Platform for revenue), by analogy with Linux Kernel vs Red Hat Enterprise Linux.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Linux manages computer resources. KnowledgeOS manages organizational intelligence resources ... which knowledge is valid, who owns it, and how can it be trusted?
a_rows_sample.statement: States the deepest claimed difference between the Linux and KnowledgeOS kernel analogies: Linux answers 'which process can access which resource', while KnowledgeOS must answer 'which knowledge is valid, who owns it, and how can it be trusted.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Rust for the KnowledgeOS Kernel, Kotlin/Spring for the Enterprise Runtime, Python for Intelligence, TypeScript for Experience.
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommends a multi-language technology stack (Rust kernel for memory-safety/correctness, Kotlin+Spring Boot enterprise runtime, Python intelligence layer, TypeScript studio/frontend) with an estimated 12-18 month timeline for a first Kernel v1.0 with a small expert team.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If you want IPO potential, do not position KnowledgeOS as 'AI chatbot' ... nor 'Documentation tool' ... Position as: The operating system for enterprise knowledge and digital transformation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues the commercial positioning category determines addressable market size; 'AI chatbot' is too easy to copy, 'documentation tool' is too small a category for IPO ambitions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel scope: 'minimal kernel, no AI' (S0167) vs the platform vision where an AI-driven Digitalization Robot is the top layer (S0171) — the corpus itself frames the robot as a distribution, keeping the kernel AI-free, so the tension is scope of the 'core' vs the 'product'.
a_rows_sample.statement: Surfaces T1: a minimal AI-free kernel proposal versus an AI-driven robot as the platform's top execution layer, resolved by the corpus's own framing (robot = distribution, kernel stays AI-free) but not formally decided.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Rust · Spring Boot · Gradle/Cargo · microservices · plugin architecture · Event Sourcing · Kafka are recommendations/hypotheses in the corpus, never adopted KnowledgeOS technology.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit preservation note keeping every named technology recommendation level-tagged as a hypothesis, never promoted to adopted architecture, while noting the existing PHP/Laravel + TypeScript/Vue platform is the ESTABLISHED current stack.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DI principle vs framework import: adopt the DI/composition-root principle without adopting Spring — the corpus wants the first, but the kernel file pairs the principle with the Spring runtime.
a_rows_sample.statement: Surfaces T4: the DI-principle proposal explicitly wants the principle without the Spring framework, yet the kernel-technology brainstorm pairs the same principle with a recommended Spring/Kotlin runtime.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KNOWLEDGEOS KERNEL protects: identity · evidence · provenance · lifecycle · authority · invariants · temporal state / higher layers provide: assurance · analytics · inference · simulation · AI · visualization · delivery ... a PROPOSED KERNEL BOUNDARY CANDIDATE, outline supported, provenance+temporal weak.
a_rows_sample.statement: H-10: tests the seven-concern kernel/higher-layer split against all three baselines per-concern; identity, evidence, lifecycle, authority, and invariants are supported, provenance and temporal state are weak, so the overall split is a candidate outline, not an established fact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: WHAT IS THE CORE DOMAIN ACT? ... Verification | Admission | Determination | Transformation | Epistemic Maintenance | Justification Preservation | Constitutional Transition
a_rows_sample.statement: Seven alternative formulations of KnowledgeOS's core domain act are compared (Verification, Admission, Determination, Transformation, Epistemic Maintenance, Justification Preservation, Constitutional Transition), each with its domain-meaning implication.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The core domain act is the constitutionally-gated transition from candidate to admissible knowledge state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Hypothesis: the Kernel's core domain act is the constitutionally-gated transition from candidate to admissible knowledge state, combining a candidate, a gate (constitutional rules), a verdict (admissibility), and a state change.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A knowledge claim cannot exist without: identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposed aggregate invariant: a knowledge claim cannot exist without identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history all present and consistent together; the Kernel is framed as 'the guardian of this aggregate invariant.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate -> Verification -> Admissibility -> Identity -> Epistemic State -> Knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Admission is modelled as a distinction chain (Candidate -> Verification[well-formed?] -> Admissibility[constitution?] -> Identity[stable anchor?] -> Epistemic State -> Knowledge) and as an 8-step process from candidate proposal to emission of KnowledgeCreated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Identity assignment | ESSENTIAL ... Semantic interpretation | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Reasoning | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Workflow | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Projection | NOT ESSENTIAL
a_rows_sample.statement: A capability table classifies identity assignment, evidence admission, justification preservation, epistemic-state determination, confidence assignment, history recording, and constitutional evaluation as ESSENTIAL (each tied to a named invariant); candidate verification as SUPPORTING; and semantic interpretation, reasoning, workflow, and projection as NOT ESSENTIAL to the Kernel's minimum domain capacity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Natural-language interpretation | Parsing | Normalization | Canonicalization | Reasoning | Candidate generation | Retrieval | Search | Ranking | Model inference | Orchestration | Workflow | Projection | UI | Infrastructure | Evidence acquisition
a_rows_sample.statement: A 15-item table enumerates responsibilities that belong OUTSIDE the Kernel, each with a DDD reason: natural-language interpretation, parsing, normalization, canonicalization, reasoning, candidate generation, retrieval, search, ranking, model inference, orchestration, workflow, projection, UI, infrastructure, and evidence acquisition -- summarized as the principle that the Kernel is representation-agnostic and does not perform semantic interpretation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Kernel is a domain boundary, not a component.
a_rows_sample.statement: Six candidate interpretations of what the Kernel 'is' are compared (aggregate boundary, domain decision boundary, admission boundary, consistency boundary, constitutional boundary, small domain core inside the aggregate); concludes the Kernel is best understood as the admission boundary + consistency boundary -- a conceptual domain boundary, not an implementation component, though it may be implemented inside the aggregate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeCreated is the domain event that signals the completion of admission.
a_rows_sample.statement: KnowledgeCreated is analyzed as the domain event signalling completion of admission -- the business moment the candidate becomes part of KnowledgeOS with identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history all established; the Kernel's job is to produce this event on success and nothing/a rejection on failure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is a governed knowledge-admission system.
a_rows_sample.statement: Four formulations of the knowledge/evidence relationship are compared (evidence registry, justified epistemic-state system, governed knowledge-admission system, constitutional knowledge machine); 'governed knowledge-admission system' is judged best supported -- evidence supports knowledge, knowledge requires evidence, evidence is admitted and preserved alongside knowledge, but evidence is not itself knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: O\rightarrow E\rightarrow Q\rightarrow I\rightarrow K and K\rightarrow D\rightarrow A.
b_rows_sample.statement: First correction: a single set K cannot mean 'knowledge' generically -- distinguishes O (Observation), E (Evidence), Q (Claim), I (Inference), K (Accepted Knowledge), D (Decision), A (Action) as different domain objects, giving epistemic progression O->E->Q->I->K and operational progression K->D->A.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Role(X,C) determines its domain meaning in context C. ... Artifact\neq EpistemicRole. Meaning is contextual.
b_rows_sample.statement: Artifact versus epistemic role: for artifact X, Role(X,C) determines its domain meaning in context C, so Artifact != EpistemicRole -- the same artifact can be evidence in one context and historical knowledge after acceptance in another; 'meaning is contextual' connects DDD directly to the mathematical model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C=(S_C,V_C,R_C,P_C,A_C)
b_rows_sample.statement: Context is formalized beyond a bounded-context name as a 5-tuple C=(S_C semantic vocabulary, V_C validity rules, R_C material distinctions, P_C policies, A_C authority model) -- a DDD bounded context is thus a semantic and governance environment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \llbracket x\rrbracket_{C_1}\neq\llbracket x\rrbracket_{C_2}. Same representation \not\Rightarrow same meaning.
b_rows_sample.statement: Bounded context as semantic space: an object x has meaning through a context-relative denotation [[x]]_C, and the same representation can have different meanings under different contexts ([[x]]_C1 != [[x]]_C2) -- 'same representation does not imply same meaning' is proposed as a mathematical foundation of DDD bounded contexts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: x_1\sim_\phi x_2\iff\phi(x_1)=\phi(x_2). ... [x]_\phi.
b_rows_sample.statement: Context mapping phi_AB: S_A -> S_B between bounded contexts is not assumed bijective (often partial/many-to-one/one-to-many/conditional/lossy); it induces an equivalence relation x1 ~phi x2 iff phi(x1)=phi(x2) with equivalence classes [x]_phi, giving a rigorous formal handle on information/semantic collapse.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SemanticViolation\iff MaterialDistinction\land UncontrolledCollapse.
b_rows_sample.statement: Semantic loss is formalized precisely: a collapse phi_AB(x1)=phi_AB(x2) where x1 is not~_A x2 is a candidate semantic-loss event, but is an error (SemanticViolation) only if the collapsed distinction belongs to R_A or R_B (i.e. is material) -- SemanticViolation iff MaterialDistinction and UncontrolledCollapse, much stronger than simply 'preserve semantics'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: M_A(x_1,x_2)\land\phi(x_1)=\phi(x_2)\Rightarrow DeclaredLoss
b_rows_sample.statement: Context-specific materiality predicate M_C(x1,x2) ('the distinction between x1 and x2 is material in context C') yields the architectural invariant candidate: M_A(x1,x2) and phi(x1)=phi(x2) implies DeclaredLoss for a transformation crossing from A to B.

b_rows_sample.anchor: T=(K_A,C_A,A_t,P_t,E_t,\tau)\rightarrow(K_B,C_B).
b_rows_sample.statement: Transformation T is progressively enriched from a bare (K_A,C_A)->(K_B,C_B) mapping to a full domain operation T=(K_A,C_A,Actor_t,Policy_t,Evidence_t,tau)->(K_B,C_B), with the DDD distinction Command (expresses intent) -> Transformation (domain operation/process) -> Event (records what happened).

b_rows_sample.anchor: L(K_t)=\{(K_i,T_i,A_i,E_i,\tau_i,C_i)\}. ... KnowledgeOS lineage = typed provenance graph.
b_rows_sample.statement: Lineage is formalized as a typed provenance graph G_L=(V_L,E_L) (nodes=knowledge states/artifacts, edges=transformations carrying metadata (T,A,E,C,tau)), generally a DAG allowing branching (K1->{K2^A,K2^B}) and merging -- substantially stronger than an ordinary version chain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Auth(a,r,c,p) mean actor a is authorized under role r, context c, and policy p. ... Identity\neq Authority.
b_rows_sample.statement: Authority is formalized as a relation Auth(a,r,c,p) (actor, role, context, policy) rather than A=User; an action is legitimate only if Auth(a,r,c,p)=True, giving Identity != Authority (authenticated but not authorized is possible).

b_rows_sample.anchor: E_q=(source,observation,context,time,method,provenance). ... E_q\xrightarrow{\mathcal I}Q.
b_rows_sample.statement: Evidence is formalized as a 6-tuple E_q=(source,observation,context,time,method,provenance) rather than a boolean Evidence=True, supporting a claim Q via an inferential procedure E_q -I-> Q.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \hat F_n\neq F. Observation\neq PopulationTruth.
b_rows_sample.statement: Statistical interpretation of evidence: the empirical distribution hat F_n(x) estimates but is not identical to the underlying distribution F, giving Observation != PopulationTruth; likewise a confidence interval must never be silently converted into a ProbabilityOfTruth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: P(\theta\mid E)=\frac{P(E\mid\theta)P(\theta)}{P(E)}. ... Bayesian machinery is one possible formalism for representing uncertainty where the domain permits probabilistic interpretation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Bayesian evidence via Bayes' rule is offered as one possible uncertainty formalism, not a mandatory commitment -- must not be introduced merely because 'KnowledgeOS is probabilistic'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance=DeterministicAssurance\cup StatisticalEvidence\cup HumanJudgement.
b_rows_sample.statement: Two assurance modes are distinguished and must not be conflated: Deterministic (I(x)=True/False, e.g. SchemaValid(x)) and Statistical (P(H|E) or an estimator with uncertainty), together with human judgment forming Assurance = DeterministicAssurance union StatisticalEvidence union HumanJudgement; the appropriate mode depends on the invariant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Hash(x)=h. ... P(X>x). ... Meaning(x,C). ... Authorized(a,p). These require different mathematical structures.
b_rows_sample.statement: Architectural properties are classified by kind, each needing different mathematics: exact (Hash(x)=h), empirical (P(X>x)), interpretive (Meaning(x,C)), normative (Authorized(a,p)) -- resolving the previous risk of treating every architectural property as probabilistically quantifiable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Set/Logic + Probability/Statistics + Semantics + Graph Theory.
b_rows_sample.statement: KnowledgeOS is proposed to span four mathematical domains: Logic (handles invariants), Statistics (uncertainty and empirical evidence), Semantics (meaning and context), Graph theory (lineage and transformation history) -- a more defensible architecture than reducing everything to one equation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeItem, Transformation, EvidenceRecord, Decision, Policy, ProvenanceRecord. Each aggregate protects its own invariants.
b_rows_sample.statement: Candidate DDD aggregate boundaries (avoiding one enormous transactional aggregate): KnowledgeItem, Transformation, EvidenceRecord, Decision, Policy, ProvenanceRecord, each with its own invariant -- e.g. KnowledgeItem 'cannot change materially without a recorded transition'; Transformation 'cannot be considered governed without an applicable authority/policy decision'; EvidenceRecord 'cannot silently change after being used to support a claim' (a source change must produce a new evidence state); Decision = f(Evidence,Authority,Context,Policy), not authoritative merely by existing; Policy determines AllowedTransformations/RequiredEvidence/RequiredAuthority/RequiredValidation, giving Policy->GovernedTransformation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ObservationRecorded, EvidenceRegistered, ClaimProposed, KnowledgeAccepted, TransformationRequested, TransformationExecuted, ValidationCompleted, DecisionApproved, KnowledgeSuperseded.
b_rows_sample.statement: Nine candidate domain events forming the temporal history, supporting an event-sourced interpretation K_t = Fold(E_1,...,E_t), i.e. CurrentState = f(EventHistory) -- explicitly noted as an implementation choice, not a mandatory architecture requirement.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal K=(State,Context,Transformation,Evidence,Authority) with Lineage being generated by the sequence of transformations: L=History(T).
b_rows_sample.statement: The kernel is reduced from the original 6-tuple (K,C,T,A,E,L) to a 5-tuple (K,C,T,E,A) by recognizing Lineage L is not independent but generated by the transformation history: L = History(T) -- an important reduction toward the minimal kernel.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SI=f(K,C,T) ... BP=f(C,T) ... EI=f(K,E) ... GA=f(A,T) ... TL=f(T_{1:n}) ... DA=f(E,T,Policy). ... the seven principles may not be seven fundamental architectural primitives. They may be derived properties.
b_rows_sample.statement: Candidate dependency equations deriving the 6 (of the earlier 7-8) named architectural principles as functions of the minimal kernel: SemanticIntegrity=f(K,C,T), BoundaryPreservation=f(C,T), EpistemicIntegrity=f(K,E), GovernedAction=f(A,T), TemporalLineage=f(T_{1:n}), Assurance/DeterministicAssurance=f(E,T,Policy) -- proposing that these principles may be derived properties rather than independent primitives, precisely the compression the historical audit sought.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'step230-minimal-architectural-kernel' POSSIBLY relates to 'knowledgeos-kernel-concept' (batch B0038). Note: Step 230 (phase_measure_theory): derives a candidate minimal mathematical/DDD kernel for KnowledgeOS, reducing the initial 6-tuple (K,C,T,A,E,L) to a 5-tuple (K,C,T,E,A) with Lineage L=History(T), and proposes the seven candidate architectural principles (Semantic Integrity, Boundary Preservation, Epistemic Integrity, Governed Action, Temporal Lineage, Assurance) as DERIVED functions of the kernel rather than independent primitives. Also formalizes the O->E->Q->I->K epistemic progression, context as a 5-tuple, the phi_AB context-mapping-induced semantic-collapse equivalence relation, candidate DDD aggregates (KnowledgeItem, Transformation, EvidenceRecord, Decision, Policy), a four-plane architecture (Semantic/Epistemic/Transformation/Governance + crossing Lineage), and a four-level stack (Mathematical/Domain/Implementation/Philosophical).

a_rows_sample.anchor: the following research lenses have been analysed
a_rows_sample.statement: Full enumerated list of research lenses consumed by the study, explicitly framed as 'research lenses only. They are not automatically kernel laws': EKS/PKS/AIP archaeological evidence; Epistemic Control Systems; Knowledge lifecycle and snapshot models; TMS/AGM belief revision; Logic and inference theory; Nyaya Tarka Shastra reasoning; Vedanta epistemology; Jnana/Jneya/Jnata distinction; Vani (expression and transmission); Zero as neutral-state metaphor; Topological invariants; Sheaf/context composition; and six Navya-Nyaya sub-lenses: Abhava (structured absence), Avacchedaka (semantic delimitation), Hetvabhasa (reasoning fallacies), Coextension without identity, Intensional identity preservation, Type-theoretic interpretation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Expected Registered Invariants ... Identity Family ... Evidence Family ... Authority Family ... Transformation Family ... Temporal Family ... Reasoning Family ... Contradiction Family ... Agent Family
a_rows_sample.statement: Part 3 schema (ID|Invariant|Dimensions|Forbidden Collapse|Evidence|Strength|Validation Target|Notes/Boundary) plus the expected 8-family protect-statements: Identity (Representation != Identity: 'knowledge identity survives representation changes'; Expression != Meaning; Context Preservation: 'meaning requires semantic frame'); Evidence ('Observation != Interpretation', 'Evidence != Authority'); Authority ('Source authority is assigned, not intrinsic'); Transformation ('Knowledge evolution must preserve lineage'); Temporal ('Knowledge exists with temporal validity'); Reasoning ('Observation != Inference'; 'Inference requires preserved justification'); Contradiction ('Contradiction != Failure'; 'Conflicting knowledge may coexist'); Agent ('Knower identity is part of epistemic state').

a_rows_sample.anchor: Family 1 -- IDENTITY (What is this knowledge? -- identity conditions of meaning)
a_rows_sample.statement: Family 1 (IDENTITY) table: INV-KOS-002 Semantic Continuity (forbids Representation->Meaning); H-KOS-Context-001 Semantic Frame Preservation (forbids Context Removal->Meaning); H-KOS-Context-002 Avacchedaka (forbids Unbounded Claim->Over-extended Knowledge; compression ruling SUBSUMES SemanticBoundary-001, Ontology-001, Abhava Boundary-001 facet, and the type-model context-clause as facets of this one row); H-KOS-Relationship-001 Knowledge Relationship Integrity/Tripuji (forbids Known Object->Detached Autonomous Truth); H-KOS-Relation-001 Epistemic Relations as First-Class (forbids Relation->Attribute; compression ruling: the general principle UNDER the separation family, with INV-001..004 + Expression!=Meaning + Observation!=Inference as its instances).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Family 2 -- EVIDENCE (Why should we believe this?)
a_rows_sample.statement: Family 2 (EVIDENCE) table: INV-001 Evidence != Authority (ESTABLISHED); INV-KOS-Pramana-001 Means of Acquisition (forbids the 'Source-role collapse' -- flattening sensor=expert statement=AI inference=historical document; the designation ruling names the Pramana source-role separation AS this row's Forbidden-Collapse content, not a separate row); H-KOS-EvidenceAuthenticity-001 Evidence vs Pseudo-Evidence (forbids Pseudo-evidence->Evidence, anti-hallucination); H-ZERO-001 UNKNOWN is a Valid Epistemic State (forbids Unknown->False / Unknown->Missing, i.e. Unknown != Absent != False); H-KOS-Uncertainty-001 Structured Doubt/Samsaya (forbids Doubt->Missing data; compression ruling: a proposed H-KOS-Abhava-001 compresses INTO Uncertainty-001).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 83.67 — New invariants: I_TemporalTruth, I_EventTime, I_HistoricalIntegrity, I_TemporalAuthority, I_TemporalUncertainty, I_TemporalSupersession
a_rows_sample.statement: States six new named invariants: I_TemporalTruth (claims whose truth can change must have explicit temporal interpretation), I_EventTime (event/observation/processing times must remain distinguishable when materially relevant), I_HistoricalIntegrity (historical decisions must be interpreted using knowledge/models/policies/authorities valid at decision time), I_TemporalAuthority (authorization must be evaluated at time of action), I_TemporalUncertainty (unknown/interval timestamps must not be converted into false point precision), I_TemporalSupersession (superseded knowledge remains historically reconstructable).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 82.72 — New invariants: I_UncertaintyPreservation, I_Dependence, I_ModelUncertainty, I_Calibration, I_EpistemicPrecision, I_DecisionSensitivity, I_UncertaintyImpact
a_rows_sample.statement: States seven new named invariants: I_UncertaintyPreservation (transformations must not silently discard material uncertainty), I_Dependence (dependencies between uncertain variables must be represented when material), I_ModelUncertainty (model-structure uncertainty must be distinguished from parameter uncertainty), I_Calibration (probabilistic claims should have defined semantics and empirical calibration where applicable), I_EpistemicPrecision (output precision must not misrepresent evidence quality), I_DecisionSensitivity (when uncertainty can change the selected action, sensitivity must remain visible), I_UncertaintyImpact (material upstream evidence changes must permit identification of affected downstream knowledge/decisions).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 84.63 — New invariants: I_Intervention, I_CounterfactualProvenance, I_CounterfactualUncertainty, I_TemporalCausalSeparation, I_CounterfactualGovernance, I_Interference
a_rows_sample.statement: States six new named invariants: I_Intervention (observed association must not be represented as causal intervention without justification), I_CounterfactualProvenance (material counterfactual claims retain their model, evidence, and assumptions), I_CounterfactualUncertainty (counterfactual results preserve uncertainty and model sensitivity), I_TemporalCausalSeparation (observed historical outcomes must remain distinct from unobserved alternative outcomes), I_CounterfactualGovernance (causal feasibility of an intervention does not imply authorization to execute it), I_Interference (counterfactual analysis must account for material interactions between agents, components, or interventions).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 85.77 — New strategic invariants: I_IncentiveAlignment, I_MetricIntegrity, I_StrategicRobustness, I_AuthorizationUnknown, I_GovernanceBoundary, I_MetaGovernance, I_IncentiveObservability
a_rows_sample.statement: States seven new strategic invariants: I_IncentiveAlignment (material incentives must not systematically reward behavior violating higher-level objectives), I_MetricIntegrity (governance metrics must not be equated with the underlying objective without justified relationship), I_StrategicRobustness (governance evaluation should consider adaptive/optimizing-against-mechanism behavior), I_AuthorizationUnknown (unknown authorization must not be interpreted as permission), I_GovernanceBoundary (material governance constraints must account for alternative execution paths), I_MetaGovernance (changes to governance mechanisms are themselves governed changes), I_IncentiveObservability (where strategic behavior is material, the system should model incentives and information as part of the behavioral model).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 87.75 — New invariants: I_Aggregation, I_AuthorityExpertise, I_CollectiveConstraint, I_Quorum, I_Delegation, I_HistoricalAggregation, I_RecommendationDecision, I_DecisionAuthorization
a_rows_sample.statement: States eight new invariants: I_Aggregation (every collective decision must use an explicitly defined aggregation mechanism), I_AuthorityExpertise (expertise, evidence quality, preference, and decision authority must not be conflated), I_CollectiveConstraint (collective preference cannot override higher-order mandatory constraints), I_Quorum (a decision requiring quorum must not become valid without sufficient authorized participation), I_Delegation (delegated authority cannot exceed the authority validly delegated by the delegator), I_HistoricalAggregation (historical decisions must be interpreted using the aggregation rules valid at decision time), I_RecommendationDecision (recommendation must not automatically become decision without required authority), I_DecisionAuthorization (a decision does not automatically grant execution authority unless the governance model explicitly defines that transition).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 86.83 — New invariants: I_Mechanism, I_IncentiveCompatibility, I_IndependentVerification, I_GovernanceSurface, I_StrategicRobustness2, I_MechanismVersioning, I_FeasibleActionSpace
a_rows_sample.statement: States seven new invariants: I_Mechanism (governance mechanisms must be evaluated by resulting behavior, not only formal rules), I_IncentiveCompatibility (where truthful/desired behavior is required, the mechanism must not create a systematic incentive to deviate), I_IndependentVerification (material claims should not depend exclusively on self-reported evidence when independent verification is feasible and material), I_GovernanceSurface (material alternative execution paths must be governed, restricted, or recognized as exception paths), I_StrategicRobustness2 (governance must be evaluated under plausible strategic responses, not only cooperative behavior), I_MechanismVersioning (changes to governance mechanisms must be versioned, authorized, and historically reconstructable), I_FeasibleActionSpace (optimization must occur within the set of constitutionally, governance, and authority-valid actions).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 88.80 — New mathematical invariants: I_InformationPreservation, I_Sufficiency, I_CompressionProvenance, I_CompressionTime, I_CompressionUncertainty, I_NegativeKnowledge, I_RetrievalAssurance, I_DerivedReproducibility, I_RepresentationSeparation
