a_rows_sample.statement: Characterizes the reviewed R_req document as covering 8 categories, 47 core distinctions, 3 priority tiers, 5 verification criteria, and 12 explicitly identified gaps -- a scale and structure notably larger than the R_req document read directly elsewhere in this batch (4 categories, 9 distinctions, 2-part verification suite), suggesting either this reviews an expanded v0.1 draft not present in this batch, or an inconsistency in self-characterization between related documents.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Known vs. Believed vs. True | TRUE != BELIEVED != KNOWN | Tier 1 ... Explicit vs. Implicit | Levesque (1984) | Tier 1 ... Stored vs. Derived vs. Entailed | KR-CONTR-FDE-2026-09 | Tier 1 ... Representation vs. Reality | Zero Lens | Tier 1
a_rows_sample.statement: Cross-references eight distinctions the Perplexity research finds already present in the KnowledgeOS corpus (Known/Believed/True, Explicit/Implicit citing Levesque 1984, Stored/Derived/Entailed citing KR-CONTR-FDE-2026-09, Observed/Inferred/Reported citing Gap Theory v1.0, NoEvidence/NotAssessed, Unresolved/False, NoKnownGap/Complete, and Representation/Reality, all citing the 'Zero Lens' specification), confirming these are independently recognized as Tier 1 by external formal-KR-literature cross-reference.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Dynamic R_req — R_req may change as the system evolves. Context-sensitive R_req — Required distinctions may depend on context. Learned R_req — System may learn which distinctions matter.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes three long-term research directions treating R_req itself as potentially non-static: a Dynamic R_req that changes as the system evolves, a Context-sensitive R_req whose required distinctions depend on context, and a Learned R_req where the system learns which distinctions matter over time.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R_req is a well-structured, evidence-based definition of required distinctions. ... It requires additional distinctions from formal KR literature, formal logic definitions, and empirical testing. ... Recommendation: Ratify R_req with 10 additional distinctions. Next Step: Formal logic definitions and empirical testing.
a_rows_sample.statement: Final recommendation: ratify R_req after incorporating the ten proposed additional distinctions, with formal logic definitions and empirical testing as the immediate next step; the response explicitly labels itself 'Status: Research Complete'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R_req = {d_1, d_2, ..., d_k} ... K preserves a distinction d in R_req iff: for all s1,s2 in S: (s1 not~_d s2) implies (E(s1) != E(s2)). If E(s1)=E(s2) when s1 not~_d s2, the language K collapses the distinction d.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates (appearing twice, verbatim, within this file) the R_req formal specification: R_req is a set of semantic distinctions {d_1,...,d_k}, each an equivalence relation on state space S; a representation language K preserves a distinction d iff states distinguished by d are always encoded differently by E, and collapses d otherwise; a projection pi is R_req-adequate iff it preserves every distinction in R_req.

type_signature.domain: state space S with equivalence relations

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1.1 Knowledge Status ... Values: KnownTrue, KnownFalse, Unknown (Open), Contradictory (Both), Underdetermined (Insufficient information to decide), NotAssessed. Formal Semantics: Evaluated over First-Degree Entailment (FDE) double-powerset truth valuations V(phi) subseteq {T,F}. Evidence: Demonstrated by KR-CONTR-FDE-2026-09.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the R_req Knowledge Status distinction (Tier P1): six values (KnownTrue, KnownFalse, Unknown, Contradictory, Underdetermined, NotAssessed) evaluated over FDE double-powerset truth valuations V(phi) subseteq {T,F}, evidenced by KR-CONTR-FDE-2026-09; notes classical logic collapses Contradictory to explosive falsity, and 3-valued logics (K3/L3) collapse Contradictory and Underdetermined into one Undefined state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 3.2 Absence of Evidence vs. Evidence of Absence ... AbsenceOfEvidence iff phi not-in K and not-phi not-in K ... EvidenceOfAbsence iff there exists e in E: e |- not-phi ... Evidence: Zero Lens Specification (Non-collapse Invariant #3).
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the Absence-of-Evidence vs Evidence-of-Absence distinction (Tier P1): AbsenceOfEvidence holds iff neither phi nor not-phi is in K; EvidenceOfAbsence holds iff some evidence e derives not-phi; cited as required by the Zero Lens Specification's Non-collapse Invariant #3, and as a distinction every other compared formalism (FOL, K3/L3, plain FDE) collapses while R_req preserves it.

type_signature.domain: K and evidence set E over proposition phi

a_rows_sample.anchor: I read the attached document in full. My assessment is that it is useful, but it is not yet safe to merge into the KnowledgeOS theory as written ... The most important work is therefore not to add all 10 proposed distinctions. It is to extract the valid theoretical contribution, correct the formalism, and prevent R_req from becoming an over-constraining 'master ontology.'
a_rows_sample.statement: Executive verdict on an R_req/ratification-style document: classified as research analysis / candidate specification, not yet ratifiable; explicitly rejects the document's own recommendation to add all ten proposed distinctions and to ratify, warning against R_req becoming an over-constraining 'master ontology'; distills the strongest contribution as R_req = the distinctions that must remain available for KnowledgeOS's required questions, combined with Representation Adequacy iff required distinctions are preserved.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I read the attached document in full. My assessment is that it is useful, but it is not yet safe to merge into the KnowledgeOS theory as written ... The most important work is therefore not to add all 10 proposed distinctions. It is to extract the valid theoretical contribution, correct the formalism, and prevent R_req from becoming an over-constraining 'master ontology.'
b_rows_sample.statement: Executive verdict on an R_req/ratification-style document: classified as research analysis / candidate specification, not yet ratifiable; explicitly rejects the document's own recommendation to add all ten proposed distinctions and to ratify, warning against R_req becoming an over-constraining 'master ontology'; distills the strongest contribution as R_req = the distinctions that must remain available for KnowledgeOS's required questions, combined with Representation Adequacy iff required distinctions are preserved.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the stronger KnowledgeOS definition should be: Adequacy(R,Q,Gamma) iff R preserves all distinctions in D_Q(Gamma) ... not: R preserves every distinction in D. The document itself notices this problem under projection adequacy, where it recommends allowing lower-tier distinctions to be lost. That observation should actually be moved up into the fundamental definition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the pairwise-preservation definition of adequacy (d(x)!=d(y) implies R(x)!=R(y) for all d) to be question-relative from the start: Adequacy(R,Q,Gamma) iff R preserves all distinctions in D_Q(Gamma), not all distinctions in D universally -- because a representation may legitimately collapse a distinction irrelevant to the current question; promotes an observation the original document made only under 'projection adequacy' up into the foundational definition.

type_signature.domain: representation R, question Q, context Gamma

b_rows_sample.anchor: For KnowledgeOS: Required != Interesting != Available in literature. A distinction belongs in R_req only if we can establish that some KnowledgeOS question, invariant, operation, assurance requirement or boundary requires it. ... analytic/synthetic, a priori/a posteriori, necessary/contingent, intentional/extensional, de dicto/de re ... their existence in the KR/philosophy literature does not establish that KnowledgeOS must preserve them.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the principle Required != Interesting != Available-in-literature: a distinction enters R_req only if some KnowledgeOS question, invariant, operation, assurance requirement, or boundary can be shown to require it; existence in KR/philosophy literature alone (cited for analytic/synthetic, a priori/a posteriori, necessary/contingent, intensional/extensional, de dicto/de re) is not sufficient grounds.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A. Strong candidates: 1. Truth vs. validity ... 2. Satisfiability vs. unsatisfiability ... 3. Soundness vs. completeness ... 4. Decidability vs. undecidability ... 5. Local vs. global scope ... 6. Intensional vs. extensional ... 7. De dicto vs. de re ... B. Probably outside core R_req: Analytic vs. synthetic ... A priori vs. a posteriori ... Necessary vs. contingent ... These should remain external research candidates, not Tier 2 requirements.
b_rows_sample.statement: Splits the document's ten proposed additional distinctions into Group A (strong candidates deserving further KnowledgeOS work: truth-vs-validity, satisfiability-vs-unsatisfiability, soundness-vs-completeness, decidability-vs-undecidability, local-vs-global scope, intensional-vs-extensional, de-dicto-vs-de-re) and Group B (probably outside core R_req: analytic-vs-synthetic, a-priori-vs-a-posteriori, necessary-vs-contingent), recommending Group B remain external research candidates rather than Tier 2 requirements.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Truth vs. Validity -- |=alpha vs. Sigma|=alpha. This is not a clean distinction ... So the important distinction is: Validity != Entailment rather than: Truth != Validity. At the semantic level: M|=alpha is truth of alpha in a model M. Then |=alpha is validity across all models. And Sigma|=alpha is entailment from Sigma. This should be corrected before incorporating the item.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a formal error in the source document's Truth-vs-Validity distinction: the real three-way distinction is M|=alpha (truth of alpha in model M) versus |=alpha (validity: true in every model) versus Sigma|=alpha (entailment from Sigma); the document's proposed 'Truth vs Validity' pairing is not clean and should be replaced by Validity != Entailment before incorporation.

type_signature.domain: formula alpha, model M, theory Sigma

b_rows_sample.anchor: we already have a critical KnowledgeOS boundary: Satisfiability != Contr because satisfiability is relative to Semantics + Language + ModelClass. Thus: Cons_S(K) iff exists M, M |=_S K could be a candidate formal consistency property. But it must not become: Contr(K) = not Cons_S(K). ... The attached document itself later says Contr requires Support Status and Resolution Status. That is actually evidence against identifying Contr with ordinary satisfiability.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects identifying Contr with ordinary model-theoretic satisfiability: Satisfiability != Contr, since satisfiability is relative to Semantics+Language+ModelClass; proposes Cons_S(K) iff exists M: M|=_S K as a candidate formal consistency property distinct from Contr(K)=not-Cons_S(K), citing the source document's own admission that Contr requires Support Status and Resolution Status as evidence against the satisfiability identification, and listing Contr's broader required distinctions (genuine contradiction, incompatible contexts, temporal divergence, supersession, insufficient evidence, theory incompleteness).

type_signature.domain: knowledge base K under reasoning system S

b_rows_sample.anchor: soundness and completeness are properties of a reasoning system: Sound(S), Complete(S,Q). They are not properties of Knowledge itself. This should therefore be added under: Formal Representation and Reasoning rather than as a universal epistemic distinction. ... Decidability is a property of a problem/procedure/formal system ... Decidable(S,Q) ... Therefore: Decidability != EpistemicStatus. But it is extremely valuable as a reasoning-system capability/property. This fits our existing Complexity(S,Q) work.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reclassifies Soundness (Sound(S)), Completeness (Complete(S,Q)), and Decidability (Decidable(S,Q)) as properties of the reasoning system S (a problem/procedure/formal-system property), not properties of Knowledge itself and not epistemic distinctions (Decidability != EpistemicStatus, distinct from Known(p) and Determined(p)); recommends filing them under 'Formal Representation and Reasoning' alongside an existing Complexity(S,Q) line of work rather than as universal epistemic distinctions in R_req.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The document identifies a weakness in its own preservation criterion: it does not account for context-sensitivity. This is correct. I would make the correction stronger. Instead of D_Q we should eventually have D_Q(Gamma) ... R_req may be a global baseline, while the actual required distinction set is: R_req(Q,Gamma). This is a major improvement.
b_rows_sample.statement: Strengthens the source document's own context-sensitivity self-correction: replaces D_Q with D_Q(Gamma) where Gamma bundles context, scope, time, authority, task, and representation regime; correspondingly R_req becomes a global baseline while the actually-applicable set is R_req(Q,Gamma) -- described as a major theoretical improvement over a fixed universal set.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I disagree with 'Tier 1 must always be preserved' ... A Tier-1 distinction d3 could be irrelevant to that question. Then R_1 may legitimately discard d3. So Tier(d) should influence governance priority, but should not automatically determine semantic preservation. The better rule is: Requiredness(Q,Gamma) > Tier.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the rule 'Tier 1 must always be preserved' as too rigid: even a Tier-1 distinction may be legitimately discarded by a representation used only for a task whose D_Q does not require it. Proposes Tier should govern governance priority, not automatically determine semantic preservation, i.e. Requiredness(Q,Gamma) takes precedence over Tier.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The document says transformation invariance should preserve distinctions, but then recognizes that transformations may intentionally modify distinctions ... define a transformation's declared change set: Chg(T) subseteq R. Then: d not-in Chg(T) implies T must preserve d. This is much better for KnowledgeOS because some operations are supposed to change state. Otherwise the preservation requirement makes state transition impossible.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the transformation-invariance rule: instead of requiring T to preserve all of R_req, defines a declared change set Chg(T) subseteq R such that d not-in Chg(T) implies T must preserve d; explicitly noting that an unconditional preservation requirement would make state transition impossible, since some operations are supposed to change state.

type_signature.domain: transformation T and distinction set R
type_signature.codomain: Chg(T) subseteq R, plus a preservation obligation on R minus Chg(T)

b_rows_sample.anchor: The document says: delta must preserve all R_req distinctions. I would explicitly reject this formulation ... What must be preserved are the invariants declared applicable to that transition. So: InvariantCustody(delta) is preferable to: PreserveAll(delta, R_req). This aligns directly with our existing invariant-custody research.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly rejects the claim 'delta must preserve all R_req distinctions': a transition delta(K_t,a)->K_{t+1} may intentionally change status, support, currency, resolution, scope, even representation; proposes InvariantCustody(delta) -- preserving only the invariants declared applicable to that specific transition -- as preferable to PreserveAll(delta,R_req), aligned with existing invariant-custody research.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 'Zero requires all Tier 1 distinctions' should NOT be adopted ... Zero does not necessarily need every distinction in R_req. Instead: Zero(K,I,Gamma,L) asks what is not justified by the available representation within the declared inquiry boundary. Therefore Zero's required distinctions are: R_Zero(I,Gamma,L) not automatically all Tier-1 distinctions. This is a major correction.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the claim 'Zero requires all Tier 1 distinctions': Zero(K,I,Gamma,L) does not need every R_req distinction, only R_Zero(I,Gamma,L), a distinct inquiry-relative subset; supports this by restating Zero's own existing epistemic-boundary vocabulary (Unknown!=Absent, NoEvidence!=EvidenceOfAbsence, Unresolved!=False, Representation!=Reality) as the actual grounding, rather than an automatic Tier-1 requirement.

type_signature.domain: inquiry I, context Gamma, lens L

b_rows_sample.anchor: The 'minimality' definition is not yet mathematically sufficient ... minimal relative to what? ... the empty set R=empty could trivially satisfy many formal preservation conditions. The correct direction is something like: R_req(Q,Gamma) = minimal distinctions sufficient for all required questions Q, subject to declared adequacy criteria. This makes R_req task-grounded rather than literature-grounded.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a mathematical gap in the source document's minimality claim (a set claimed minimal 'relative to what?' -- as stated, an empty distinction set could trivially satisfy preservation/non-collapse/compositionality conditions); corrects the definition to R_req(Q,Gamma) = the minimal distinction set sufficient for all required questions Q, subject to declared adequacy criteria, making R_req task-grounded rather than literature-grounded.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 'Completeness of R_req' is itself a dangerous concept ... There may be no useful universal set D_all. There can always be another task requiring another distinction. So instead of asking 'Is R_req complete?' we should ask: Complete relative to which task/question/domain? ... Complete(R_req,Q,Gamma) could mean: no currently declared required question in Q requires a distinction absent from R_req. That is a tractable governance question. 'Complete for all possible knowledge representation' is not.
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns that asking whether R_req is 'complete' in an absolute sense is a dangerous, likely-unanswerable question (no useful universal distinction set D_all can be assumed to exist, since any new task can require a new distinction); replaces it with a tractable relativized governance question Complete(R_req,Q,Gamma): no currently declared required question in Q requires a distinction absent from R_req.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The 47 distinctions should therefore NOT be frozen as universal ... Better: 47 currently identified candidate distinctions within the present KnowledgeOS research scope. ... We should preserve KnownSet(R) without claiming R=D.
b_rows_sample.statement: Downgrades the source document's claim that its 47 distinctions form a comprehensive foundation, to '47 currently identified candidate distinctions within the present KnowledgeOS research scope', distinguishing the known distinction set KnownSet(R) from a claim that R equals the (unknowable) universal distinction set D.

b_rows_sample.anchor: After filtering the document, I would extract seven concrete contributions. RQ-1 Required Distinction Set R_req(Q,Gamma) PROMOTE TO THEORY CANDIDATE ... RQ-2 Representation Preservation Preserve(R,d) PROMOTE ... RQ-3 Representation Collapse Collapse(R,d) PROMOTE ... RQ-4 Representation Adequacy Adequacy(R,Q,Gamma) PROMOTE ... RQ-5 Contextual Requiredness R_req = f(Q,Gamma) PROMOTE ... RQ-6 Transformation Change Set Chg(T) subseteq R STRONG CANDIDATE ... RQ-7 Formal Reasoning Properties Sound(S), Complete(S,Q), Decidable(S,Q), Complexity(S,Q) PROMOTE AS REASONING-SYSTEM PROPERTIES
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists seven concrete contributions extracted from the filtered document, each with a promotion status: RQ-1 Required Distinction Set R_req(Q,Gamma) (PROMOTE TO THEORY CANDIDATE); RQ-2 Preserve(R,d) (PROMOTE); RQ-3 Collapse(R,d) (PROMOTE); RQ-4 Adequacy(R,Q,Gamma) (PROMOTE); RQ-5 Contextual Requiredness R_req=f(Q,Gamma) (PROMOTE); RQ-6 Transformation Change Set Chg(T) subseteq R (STRONG CANDIDATE); RQ-7 Formal Reasoning Properties Sound(S)/Complete(S,Q)/Decidable(S,Q)/Complexity(S,Q) (PROMOTE AS REASONING-SYSTEM PROPERTIES).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Loss_req(pi,Q,Gamma) = R_req(Q,Gamma) intersect Collapsed(pi). Then: Loss_req = empty is a very strong adequacy condition. This is far more useful than a generic 'information loss' metric. ... FDE preserves some distinctions but collapses others. The relevant question is not 'Does FDE have four values?' It is: Does FDE preserve every distinction in R_req(Q,Gamma)? Our previous experiments already showed that it does not.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Loss_req(pi,Q,Gamma) = R_req(Q,Gamma) intersect Collapsed(pi) as a required-information-loss metric, with Loss_req=empty as a strong adequacy condition, judged more useful than a generic information-loss measure; reframes the earlier FDE-insufficiency finding not as 'does FDE have four values' but as 'does FDE preserve every distinction in R_req(Q,Gamma)', concluding it does not (per prior experiments) -- positioning R_req as the formal language for STATING why a representation is inadequate rather than a prescription of which representation must be used.

type_signature.domain: projection pi, question Q, context Gamma
type_signature.codomain: a subset of R_req(Q,Gamma) that pi collapses

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero -> Boundary analysis -> Required distinctions rather than: Zero = absence of Tier-1 distinctions. This is a substantial theoretical improvement. ... each operation should have: Pre(delta), Post(delta), Inv(delta), Chg(delta). Then: d in Inv(delta) means the distinction must survive the transition. Whereas: d in Chg(delta) means the transition is explicitly permitted/required to change it. This is much more compatible with DDD and formal transition semantics.
b_rows_sample.statement: Clarifies the role of Zero as Zero->Boundary-analysis->Required-distinctions (not Zero=absence-of-Tier-1-distinctions), and clarifies delta's structure as needing four named components -- Pre(delta), Post(delta), Inv(delta) (distinctions that must survive the transition), and Chg(delta) (distinctions the transition is permitted/required to change) -- judged more compatible with DDD and formal transition semantics than a single undifferentiated preserve-everything rule.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The attached document recommends: HPA review -> feedback -> ratification -> kernel selection. I would change the last step. Do not: R_req -> KernelSelection directly. Instead: R_req -> AdequacyConstraints -> CandidateRepresentations -> CandidateOperations -> Verification -> KernelSelection. This is crucial. R_req tells us what must not be lost. It does not tell us which implementation/formalism is the kernel.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the source document's governance chain (HPA review -> feedback -> ratification -> kernel selection, with R_req feeding kernel selection directly), replacing the last step with a longer chain: R_req -> AdequacyConstraints -> CandidateRepresentations -> CandidateOperations -> Verification -> KernelSelection; states R_req tells us what must not be lost, not which implementation/formalism is the kernel.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Final classification of the attached document [table]: R_req concept Strong; Zero = all Tier 1 Reject; Contr = satisfiability failure Reject; delta preserves all R_req Reject; 47 distinctions = complete Reject; Immediate ratification Premature; Direct kernel selection Reject.
b_rows_sample.statement: Consolidated final classification table judging each part of the reviewed document: most core concepts (R_req, Preservation, Collapse, Adequacy, Projection analysis) rated Strong (some with corrections); Composition preservation rated too strong as written; Tier system rated a useful governance device but not semantic law; several proposed distinctions (analytic/synthetic, a priori/a posteriori, necessary/contingent) rated Not currently required; and five specific claims explicitly Rejected -- Zero=all-Tier-1, Contr=satisfiability-failure, delta-preserves-all-R_req, 47-distinctions=complete, and direct kernel selection -- with immediate ratification rated Premature.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'r-req-question-relative-correction-package' POSSIBLY relates to 'r-req-formal-specification' (batch B0062). Note: A corrective reformulation of R_req making it context/question-relative rather than a fixed universal set: R_req(Q,Gamma) subseteq D (the distinctions required to answer question Q under context Gamma), Adequacy(R,Q,Gamma) iff R_req(Q,Gamma) subseteq Preserved(R,Gamma), and Loss_req(pi,Q,Gamma) = R_req(Q,Gamma) intersect Collapsed(pi) as a required-information-loss metric (Loss_req=empty as the strong adequacy condition). Distilled into eight core propositions RREQ-1..RREQ-8 (Requiredness, Preservation, Collapse, Adequacy, Projection, Required Information Loss, Transformation Change, Reasoning-System Properties) proposed as the artifact KR-RREQ-2026-09, superseding a prior document's universal/literature-grounded R_req and its direct R_req->KernelSelection governance chain.

a_rows_sample.anchor: RAG should not become the KnowledgeOS knowledge model. RAG should become a controlled knowledge-access and projection layer over the KnowledgeOS epistemic core.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extraction from a RAG-with-Python book, applying the established Zero/DDD/Nyaya/Chinese/Adversarial/Agent lenses; central finding: 'RAG should not become the KnowledgeOS knowledge model. RAG should become a controlled knowledge-access and projection layer over the KnowledgeOS epistemic core' -- the book's own progression (Data->Preparation->Chunking->Embedding->Vector/Graph Storage->Retrieval->Reranking->Context Assembly->Generation->Evaluation->Agentic action) is read as a knowledge-acquisition/representation/retrieval/reasoning/evaluation/action pipeline, complementary to the architecture-patterns-python-technical-pattern-lens's (S0440) domain-mutation pipeline.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A single vector retriever is not a KnowledgeOS retrieval architecture. ... retrieval ≠ one operation
a_rows_sample.statement: Lens 0 (Zero): simple vector retrieval breaks on multistep or multi-data-type questions, requiring orchestration beyond similarity search -- 'a single vector retriever is not a KnowledgeOS retrieval architecture'; retrieval is a pipeline, not one operation (query->candidate generation->filtering->ranking->context expansion->context assembly), giving Pattern 1 Multi-Stage Retrieval (Candidate Retrieval->Filtering->Fusion->Reranking->Context Selection), with reranking described in the source as an explicit second-stage operation over initially-retrieved candidates.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Retrieved ≠ Relevant ≠ Supported ≠ True ≠ Authoritative ... Retrieval Evidence Boundary
a_rows_sample.statement: Zero-lens inference (proposed as a candidate constitutional principle): Retrieved != Relevant != Supported != True != Authoritative, since the source treats evaluation as separate from retrieval and generation and vector similarity finds only semantic similarity, not truth. Proposes a Retrieval Evidence Boundary pattern: KnowledgeOS{Authoritative Knowledge Core, Retrieval Projections{Vector index, Keyword index, Graph projection, Metadata index, Search cache}} where indexes are derived projections, not canonical sources -- exactly analogous to CQRS (canonical domain state->events->retrieval projections), explicitly strengthening the architecture extracted from architecture-patterns-python-technical-pattern-lens (S0440).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Retrieval Policy ... very compatible with the earlier Chinese Context Envelope idea
a_rows_sample.statement: Pattern 2 (Constraint-Aware Retrieval): context/metadata constraints can precede or follow candidate generation depending on domain (Graph RAG example: semantic search combined with graph filters narrowing candidates before ranking); generalized into a RetrievalPolicy{query_strategy, allowed_sources, context_constraints, authority_constraints, temporal_constraints, ranking_strategy, max_candidates, evidence_requirements} object, explicitly compatible with the Chinese-lens Context Envelope idea from S0440's second pass.

a_rows_sample.anchor: These should not all become entities inside the Knowledge domain. ... Its responsibility is: Find potentially useful knowledge. Not: Decide what knowledge is valid.
a_rows_sample.statement: Lens 1 (DDD): the book's implicit domain boundaries (Document/DocumentChunk/Embedding/RetrievalQuery/RetrievalResult/Evidence/Context/Tool/Agent/Workflow/Evaluation) should not all become entities inside the Knowledge domain; instead a separate Retrieval Context bounded context is proposed with the explicit responsibility 'find potentially useful knowledge', not 'decide what knowledge is valid' -- proposing a RetrievalRequest aggregate (query, context, constraints, retrieval_policy) producing a RetrievalResult (candidate, score, source, position, retrieval_method, provenance) where retrieved chunks are observations/results, never authoritative entities.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Similarity Is Not Pramana ... Embedding similarity should never be interpreted as Epistemic confidence.
a_rows_sample.statement: Lens 2 (Nyaya/Epistemic), rated perhaps the most important epistemic safeguard for an AI KnowledgeOS: 'similarity is not pramana' -- an embedding score establishing semantic similarity does not establish that a proposition is justified, so embedding similarity must never be interpreted as epistemic confidence; proposes an Evidence Qualification Pipeline (Retrieved Candidate->Relevance->Source Provenance->Authority->Context Match->Evidence Sufficiency->Epistemic Assessment), distinguishing 'here are things that might help' (retriever) from 'here is what we can actually justify' (KnowledgeOS).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Retrieval correctness ≠ Generation faithfulness ≠ Answer usefulness ... Three-Layer AI Assurance
a_rows_sample.statement: The book's evaluation architecture separates Context precision ('did retrieval find useful information?'), Faithfulness ('does the answer stick to retrieved facts?'), and Response relevancy ('does the answer address the question?') as independently-moving metrics, giving Retrieval correctness != Generation faithfulness != Answer usefulness; proposed as a KOS/AI-Platform pattern 'Three-Layer AI Assurance' (L1 Retrieval Assurance, L2 Grounding Assurance, L3 Intent Assurance) mapping almost directly onto the book's three metrics.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Graph RAG is not merely an optimization of vector search. It is a representation of relational context. ... Names Are Not Enough
a_rows_sample.statement: Lens 3 (Chinese Philosophy) applied to RAG: Context Is Constitutive (query+role+situation+institution+time+purpose->meaningful retrieval, rather than bare query->similar chunks, giving Pattern Contextual Retrieval: Retrieve(query, context)); Relational Identity -- Graph RAG's example (a Clause anchored to ClauseType/Company/Address/SLA) is read as 'not merely an optimization of vector search, it is a representation of relational context', a direct technical realization of the relational-identity observation. Names Are Not Enough -- vector retrieval for an ambiguous term like 'Customer' across 500 documents cannot resolve which institution/jurisdiction/version/role/business-context is meant, so Name-Referent Separation (from S0440 Pass 2) should feed directly into retrieval: Query->Entity/concept resolution->Context resolution->Retrieval, not Query->Embedding.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Perspective-Aware Retrieval ... Best according to whom?
a_rows_sample.statement: Chinese Lens D (Perspective) applied to retrieval: basic RAG tends toward a single 'best documents' set; the perspective lens asks 'best according to whom?', proposing Perspective-Aware Retrieval (RetrievalRequest{proposition, perspective, role, context, jurisdiction, temporal_scope}) that can return multiple perspective-grouped evidence sets rather than collapsing everything into top_k=5.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Conflict-Aware Retrieval ... Are they contradictory? Or: different jurisdictions? different dates?
a_rows_sample.statement: Chinese Lens E (Contradiction) applied to retrieval: a vector retriever returning apparently conflicting documents ('X is recommended' vs 'X is prohibited') should not be synthesized by a naive LLM as 'X has different recommendations' without checking whether they differ by jurisdiction/date/product/role/authority/meaning; proposes Pattern Conflict-Aware Retrieval (Candidate Set->Conflict Detection->Context Comparison->Conflict Classification->Contextual Synthesis), connecting directly to the Contradiction Taxonomy from S0440.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What semantic information was lost or altered at each transformation? ... Transformation Provenance ... Evidence Transformation Chain
a_rows_sample.statement: Chinese Lens F (Transformation): the ingestion pipeline (Document->Chunks->Embeddings->Index, or PDF->OCR->text->chunk->summary->embedding) is not mere copying -- every transformation potentially loses or alters information, so 'what semantic information was lost or altered at each transformation?' motivates a Transformation Provenance / Evidence Transformation Chain pattern (SourceArtifact-extracted-from->ExtractedContent-normalized-to->KnowledgeFragment-embedded-as->RetrievalRepresentation), with every edge traceable; supported by the source's own multimodal-PDF recommendation to partition text/images/tables separately while preserving metadata (original filepath, page numbers) -- 'provenance-preserving knowledge transformation.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Independent Stage Verification ... fixing retrieval before debugging generation
a_rows_sample.statement: Lens 4 (Adversarial/Falsification): the source recommends evaluating the retriever independently and fixing retrieval before debugging generation when retrieval returns irrelevant chunks, separating human evaluation/synthetic evaluation/context-precision/faithfulness/response-relevancy; proposes Pattern Independent Stage Verification (verify after Ingestion, Chunking, Embedding, Retrieval, Reranking, Context assembly, Generation individually), called extremely compatible with the existing deterministic-assurance/verification-gate architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Retrieval Falsification ... what evidence should have been found but wasn't? ... Faithfulness Verification ... Claim-Level Grounding
a_rows_sample.statement: Two adversarial algorithms: Retrieval Falsification (compare retrieved set R against expected evidence E for precision/recall/coverage/ordering, then explicitly ask 'what evidence should have been found but wasn't?', judged more important than just asking whether the LLM's answer was good); Faithfulness Verification (extract atomic claims from an answer, locate supporting evidence for each, check entailment/support, record supported/unsupported/contradicted/ambiguous), proposing a Claim-Level Grounding pattern (Answer{Claim A->Evidence E1->supported, Claim B->Evidence E3->supported, Claim C->no evidence->unsupported, Claim D->Evidence E7->contradicted}) replacing a single answer.grounded=true flag, called a potentially major KnowledgeOS pattern.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Should KnowledgeOS itself become an agent? My answer: No. ... Knowledge Tool Boundary
a_rows_sample.statement: Lens 5 (Agent): the book's agentic-RAG patterns (Prompt Chaining, Routing, Parallelization, Orchestrator-Workers, tool-based workflows) map onto the AI Engineering Platform, but Lens 0 asks 'should KnowledgeOS itself become an agent?' -- answered 'No': KnowledgeOS should expose Knowledge Query/Evidence/Context/Assessment/Actions to agents, which orchestrate, avoiding KnowledgeOS=Agent+RAG+VectorDB+Graph+LLM (which would collapse bounded contexts); proposes a Knowledge Tool Boundary pattern exposing focused single-responsibility tools (search_knowledge/retrieve_evidence/resolve_concept/compare_claims/get_authority/get_lineage/evaluate_claim/find_conflicts) rather than one giant ask_knowledgeos() tool.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sequential, Routing, Parallel, Orchestrator-workers, Iterative/agentic workflow classes ... should be workflow primitives, not necessarily KOS domain patterns
a_rows_sample.statement: Five agentic workflow pattern classes extracted (Sequential: extract->normalize->validate->store; Routing: query->router->{SQL,Vector,Graph,API}; Parallel: query fanned to Vector/Graph/SQL/Web; Orchestrator-workers: Orchestrator dispatching to specialized workers then a Synthesizer; Iterative/agentic: observe->reason->act->observe loop) explicitly classified as workflow primitives belonging to the AI Engineering Platform, not necessarily KOS domain patterns.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Retrieval algorithms extracted from the book ... A1..A27
a_rows_sample.statement: A four-category, 27-item retrieval algorithm catalogue: Candidate generation (A1-A5: vector similarity, keyword/BM25, metadata filtering, graph traversal, hybrid search -- the source demonstrates combining semantic similarity with graph filtering); Query transformation (A6-A10: query expansion, multiquery, HyDE, query decomposition, query routing -- multiquery generates similar variants while decomposition creates distinct subquestions, explicitly distinguished by the source); Context expansion (A11-A14: sentence-window, parent/child, auto-merging, graph expansion -- fixed positional expansion distinguished from relevance-based auto-merging); Ranking (A15-A19: similarity ranking, BM25 ranking, RRF/result fusion, cross-encoder reranking, LLM reranking -- reranking described as a second pass over merged candidates, not a replacement for initial retrieval).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance A20..A27 ... synthetic datasets ... synthetic tests do not adequately capture ambiguous real-world queries or human experience
a_rows_sample.statement: Assurance algorithm category (A20-A27: Recall@k, Precision@k, Context Precision, Faithfulness, Response Relevancy, Human Pairwise Evaluation, Synthetic Test Generation, Regression Evaluation); the source recommends synthetic datasets covering different document types, question complexities, multihop reasoning, and knowledge-boundary edge cases, while explicitly warning that synthetic tests do not adequately capture ambiguous real-world queries or human experience -- a self-limitation preserved in the extraction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS should have TWO fundamentally different pipelines ... Pipeline A — Knowledge Governance ... Pipeline B — Knowledge Access
a_rows_sample.statement: Central architectural synthesis: KnowledgeOS should have two fundamentally different pipelines -- Pipeline A Knowledge Governance (the canonical truth/authority pipeline: Knowledge Change->Command->Domain Validation->Aggregate->Evidence/Authority->Commit->Domain Event->Knowledge Lineage, from architecture-patterns-python-technical-pattern-lens/S0440) and Pipeline B Knowledge Access (the retrieval pipeline: User/Agent Query->Query Understanding->Context Resolution->Retrieval Policy->Candidate Generation->Hybrid Search->Graph Expansion->Reranking->Evidence Qualification->Context Assembly->LLM/Agent->Grounding Verification, from this book); these must not be confused, formalized into a four-layer KNOWLEDGEOS diagram (KNOWLEDGE CORE->domain events->KNOWLEDGE PROJECTIONS->RETRIEVAL ENGINE->AI ENGINEERING), argued to be substantially more convincing than 'KnowledgeOS needs RAG.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Contextual Retrieval Contract ... Retrieval Path Provenance ... RetrievalTrace
a_rows_sample.statement: Two new patterns combining the RAG book with the Chinese lens: Contextual Retrieval Contract -- RetrievalRequest{query, context, perspective, role, jurisdiction, temporal_scope, authority_scope, knowledge_scope, retrieval_policy} and RetrievalResult{evidence, relevance, provenance, semantic_context, structural_context, authority_context, retrieval_path}. Retrieval Path Provenance / RetrievalTrace{query, strategy, sources, candidates, filters, graph_paths, ranking, selected_evidence} -- a result is not merely 'Document X' but arrived via a traceable path (e.g. Query->semantic match->Clause->SLA->Company->Industry->filter->reranking, per the source's Graph RAG architecture of initial search/graph expansion/optional filtering-ranking/context assembly), extremely useful for deterministic audit.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AI output must be inspectable and replayable ... Execution{Query, KnowledgeSnapshot, RetrievalPolicy, RetrievalTrace, EvidenceSet, ContextAssembly, Model, Prompt, Output, GroundingAssessment, Decision}
a_rows_sample.statement: The existing principle 'AI output must be inspectable and replayable' is strengthened by RAG's retrieval-trace + prompt/context + model + generation + evaluation chain, proposing a full Execution{Query, KnowledgeSnapshot, RetrievalPolicy, RetrievalTrace, EvidenceSet, ContextAssembly, Model, Prompt, Output, GroundingAssessment, Decision} record -- called a very strong convergence between RAG architecture and the existing deterministic-assurance architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A. Model Knowledge | Training -> Parameters -> LLM Response | Implicit, non-traceable, non-governed... B. External Retrieval... C. KnowledgeOS Knowledge... LLM Response != KnowledgeOS Knowledge / Retrieved Document != KnowledgeOS Knowledge / Training Data != KnowledgeOS Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three information pathways that must not be conflated: (A) Model Knowledge -- implicit, non-traceable, non-governed LLM parametric output, to be interpreted but never treated as authoritative; (B) External Retrieval -- explicit, traceable, but ungoverned source material, a candidate-evidence source only; (C) KnowledgeOS Knowledge -- explicit, traceable, governed, versioned Epistemic State, the sole authoritative representation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SOURCE PLANE ... KNOWLEDGE PLANE ... EPISTEMIC ENGINE ... The Source Plane answers: "Where did this information come from?" The Knowledge Plane answers: "What do we currently represent as knowledge?" The Epistemic Engine answers: "How justified, complete, current, and coherent is that knowledge?"
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a Source Plane (Documents/APIs/Git and their Entities/Assertions/Dimensions/Relations) architecturally separated from a Knowledge Plane, with an Epistemic Engine (Zero/Lord feeding Sarathi) mediating between the two; the three planes answer three distinct questions (provenance, current representation, justification/completeness/coherence).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Invariant 1: Source != Knowledge ... Invariant 2: LLM Output != Knowledge ... Invariant 3: Retrieval != Knowledge Creation ... Sources provide information; KnowledgeOS constructs governed knowledge from it. LLMs interpret; KnowledgeOS evaluates and governs. Retrieval supplies evidence candidates; it does not automatically create knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes three constitutional invariants for source governance: Source != Knowledge (documents/API responses/git repos are not knowledge), LLM Output != Knowledge (LLM output must pass through Candidate Interpretation and Epistemic Processing before becoming knowledge), and Retrieval != Knowledge Creation (retrieval produces evidence candidates that must be evaluated, not automatic knowledge); Source Connectors, Semantic Reconstruction, Candidate Assertions (held pending until evaluated), and Evidence Objects (with full provenance) are named as the required first-class implementation components.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Book's assumption: The model learns to predict the "correct" next token. There is an objective truth in the training data. KnowledgeOS's principle: There is no objective truth. Knowledge is always provisional, epistemic, and context-dependent. What to avoid: Don't assume the LLM's output is "true." Always treat it as a candidate interpretation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns explicitly against importing the source book's implicit "objective truth in training data" assumption into KnowledgeOS: KnowledgeOS's principle is that there is no objective truth and knowledge is always provisional/epistemic/context-dependent, so any LLM output must always be treated as a candidate interpretation, never as true.

a_aliases: RAG as controlled knowledge access layer, not knowledge model

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'source-knowledge-plane-three-pathways-separation' POSSIBLY relates to 'rag-knowledge-access-layer-lens' (batch B0031). Note: A DeepSeek external-research artifact (phase_measure_theory/external_research/) proposing three distinct information pathways (Model/LLM parametric knowledge, External Retrieval, KnowledgeOS governed Knowledge), a Source-Plane/Knowledge-Plane architectural split mediated by the Epistemic Engine (Zero/Lord/Sarathi), and three source-governance invariants (Source!=Knowledge, LLM-Output!=Knowledge, Retrieval!=Knowledge-Creation); extends the earlier RAG-as-access-layer position (rag-knowledge-access-layer-lens, B0011) but is not identical to it -- unvetted per the folder readme, no adjudication against the ratified invariant catalog performed here.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I asked the author to choose among five status vocabularies. That question was malformed, and the refusal was correct. The 'eleven competing vocabularies' were never competing. They are FIVE DIFFERENT KINDS OF THING crammed into one field. Once separated, the epistemic core is uniquely determined at
a_rows_sample.statement: Retracts the verifier's own prior escalation of the status-vocabulary question to the author (B1 in S1605): the framing of 'competing vocabularies' was itself malformed, since the 11+ terms are not alternatives for one dimension but instances of 5 different kinds of thing conflated into a single field; once separated, the true epistemic core is uniquely determined at 3 states.

a_rows_sample.anchor: All discovered vocabularies (executed enumeration, 24 terms) [table with file counts and numbered-step spans, e.g. Unknown 45 files/steps 12..242, Supported 24/8..245, ...]
a_rows_sample.statement: Executes a corpus-wide enumeration finding 24 distinct status-like terms in use (Unknown, Supported, Rejected, Inferred, Candidate, Observed, Accepted, Confirmed, Superseded, Conflicted, Approved, Validated, Refuted, Proposed, Contested, Established, Corroborated, Verified, Disputed, Determined, Authoritative, Deprecated, Retired, and their file/step-span counts) -- the empirical basis for the subsequent semantic classification.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Test applied to every term: is it a property of ONE assertion, a relation between TWO, a lifecycle marker, a governance act, or derivable from the others? [5 categories: STATE n=3 Unknown/Supported/Refuted; DERIVED n=5; RELATION(binary) n=4; LIFECYCLE n=4; GOVERNANCE n=7; COLLISION n=1 Determined]
a_rows_sample.statement: Classifies all 24 discovered terms via a 5-way decisive test (unary epistemic property vs binary relation vs lifecycle marker vs governance act vs derivable-from-others) into: 3 irreducible unary epistemic states (Unknown, Supported, Refuted), 5 derived values (Conflicted, Observed, Established, Inferred, Confirmed), 4 binary relations (Superseded, Contested, Corroborated, Disputed), 4 lifecycle markers (Proposed, Candidate, Deprecated, Retired), 7 governance acts (Approved, Rejected, Accepted, Validated, Verified, Authoritative, Invalidated), and 1 genuine terminological collision (Determined).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Superseded is a RELATION, not a state. It requires two assertions. Step 218.21 states this itself: C1 --superseded--> C2, not delete(C1). ... Deprecated is explicitly NOT epistemic -- step-218.22 boxes Deprecated != Falsified. ... Observed and Inferred differ by EVIDENCE TYPE, not epistemic state. .
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives the decisive individual justifications behind the classification, each grounded in corpus citation: Superseded requires two assertions (step-218.21's C1-->superseded-->C2, never a delete); Deprecated is explicitly non-epistemic per step-218.22 (Deprecated != Falsified); Observed and Inferred both mean Supported but differ only in evidence type (belongs in E, not Sigma); Established reduces to Supported plus an uncodified corroboration threshold with no distinguishing operation; Determined is a genuine terminological collision (a status at steps 186-189, an aggregate at step 196.26).

a_rows_sample.anchor: I proposed a four-state set (Unknown/Supported/Refuted/Conflicted). That is one too many. Conflicted(A,K) := exists A' in K: same (subject,predicate), different object, overlapping validity, same context, neither Refuted. Conflicted is computable from the state. No operation requires it as a stored
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a previously proposed 4-state Sigma set (adding Conflicted) down to a minimal 3-state Sigma={Unknown, Supported, Refuted}, by giving an explicit computable definition of Conflicted(A,K) as a derived predicate over the state (same subject/predicate, differing object, overlapping validity, same context, neither Refuted) that no operation requires as a stored primitive, and warning that storing it duplicates derivable information and risks an update anomaly (stored flag disagreeing with computed value).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 4-state (adds Conflicted): REFUTED as minimal. 6-state historical (Proposed/Supported/Established/Superseded/Contested/Invalidated): REFUTED -- mixes four categories ... Only Supported is an epistemic state, and Contested is a relation. Two orthogonal dimensions: CONFIRMED. 3-state core + separate d
a_rows_sample.statement: Tests and refutes two larger candidate status sets: a 4-state candidate (Conflicted refuted as derived, per the prior finding) and a 6-state 'historical' candidate (Proposed/Supported/Established/Superseded/Contested/Invalidated) which is shown to mix all 5 category types at once (lifecycle, epistemic, derived, relation, governance) with only Supported actually being an epistemic state; the surviving candidate is a 3-state epistemic core plus separate orthogonal dimensions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sigma perp Gamma -- orthogonality CONFIRMED by construction. All four quadrants are meaningful and occur in the domain: [Supported/not-approved; Unknown/permitted; Refuted/still-authoritative; Supported/rejected]. Corpus support: step-194.19 boxes EpistemicStrength != GovernanceStatus; step-008 sepa
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms by explicit 2x2 construction that epistemic status (Sigma) and governance status (Gamma) are orthogonal dimensions: all four quadrant combinations (Supported+not-approved; Unknown+permitted; Refuted+still-authoritative; Supported+rejected) correspond to meaningful, realistic domain cases, and the corpus itself states the separation (step-194.19: EpistemicStrength != GovernanceStatus; step-008: acceptance vs commitment; step-232.4: Validation->Assessment) even though it then violates it by storing governance terms inside Sigma.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assertion A=(id,P,Sigma,E,tau,Pi) with Sigma in {Unknown,Supported,Refuted}. Gamma governance: separate, attached to the governance context -- not to A. Superseded: a relation in R or in History -- not a value of Sigma. Valid(K): the blocking sub-predicate was state consistency, which needed a vocab
a_rows_sample.statement: Derives the operational consequences of the 3-state Sigma resolution: the Assertion tuple becomes A=(id,P,Sigma,E,tau,Pi) with Sigma restricted to {Unknown,Supported,Refuted}; Gamma (governance) attaches separately to a governance context, not to A; Superseded becomes a relation in R or History rather than a Sigma value; the previously blocked state-consistency sub-predicate of Valid(K) (from S1603/S1605) becomes computable now that Sigma is fixed; Merge/Supersede become well-typed since supersession operates on the relation rather than mutating a status field.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t shape: relations must live somewhere -- this constrains the container. UL: 24 terms reduce to 3 states + 4 relations + 7 governance + 4 lifecycle. The 'eleven vocabularies' dissolve.
a_rows_sample.statement: Notes a downstream constraint on the still-open K_t shape blocker (B2): since relations (Superseded, Contested, Corroborated, Disputed) now need an explicit home in the container, this constrains what K_t's tuple/shape can be; and restates the overall UL resolution -- the notorious 'eleven competing vocabularies' dissolve into a clean 3+4+7+4 partition (states + relations + governance + lifecycle).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Recommended canonical model: Sigma: Assertion -> {Unknown,Supported,Refuted} epistemic, minimal, DERIVED from Assessment. Gamma: Assertion x GovernanceContext -> GovernanceStatus, governance, separate dimension. R subseteq AxA: supersedes, contests, corroborates, disputes. Lifecycle: metadata, not e
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes the final canonical model for the epistemic/governance/relation/lifecycle split: Sigma:Assertion->{Unknown,Supported,Refuted} (derived from Assessment); Gamma:Assertion x GovernanceContext -> GovernanceStatus (a separate dimension); R subseteq AxA carrying supersedes/contests/corroborates/disputes; Lifecycle as non-epistemic metadata -- classified overall as DERIVED (from corpus evidence plus executed classification and minimality tests), not a normative proposal.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Not Sigma. Sigma is determined at three states by the mathematics and the corpus. The one residue: Gamma's value set ... That is a governance-process question, not a mathematical one, and it does not block the formal theory ... Therefore I am NOT asking the author to decide anything yet.
a_rows_sample.statement: Closes the B1 blocker without escalating to the human author: Sigma itself is now fully derived (not normative), and the only residual open item -- Gamma's own value vocabulary (which governance statuses the domain recognizes) -- is explicitly deferred as a later, non-blocking governance-process question rather than treated as an immediate normative decision, correcting the S1605 escalation of B1 to AUTHOR INPUT REQUIRED.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Downstream effect: B1 is resolved. The next load-bearing gap moves to K_t's shape -- and Section 9 has just constrained it, because relations (R) now provably need a home.
a_rows_sample.statement: Records the downstream effect of closing B1: the single remaining load-bearing (normative) blocker from S1605's matrix becomes B2, K_t's tuple shape -- now further constrained by the requirement that relations R have an explicit home in the container.

a_rows_sample.anchor: TIER 1 -- DELIVERED UNDER A DIFFERENT NAME (substance exists) -- 24 [examples: MATHEMATICAL-KERNEL-REVERIFICATION -> KERNEL-AUDIT-230-232 + KERNEL-RECONCILIATION-230-236; K-EQUALITY-AND-IDENTITY-AUDIT -> IDENTITY-ROUNDTRIP-AUDIT; EPISTEMIC-STATUS-RECONCILIATION -> DECISION-SIGMA-EPISTEMIC-STATUS]
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies 24 of the 93 nominally missing artifacts as actually delivered under different filenames (e.g. the demanded EPISTEMIC-STATUS-RECONCILIATION.md was in fact delivered as DECISION-SIGMA-EPISTEMIC-STATUS.md, i.e. S1606; K-EQUALITY-AND-IDENTITY-AUDIT.md as IDENTITY-ROUNDTRIP-AUDIT.md, i.e. S1600), and notes one demanded artifact class (216-STEP-* files) is now superseded outright since the corpus has grown to 246 steps.

Determine whether the historical '11 competing vocabularies' are actually different dimensions that were incorrectly collapsed in
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses 4 explicit, mutually-non-exclusive hypotheses to test regarding epistemic status (H1: one canonical finite set is mathematically required; H2: status is genuinely multidimensional, with the '11 competing vocabularies' possibly being distinct dimensions incorrectly collapsed into one field; H3: status is context-dependent, requiring a parameterized algebra; H4: status is partly derived rather than stored) -- H2 and H4 are exactly what S1606's subsequent analysis independently confirms.

a_rows_sample.statement: Scores the S1611-mandated 4 status hypotheses against S1606's findings: H1 (one canonical set) REFUTED; H2 (multidimensional) CONFIRMED (Sigma-perp-Gamma); H3 (context-dependent algebra) NOT REQUIRED (context lives in the assertion); H4 (partly derived) CONFIRMED (Sigma derives from Assessment, Conflicted derives from state) -- explicitly closing the hypothesis-testing loop the mandate opened.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Transition relation Sigma x Event -> Sigma: total and deterministic over three states; Unknown -> Supported on supporting evidence, -> Refuted on contradicting, and back to Unknown on retraction. No artificial exceptions are needed. The six-state historical vocabulary cannot achieve this: Superseded
a_rows_sample.statement: Executes the S1611-mandated status-transition-algebra test: the 3-state Sigma admits a total, deterministic transition relation with no artificial exceptions, while the rejected 6-state historical vocabulary structurally cannot (Superseded and Invalidated have no valid Sigma-transitions since they are a relation and a governance act respectively) -- providing the mathematical (not preference-based) criterion the mandate demanded for choosing between vocabularies.

a_rows_sample.anchor: status transitions follow the covering relation and cannot skip levels. The current corpus says this invariant is witnessed, but also explicitly identifies a missing transition calculus: the ladder tells us which states exist, but not yet what operation moves an item between them. ... Epistemic stat
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a distinct gap in the epistemic-status ladder (invariant I-12, covering relation, no level-skipping): the corpus defines which epistemic states exist but not the operation that moves an item between them -- an epistemic transition function distinct from, and still missing alongside, the ordinary state transition delta/T.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A state transition may actually contain at least two different transitions: Knowledge-object lifecycle (K -> K') and Epistemic-status transition (e_i -> e_j). ... K_{t+1}=T(K_t) may be too coarse to explain Status_t -> Status_{t+1}.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues 'state transition' actually conflates two distinct transitions -- knowledge-object lifecycle (K->K') and epistemic-status transition (e_i->e_j, constrained by the covering relation) -- concluding the abstract K_{t+1}=T(K_t) formulation may be too coarse to explain status evolution on its own.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Unknown != False. This means Unknown should be modeled as an epistemic status, not as a Boolean negative. ... Identity != Representation and Identity != Dimension. ... Identity(K_t) = Identity(K_{t+1}) under revision? The corpus still records this as unresolved.
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms Unknown!=False (epistemic status, not Boolean negative) and Identity!=Representation / Identity!=Dimension as strong vocabulary anchors, while leaving genuinely open whether an object's identity is preserved across revision (Identity(K_t)=Identity(K_{t+1})?), recorded elsewhere in the corpus as unresolved.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ReplayAssertion -- identity is a content hash including time; policy captured externally as a hash; no status field; documented invariant 'once created is immutable... they do NOT mutate.' EvidenceSet -- 'References are opaque strings... this VO holds no transport' (ADR-T16). Evidence by reference,
a_rows_sample.statement: Finds 4 independent corroborations from unrelated production bounded contexts (convergent evolution, not KnowledgeOS-derived): ReplayAssertion uses a content hash (including time) as identity, captures policy externally, has no status field, and is documented immutable -- matching the S1595 identity-repair direction; EvidenceSet holds evidence strictly by reference, never by value (ADR-T16), exactly matching the corpus derivation's rejection of embedding evidence objects; EventProvenance uses (correlationId,causationId), explicitly scoped to Integration Events only; and authorities.yaml documents governance status as independent of lifecycle status, meaning Sigma-perp-Gamma orthogonality (S1606) is enforced in running production configuration by a linter, not merely a theoretical derivation.

b_rows_sample.statement: Records the human author's actual response to the two questions S1605 escalated as AUTHOR INPUT REQUIRED (status vocabulary, K_t shape): the author declines to choose, states they do not know which alternative is correct, and instructs the verifier to first determine how much more can still be derived from the corpus/mathematics/statistics/computability/DDD/practical requirements before asking again -- a governance-significant act distinct from the verifier's own self-generated mandates elsewhere in this chain.

[24 named capabilities] For every capability answer: [8 placement questions, including] Does putting it inside K create circularity? Does removing it from K lose information? Do not assume
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires a Knowledge-State Requirements Register testing 24 named capabilities (assertion representation, epistemic status, evidence association, provenance, context, temporal validity, uncertainty, contradiction, missingness, unknown, identity, equality, membership, state transition, supersession, merge, replay, validation, authority, governance, lineage, determinism, composability, computability) against an 8-question placement test (property of K vs relation vs transformation vs history vs external assessment vs governance metadata vs circularity risk vs information loss on removal), explicitly rejecting the assumption that every KnowledgeOS requirement must be a K-component.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not simply select one [kernel lineage]. Perform a semantic reconciliation. ... Determine whether apparently different primitives are: A. genuinely different concepts; B. aliases; C. different levels of abstraction; D. projections of one structure; E. historical alternatives; F. orthogonal dimensi
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires reconciling the corpus's two competing kernel lineages via a 7-category relationship classification (genuinely different concepts / aliases / abstraction levels / projections of one structure / historical alternatives / orthogonal dimensions / incorrectly conflated concepts) applied to 18 named primitives, with an explicit ban on reconciling by chronology or assuming later definitions supersede earlier ones -- generalizing the anti-recency bias already voiced in S1605.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Define K1 = K2 without accidentally making equality depend on: history; provenance; insertion order; event IDs; storage representation. Test whether the definition satisfies reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires defining Knowledge-State equality with an explicit checklist of accidental dependencies to guard against (history, provenance, insertion order, event IDs, storage representation) and requires verifying the standard equivalence-relation properties (reflexivity, symmetry, transitivity) rather than assuming them.

b_rows_sample.anchor: observation != evidence; evidence != determination; determination != decision; decision != authorization; authorization != execution; validation != transformation; knowledge state != transformation history; provenance != lineage. ... If the mathematics collapses two DDD concepts into one object, rec
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists 8 specific forbidden DDD conflations to test against the mathematics (observation!=evidence, evidence!=determination, determination!=decision, decision!=authorization, authorization!=execution, validation!=transformation, knowledge-state!=transformation-history, provenance!=lineage), requiring that any point where the formal model collapses two of these be recorded as a contradiction rather than silently accepted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Construct: Mathematical Object -> KnowledgeOS Concept -> Data Structure -> Operation -> Test. ... Do not invent implementation details merely to make the mapping work. If no implementation mapping exists, classify the concept as: THEORETICALLY DEFINED / IMPLEMENTATION MISSING.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires a 5-stage implementation-bridge chain (Mathematical Object -> KnowledgeOS Concept -> Data Structure -> Operation -> Test) for every proposed theory object, with an explicit fallback classification (THEORETICALLY DEFINED / IMPLEMENTATION MISSING) rather than inventing implementation details to force the mapping to close.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reject any numerical uncertainty claim that lacks a valid statistical basis. Distinguish: epistemic uncertainty; aleatory uncertainty; missingness; non-identifiability; contradiction; ignorance/unknown. Do not let a probability number become a substitute for these distinct concepts.
b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a statistical audit rejecting any numerical uncertainty claim lacking a valid statistical basis (random variable, sample space, estimand, observation model, probability space, conditioning information, estimator, calibration semantics, uncertainty interpretation all specified), and requires distinguishing 6 named concepts (epistemic uncertainty, aleatory uncertainty, missingness, non-identifiability, contradiction, ignorance/unknown) that a bare probability number must never be allowed to substitute for.

[pipeline: Historical Corpus -> Conceptual Theory -> Formal Theory -> Computable Theory -> KnowledgeOS Model -> Executable Implementation -> Empirical Validation] Each gap must have: GAP-ID, Question, Why it matters, Evidence, Current status, Blocking?, Can b
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires a Theory Completion Gap Register mapping gaps across a 7-stage pipeline (Historical Corpus -> Conceptual Theory -> Formal Theory -> Computable Theory -> KnowledgeOS Model -> Executable Implementation -> Empirical Validation), each gap carrying an 11-field record (GAP-ID through Resolution path) -- the most granular gap-tracking schema introduced in this batch's mandate chain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not attempt to 'complete the theory' by silently inserting engineering preferences. Explicitly divide results into: Mathematical necessities; Empirical facts; Historical facts; Architectural consequences; Design choices; User/business/governance decisions. This separation is mandatory.
b_rows_sample.statement: Mandates a strict 6-way mandatory division of every result (mathematical necessity, empirical fact, historical fact, architectural consequence, design choice, or user/business/governance decision), explicitly forbidding silently inserting engineering preferences as if they were mathematical necessities -- a finer-grained successor to the earlier A/B/C/D evidence-class scheme (S1596).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Only include decisions for which: the corpus does not determine the answer; mathematics does not determine the answer; DDD semantics does not determine the answer; implementation requirements do not determine the answer; empirical testing cannot determine the answer. ... b_rows_sample.statement: Sharpens the S1604 author-escalation protocol into a stricter 5-way exhaustion test (corpus, mathematics, DDD semantics, implementation requirements, and empirical testing must ALL fail to determine an answer) before a question may be classified as a genuinely irreducible user decision -- explicitly forbidding escalation merely because the corpus contains competing alternatives (exactly the mistake S1606 later shows the verifier made with the status vocabulary).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not use: 'verified'; 'complete'; 'canonical'; 'minimal'; 'correct'; 'production-ready' unless the corresponding proof/evidence exists. ... b_rows_sample.statement: Bans 6 specific completion-claiming words (verified, complete, canonical, minimal, correct, production-ready) unless matching proof/evidence exists, and defines the actual completion criterion as an independent-reconstruction test: a senior mathematician, statistician, DDD architect and software architect must each be able to reconstruct the theory from the final specification, compute every operation, identify every assumption, reproduce every result, and separate proven theory from design choice and hypothesis.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #1 — Knowledge as a generic object: forbidden in 208, used as an Owner in 210
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.28 boxes a prohibition: the Data->Information->Evidence->Assessment->KnowledgeClaim transformations of semantic status 'should not [be collapsed] into one generic object called Knowledge.' Step 210 Section 210.25's matrix row I11 nonetheless assigns Owner='Knowledge' (and row I3 compounds it with 'Knowledge infrastructure'), the exact generic object Step 208 boxed a prohibition against two files earlier in the same band. Severity HIGH; neither Step-206 bounded context, and neither file notices.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #2 — Provenance composition (208) excludes the authority Step 209 requires
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.25 asserts as an equality P(G)=P(A)∪P(E), boxed as 'provenance must be closed under semantic transformation.' Step 209 Section 209.4 requires Final(D)⇒DecisionBasis(D)∧Authority(D). Since Authority(D), the governance grant that made a decision final, is in neither P(A) nor P(E), a governed decision's provenance under Section 208.25 cannot contain its own authority, yet Step 209's own traceability requirement (Basis(D) including authority) demands that it does -- the two cannot both hold. Independently checked, the equality is additionally vacuous if closure holds (P(A)⊇P(E) implies the union is just P(A)) and self-refuting if it does not. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #3 — The evidence-strength scale is recalibrated between Step 210 and Step 212
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 Section 210.30 defines E_1=documentation, E_2=manual inspection, E_3=automated test, E_4=property-based test, E_5=formal verification. Step 212 Section 212.6 defines E_0=No evidence, E_1=Claim/documentation, E_2=Static implementation evidence, E_3=Executable test evidence, E_4=Runtime/production evidence, E_5=Formal verification. E_2, E_3 and E_4 disagree between the two files (only E_5 agrees), so a claim 'has E_4 evidence' means a property-based test under Step 210 and production observation under Step 212 -- entirely different assurance. Aggravating factor: Step 212's calibration silently matches the uncited Step 109's (E2=implementation, E4=runtime), so Step 212 restores an earlier convention without knowing it. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #4 — E_1 bound twice inside Step 210 itself
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 Section 210.20 writes E_1⇒P and E_2⇒¬P (evidence items entailing propositions); Step 210 Section 210.30, ten sections later, writes E_1=documentation (an ordinal assurance rung). Same symbol, same document, incompatible types, undisambiguated. Severity MEDIUM-HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #5 — Evidence/Test ordering reversed between Step 210's own boxed conclusion and Step 211's boxed conclusion
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 Section 210.40 boxes Invariant->Owner->Enforcement->Evidence->Test->Assurance; Step 211 Section 211.2 boxes I->Owner->Mechanism->Test->Evidence -- directly conflicting orderings, both boxed as conclusions in consecutive files. Step 210's own Section 210.1 tuple and Step 209's tail agenda both side with Step 211's ordering, so Step 210's boxed conclusion contradicts Step 210's own boxed tuple. Severity MEDIUM; the direction matters since Evidence->Test means evidence licenses the test while Test->Evidence means the test produces the evidence, which is what Steps 212-214 assume throughout.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #6 — min over assurance vs. the prohibition on scalarization, both boxed in Step 211
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 211 Section 211.6 states Assurance(I_global)<=min{Assurance(I_1),Assurance(I_2),...}; Step 211 Section 211.17 boxes 'Vector assurance is preferable to premature scalarization.' min over a set requires a total order on the codomain, but Section 211.9 makes assurance a 6-vector (only partially ordered), so evaluating min requires exactly the scalarization Section 211.17 forbids -- the two boxed positions of one file are mutually exclusive. Aggravated by Section 211.4's ordinal-only assurance-adjacent quantities and by Section 211.17's own use of cardinal values A_s=1, A_p=0, 0.83. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #7 — Step 212 builds ownership diagnostics and deletes the ownership data needed to run them
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 212 Section 212.15 boxes 'Ownerless Invariants' as a finding to explicitly search for (I exists but Owner(I)=empty set), yet Step 212 Section 212.4's register reprints all fifteen invariants with the Owner column removed (columns reduced to ID|Property|Target), and no search for ownerless invariants is performed anywhere in the file. Step 210's deleted Owner column contained exactly the data Sections 212.15/212.16 are designed to interrogate: 7 of 15 rows owned by a layer or pattern (effectively ownerless), 5 of 15 slash-shared. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #8 — F/D/P/U mandated in Step 213, applied zero times across Steps 213-215
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 213 Section 213.26 mandates that every important statement during reconstruction carry an [F]/[D]/[P]/[U] label ('our editorial control system'). A machine count of applied labels in Steps 213, 214, and 215 finds 4, 0, 0 respectively, and all four occurrences in 213 are the legend itself. Zero of the hundreds of statements in the three files that mandate the labels carry one, even though Section 213.26 explicitly scopes the requirement to these reconstruction documents themselves. Severity HIGH; this is a performative contradiction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #9 — Step 214's self-assessment table violates Step 214's own boxed evidentiary rule eight lines later
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 214 Section 214.32 boxes 'no architectural claim should be stronger than the evidence supporting it.' Step 214 Section 214.33's final row states 'Risk of overclaiming | Explicitly controlled' -- a claim about the corpus's own overclaiming risk with zero supporting evidence, in a table that also self-awards 'Very strong' on five dimensions in a file containing no evidence at all. Severity MEDIUM-HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #10 — Three incompatible ledger arities inside Step 214
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 214 Section 214.1 boxes a 10-tuple EL_i=(Step,Artifact,Observation,Fact,Derivation,Decision,Architecture,Invariant,Evidence,Status); Section 214.6 gives a 15-field schema table; the Section 214 tail (line 1095) gives an 8-column matrix header whose columns barely overlap the 10-tuple's. Three incompatible schemas for 'the Evidence Ledger' in one file, with no reconciliation and no statement of which is normative. Severity MEDIUM.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #11 — Step 215 prohibits new formulas and mints three (four) in the same file
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 215 Section 215.30 prohibits 'creat[ing] more theoretical formulas merely because we can,' yet the same file mints R(S_i)=(O_i,L_i,A_i,V_i,U_i) (215.1), Convergence(I)=NumberOfIndependentEvidencePaths(I) (215.7), the boxed SemanticIntegrity∝DistinctionPreservation (215.10), and the boxed B=Synthesize(Evidence,Experiments,Failures,Insights,Architecture,PhilosophicalReflection) (215.32) -- four new formal objects, none computed. Severity MEDIUM; aggravated because the proportionality is not merely new but ill-typed, and Synthesize is never specified.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #12 — Step 215 exempts itself and its seven predecessors from its own discipline
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 215 Section 215.31 (Phase 1) targets S_1...S_182 -> EvidenceLedger, goal 'understand what actually happened'; the same file's closing paragraph defers 'what we previously called Step 183 onward' to a later decision about renaming or absorption. Steps 183-215 include all eight in-scope files of this verification, so the reconstruction discipline is scoped to exclude the very documents that mandate it -- compounded by Contradiction #8 (zero labels applied). Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #13 — The scope of the derivation phase disagrees between Step 212 and Step 215
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 212 Section 212.5 states 'Steps 1-211 have largely been derivation'; Step 215 Section 215.31 and five other occurrences scope the reconstruction to S_1...S_182. The corpus states the derivation ran to 211 while scoping reconstruction to 182; the 29-step remainder is never reconciled, and 182 is never justified anywhere. Severity MEDIUM.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #14 — Subtraction on an undefined information measure, forbidden in Step 208 and performed anyway in Step 212
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.10 writes L(C)=I_required-I_preserved and immediately cautions 'we should not treat this as a literal numeric quantity until we define an information measure.' Step 212 Section 212.19 writes L(C)=InformationBefore(C)-InformationAfter(C) without that caveat and without citing 208.10 -- no information measure is defined anywhere in the intervening four files. This is the fourth occurrence of the pattern in the band (208.3's I(A)<I(E), 208.10, 212.19, and 214.7's SemanticLoss(A)>0). Severity MEDIUM-HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #15 — Total order on epistemic strength declined in Step 209 Section 209.21 and then used in 209.25 and 210.9
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 Section 209.21 states Unknown≺Hypothesized≺Supported and explicitly declines a universal total ordering ('the actual epistemic lattice must be derived from the domain'). Step 209 Section 209.25 (S(T(x))>S(x)) and Step 210 Section 210.9 (Strength(T(x))>Strength(x)) both then use strict > on the same kind of quantity, presupposing the order that was just declined four sections earlier and never derived. Severity MEDIUM.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #16 — Invariants modeled as a dependency graph and as a flat conjunction, consecutively, within Step 209
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 Section 209.31 states that some invariants depend on others (HistoricalTraceability depends on Identity+Versioning+Provenance), illustrated with a 24-line ASCII dependency graph. Step 209 Section 209.32 then composes all invariants as a flat, order-free conjunction I_global=AND_{i=1}^n I_i. A conjunction cannot express dependency; the two sections model the same invariant set with incompatible structures, consecutively. Severity MEDIUM.

a_rows_sample.statement: Summary tally of Part 6's contradiction catalogue across Steps 208-215: 16 contradictions total, of which six are internal to a single file (#4, #6, #9, #10, #11, #16) and ten are cross-file within the band (#1, #2, #3, #5, #7, #8, #12, #13, #14, #15).
